review2: oracle.summary: Lens "oracle". I ran 26 400 programs (20 400 generated by a typed random generator, 6 000 mutated from the interpreter and corpus programs and from accepted generated programs) through `weft check` at 328a39b. I ran the 8 521 accepted programs with the stock `weft run/test --unchecked` and with an instrumented interpreter, each on 6 seed and worker combinations (about 140 000 runs). The instrumented interpreter is a copy of the same commit with a patch in weft-interp only (SCRATCH/r2/oracle/interp_oracle.patch). It adds a fault on freed cells, a Vec that moves its buffer on push, pop and clear, a fault on references into dead locals, linear-leak checks, a vector-clock race detector, and a check that a stealable task holds no nonportable value. It makes no false alarm on the accepted interpreter and corpus programs. I found 8 blockers (OR1, OR2, OR3, OR5, OR6, OR7, OR8, OR9), 1 major false positive (OR4) and 2 minor items (OR10, OR11). 6 of the 8 blockers fault with the stock interpreter. OR7 and OR8 are data races, so only the race detector shows them. The round-1 fixes hold: each round-1 red-team probe that must fail gets an error. `weft agree` passes on 2 500 generated and mutated programs. Each finding has a minimal repro in SCRATCH/r2/oracle/repro/. The stock and instrumented result for each function is in verify_out.txt in the same oracle directory.

findings.title: A closure returned by a function does not point into its reference arguments
findings.description: `fn reader(v: &Vec<u64>) -> fn() { || print(v.len()) }`. The caller does `let f = reader(&v)`, then moves `v`, ends its scope or clears it, then calls `f()`. The checker accepts all three forms. Each one faults with the stock interpreter ("a value is used after it was moved" or "a place does not exist"). The same closure made in the body, or passed through `id(...)`, gets W0301. Cause: a call result of type fn() carries the `ret` part (its effects) but has no points_into for the places that the closure captured from the arguments. ADR 0003 says a call result points where the arguments can flow. This is not the ADR 0005 open item, which covers a closure inside a returned tuple or struct.
findings.repro: SCRATCH/r2/oracle/repro/OR1_returned_closure.wf (functions moved, scope_ended, cleared; also probes/a3_ret_closure_elem.wf and probes/a6_ret_closure_scope.wf)
findings.suggested_fix: Give a call result that can hold a function value the points_into places of its reference arguments (a wildcard place, as for a reference result with no stated place). A call of the result then uses those places, so W0301 and W0302 apply.

findings.title: The checker moves a captured value when the closure is made; the interpreter moves it when the closure runs
findings.description: `let f = || print(take(v)); v = Vec.new(); f(); print(v.len())` is accepted. At run time it faults with "a value is used after it was moved". The facts put moved_at(v) at the node that makes the closure. The interpreter takes the value from the cell when the closure runs, as ADR 0003 says. A new value given between the two points goes into the closure. The task form (`s.spawn(|| print(take(v)))`, then `v = Vec.new()`, then join) fails the same way on every seed. The same cause also gives a false positive: a closure that is made but never called still moves `v`, so a later `v.push(2)` gets W0302 (OR2b, and the reduced fp/W0302_p1066.wf and fp/W0502_p3681.wf).
findings.suggested_fix: Choose one move point. Either the interpreter moves the captured values at closure creation (this agrees with ADR 0006 for tasks), or the facts move them at each node where the closure runs and treat a new value of the variable while the closure is live as an overwrite. Then update ADR 0003 and ADR 0006 to agree.

findings.title: A callee that calls a callback more than once is not checked for W0301
findings.description: `fn twice(f: fn()) { f(); f() }`; `let r = &v[0]; twice(|| { print(r + 1); v.clear() })` is accepted. The second call reads a dangling reference (stock: "a place does not exist"). `g(); g()` and `for i in 0..2 { g() }` get W0301. Also accepted and faulty: a loop in the callee (`each`), two levels (`twice2` calls `twice`), and a returned closure that calls its function twice (`wrap`). Cause: the `repeats` part of a signature (ADR 0006) is used only for tasks that a closure spawns. It is not used for the references that the closure captures.
findings.suggested_fix: When a closure goes to a parameter in `repeats` (or to a returned value that calls it twice), check its captures as for two calls in a row: a mutation inside the closure invalidates the references that it captures for the next call (W0301).

findings.title: False W0602 and W0503 for a linear value that lives outside the handle
findings.description: `let l = Lk{id: 1}; let n = handle Ask { fn ask() { 0 } } in { ask() + 1 }; unlock(l)` gets W0602. A multi `pick` inside a local handle gets W0503 and W0602 for `l` outside the handle. Both run cleanly on all seeds. The abort ends at the handler, so `l` is not unwound. A multi resume copies only the frames of the handled body, so it never copies `l`. The same code inside a function (`guarded()`, `solve()`) is accepted, so the result depends on an inline step. Cause: abort_unhandled and live_across_multi use may_abort(P) and multi_at(P) at the perform node with every live value of the body, not only the values inside the handled body. This is not in the ADR 0005 or 0007 imprecision lists.
findings.repro: SCRATCH/r2/oracle/repro/OR4_fp_outside_handle.wf (inline_abort, inline_multi are rejected; call_forms is accepted; all run cleanly)
findings.suggested_fix: For a perform that a local handle handles, limit W0602 and W0503 to the values that are live inside that handled body. Check the outer values at the handle node against the outer handlers only (rule 1 of proofs/effects).

findings.title: A reference made while a task is active stays valid after the join
findings.description: `let t = s.spawn(|| v.clear()); let r = &v[1]; t.join(); print(r + 1)` is accepted. It faults on every seed ("a place does not exist"). The checker counts the task's mutation only at the spawn node. `r` gets its value after that node, so nothing invalidates it. use_after_scope (r = &v[1] inside the scope, used after the scope) has the same defect. The borrow `&v[1]` is also not an access for W0405, although the index reads the length and buffer of `v` while the task clears it. `v.get(1)` and `let n = v[1]` get W0405.
findings.suggested_fix: At the join node and at the scope end, invalidate each reference that points strictly inside a place that the task writes, through an unstable step (or every reference into a place that the task frees). Record a borrow through an index as a read of the indexed place, so W0405 sees it.

findings.title: A variable as an expression statement drops the value at run time; the checker sees no move
findings.description: `let v = Vec.new(); v.push(1); v; print(v.len())` is accepted. The interpreter compiles the statement `v` as a read and a pop, so it moves the value out and drops it. The next use faults ("a value is used after it was moved"). Other effects: a reference into the value dangles (`dangling`); a linear value goes away with no W0601 (`linear_dropped`; the instrumented interpreter reports a linear leak); a !Move value is dropped while its self-reference is used (probes/n8_immov_expr_stmt.wf). Mutation found this from a duplicated tail line `v` in a helper.
findings.suggested_fix: Make sema and the interpreter agree. Either compile a bare place in statement position without a read and a drop, or record moved_at and a drop for it in the facts, so that W0302, W0301 and W0601 apply.

findings.title: A function parameter that runs as a task or a fork branch gets no separation, portability or pinning check
findings.description: `fn par(f: fn(), g: fn()) / par { fork(f, g) }`, then `par(|| n += 1, || n += 2)` is accepted, but two threads write `n`. `fn bg(f: fn()) { scope { s => s.spawn(f); s.spawn(f) } }`, then `bg(|| n += 1)` is accepted, but two tasks write `n`. `bg_and_call` spawns f and calls g at the same time; it is accepted and races. The direct forms get W0403 and W0405. `bg_one(|| print(a.hp))` with `a: Rc<E>` gives a task that the scheduler marks stealable, although it holds a nonportable Rc. The race detector and the stealable check report each case on every seed. Cause: the `tasks` part of a signature (ADR 0006) is used only for W0314 at the caller.
findings.repro: SCRATCH/r2/oracle/repro/OR7_tasks_of_fn_params.wf (via_fork, via_spawn_twice, via_spawn_and_call, stealable_rc); run with the instrumented binary oracle/weft-inst/target/release/weft
findings.suggested_fix: Check a closure that goes to a parameter in `tasks` like a spawn at the call. Apply W0401 and W0403 if the callee can run it on another thread (fork, stealable task). Apply W0405 against itself if the parameter is also in `repeats`, and against the other function arguments that the callee runs in the same scope. Mark the task pinned unless the value is known to be portable.

findings.title: A use or a new value of a whole local is not an access for W0405
findings.description: `let count = 0; scope { s => s.spawn(|| count += 1); print(count) }` is accepted, but it is a data race. Also accepted with races: a task that prints `count` while the parent does `count += 5`; `print(v)` of a whole Vec while a task clears it; `r = &v[1]` while a task reads `r`. Fields (`c.k`), elements (`v[0]`), calls with `&v`, and two tasks that both write `n` are checked correctly. Cause: in crates/weft-sema/src/body/expr.rs, `name()` reads only the places that a reference local points into. It never reads the root place of the local, so a task that only reads a captured variable has no task_reads for it. A new value of a local is rebound_at, not an access.
findings.repro: SCRATCH/r2/oracle/repro/OR8_task_whole_local.wf (parent_reads, task_reads, whole_vec, ref_rebind); run with the instrumented binary
findings.suggested_fix: In name(), when a local is used as a value, read its root place. For W0405, treat a new value of a local as a write of its root place. Keep the ADR 0006 rule that a use of a reference does not read every place that it can reach.

findings.title: A resume inside a spawned task runs the handled body on another task
findings.description: A clause `fn ask() { scope { s => s.spawn(|| { let _ = resume(1) }); print("clause") } }` is accepted. The rest of the handled body then runs on the child task. A later operation of an outer handler on the parent stack then has no handler. The stock interpreter faults with "no handler for `Note.note` on this task" (an unhandled effect at run time). In race(), the body (`c.k += ask()`) runs at the same time as the clause (`c.k += 1`), which is a data race on a field. W0314 checks only the other direction (a task that performs through a handler of another task).
findings.suggested_fix: Reject a resume or a continuation value in a closure that runs as a task or a fork branch. Alternatively, check the handled body as code of that task: W0314 for its operations and W0405 against the clause.

findings.title: False W0405: a call reads all of its reference arguments
findings.description: `let t = s.spawn(|| grow_w(&w)); w.score += 1; t.join()` gets W0405 ("mutates `w.score` while a task reads `w`"). grow_w touches only w.es (inferred mut(w.es)). The program runs cleanly on all seeds. ADR 0006 states the rule ("a call reads its reference arguments"), but the imprecision list does not give its cost. Reduced from generated programs (fp2/W0405_p40989.wf).
findings.suggested_fix: Add this cost to the ADR 0006 imprecisions, or infer a read footprint for each signature, as for `mut`.

findings.title: The stock interpreter is a weak oracle for the design faults
findings.description: With `weft run --unchecked`, these programs run to the end with no error, although the checker rejects them and the design calls them faults. `print` of a dangling reference prints `<dangling>` (show.rs). A reference into a dead local of plain data stays readable. Vec.push never moves the buffer, so a reference into v[] survives a push. A live linear value that goes away silently is not reported. There is no race detector, so W0405, W0401 and W0403 have no dynamic check. So the stock interpreter cannot show OR7 and OR8 at all, and it shows other checker defects only by chance.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the checks of SCRATCH/r2/oracle/interp_oracle.patch to weft-interp behind an option (freed-cell faults, buffer move on mutation, dead-local references, linear leaks, vector-clock races, stealable portability). Then use that option in the corpus and agreement tests.

S5a: implement.summary:
Stage S5a is done on review/s5 in /home/user/wt-core. Base is 328a39b. There are four commits on top: a6f156c, 532a121, 6712164 and 963ed0f (head). Nothing was pushed.

Before each change I reproduced the gap with a program in SCRATCH/s5/p/. At base the checker accepted each one, and each one either faulted in `weft run --unchecked` or broke a design rule. The faults were "no handler for Note.note on this task", `<dangling>`, "a linear value was consumed twice", "has no on abort", and a Tx that was neither committed nor rolled back.

**Status of the items:**
- **Fixed:** 1 (all four parts), 2 (both parts), 3a, 3c, 4 (both parts), 6a, 6b and 6c.
- **Covered already, cases added:** 5. The closure modes from S4 already handle a closure that holds a fresh continuation. I added the r2a, r2a_twice and similar cases to corpus 63.
- **Kept and documented:** 3b. The Vec rule is sound but it rejects too much. The trade-off is in ADR 0007, and corpus 88 has it as a known-gap test.

**One gap outside the task list.** While I worked on 6a, I found a soundness gap: a clause that does not resume ends the handled body, but the graph had no edge for that path. Because of this the checker missed:
- W0301 for a reference that the body gives a new value after the operation;
- W0601 for a linear value outside the body, which the interpreter then leaked;
- W0313 for a local outside the body that keeps a closure.

I added the abort edges, which also made the 6a fix sound. Corpus 89 covers it.

**Spec change for 6b.** It went through the full 8-step checklist. There is a new input relation `empty_at`, so `live_linear` does not start at a value such as `None`. `live_linear` now also starts at `overwrites`. This changes the spec, rules.rs, facts, the bridge, the random generator and the code texts.

**New signature parts:**
- `holds` (3a)
- `fn_stores` (1b)
- `op_effects` (2b)
- `reach_repeats` (2a)
- `RetFn.op_fns` and `RetFn.tasks` (2b)
- `SigStep::Held` (4a)

**Diagnostic changes in existing corpus files:**
- 67 line 95 and the new 85 lines now also get W0314 at the spawn inside the clause. This is a true second report.
- 63 gets the new rule-2 cases.

**Comparison with the base binary.** I ran both on about 4,600 probe and corpus files, plus 3,000 sampled files from r2. The only differences are the expected fixes and the expected W0304 location move. The S4 probe lin1 line 44 and the S3 probe r12d line 27 are now detected, which their own markers expect. The false W0601 for `None` and the false W0313 in e1_fp are gone.

**Speed.** Lowering is about 20% slower on 1,000 sequential handles. The base already grows quadratically there.

**Remaining open items, recorded in ADR 0005:**
- A node that runs a clause and that only the stored-value pass finds gets no abort edge.
- A value the body cannot follow that goes to a caller's operation is not checked for W0314.
- A reference stored behind a closure or clause parameter is still seen as the outer place only.

**Gates** all pass: fmt, clippy with -D warnings, `cargo test --workspace` (483 passed, 0 failed), and `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc`. verify-all.sh was not needed: I did not touch weft-verified or proofs. The scale test once failed on a timing limit under machine load; base did the same, and both pass when run back to back. I deleted the scratch build directories. 12 GB of disk is free.

findings.id: 1a: task runs a function value from a store
findings.evidence: Repro scratchpad/s5/p/i1a.wf, i1a2.wf and item_store.wf were accepted at base and faulted with 'no handler for Note.note on this task'. Now each is W0314. Corpus tests/programs/84_task_stores.wf has these bad cases: behind a reference, a Vec, a closure, by value, through a callee, a user effect in a local field or Vec, a function item behind a reference or in a field, an operation result, a closure parameter and an unknown value. It has controls for a quiet closure, a std effect and a handler inside the task.
findings.notes: Capabilities now carry marks (caps.rs): an escaped effect, a function parameter, and UNKNOWN_FN. A function parameter whose value holds function values is part of `tasks`. Callers check arguments that hold function values. Function items carry their effects. Imprecise, recorded in ADR 0006: a task that runs a value from a closure or clause parameter is W0314.

findings.id: 1b: callee copies a fn value out of a reference argument
findings.evidence: Repro i1b.wf (copy, copy_vec, take_out) was accepted and faulted at base. Now W0313. Corpus 83_kept_values.wf has copies, copies_vec, takes_out, returns_out, returns_pair and closure_copies. Controls: copies_harmless, reads_inside, copies_inside.
findings.notes: New signature part `fn_stores`. A result that can hold a function value gets the capabilities of the reference arguments.

findings.evidence: Repro i1c.wf (local, field, Vec, clause value) was accepted and faulted at base. Now W0313. Corpus 83 has clause_keeps_in_local, in_field, in_vec, returns_it, from_callee and keeps_job. Controls: clause_calls_it, clause_keeps_harmless.
findings.notes: A clause parameter now holds the capabilities of the values that the nodes give to its operation.

findings.evidence: Repro i1d.wf printed <dangling> at base. Now W0301. Corpus 86_op_refs.wf has picks, picks_opt, picks_through_callee, picks_from_argument, picks_out_of_handle, picks_from_caller, mutates_through (W0301) and mutates_undeclared (W0703). A handle that returns a reference into a clause local is W0204. Controls: picks_other, picks_clause_local_inside, picks_from_caller_ok.
findings.notes: New file crates/weft-sema/src/body/oprefs.rs. The op result first points into its own root; at the end of the body its facts are moved onto the places that each resume gives. A result from a caller's handler can point anywhere in the parameters.

findings.id: 2a: stored spawning closure at a reach node starts one copy
findings.evidence: Repro i2a.wf was accepted at base, while two copies of the task both mutated st.count. Now W0405. Corpus 82_stored_spawns.wf has stored_in_field, stored_in_vec, stored_through_callee and stored_closure_runs_twice. Controls: stored_run_once, stored_reads_only.
findings.notes: New signature part `reach_repeats`. A node that can run a stored value twice gets a 'spawn again' node inserted after it.

findings.id: 2b: clause runs a parameter of a finished closure as a task
findings.evidence: The direct closure case was already W0314 at head. Two real shapes were open: i2b3.wf `gives()` and i2b4.wf `mk()`, which faulted at runtime, and i2b5.wf (a returned closure that spawns its parameter). Corpus 85_op_args.wf has callee_gives, callee_gives_through, callee_gives_user_effect, callee_gives_local_log, from_maker (W0313 W0314) and from_spawning_maker. Controls: quiet, runtime log, clause_calls, spawning_maker_ok.
findings.notes: New signature part `op_effects`. RetFn gets `op_fns` and `tasks`.

findings.id: 3a: generic callee aborts or is multi while it holds a linear T
findings.evidence: Repro i3a.wf and i3a2.wf faulted at base ('has no on abort', 'consumed twice'). Now W0602 or W0503. Corpus 81_generic_holds.wf has aborts, multis (W0503 W0602), through_param, in_pair, nested and renamed. Controls: guarded, plain, quiet_param, no_abort_while_held, multi_plain.
findings.notes: New signature part `holds`, found by a dataflow in `finish`. The caller holds a hidden variable of the type argument across the call node, so the spec rules see the linear value there.

findings.id: 3b: Vec of linear values has no consumer
findings.evidence: This is sound: at base it is always W0601, and the interpreter does not track it. Corpus 88_empty_values.wf has vec_drained and vec_left as known-gap cases.
findings.notes: ADR 0007 states the trade-off. A sound consumer needs a run-time check that the Vec is empty, plus an abort path for its elements.

findings.id: 3c: return/break in a later operand leaves a linear value
findings.evidence: Repro i3c.wf was accepted at base, breaking the rule that a linear value must be consumed on every path. Now W0601. Corpus 80_operand_jumps.wf has return, break, continue, tuple, struct field and closure-return cases. Controls: break_inside_operand, return_inside_closure_operand, jump_before_operand, return_after_call.
findings.notes: Values held on their way to a call are tracked with their jump and loop depth. A jump that leaves them ends their scope.

findings.id: 4a: references stored behind a reference parameter
findings.evidence: Repro i4a.wf read_back and i4a2.wf (mutation through a stored reference) were accepted at base and printed <dangling>. Before the fix, a reference read behind a reference parameter had no places at all, so the mutation through it was missing from the facts. Now W0301, W0703 or W0204. Corpus 87_stored_refs.wf has read_back, mutates_stored, mutates_inferred, mutates_in_option, mutates_through_callee, first_elem (W0204) and grow_undeclared (W0703). Controls: read_back_ok, grow_other.
findings.notes: A new root `*p` and `SigStep::Held`; `mut(p..)` and `in p..` cover it. This applies only to parameters whose pointee holds references. Open, in ADR 0003: the same for closure and clause parameters.

findings.id: 4b: stale holder after a join on a continue path
findings.evidence: Repro i4b.wf, plus loopjoin.wf continue_keeps and an if/else case, gave false W0301 at base. Now clean. Corpus 87 has branch_stale and continue_stale; branch_live keeps its real W0301. The break_keeps case is still reported correctly.
findings.notes: This was an imprecision, not a soundness gap. A stale holder now gets a new value on the edges into an if/match join, a loop head and a loop exit.

findings.id: 5: closure that holds a fresh once continuation (rule 2)
findings.evidence: The S4 closure modes already cover it: probe eff2 r2a is W0503 and r2a_twice is W0502. Corpus 63_suspension.wf now has fresh_in_closure, fresh_in_closure_twice, fresh_in_nested_closure, fresh_in_field and fresh_to_callee. Control: fresh_in_closure_after.
findings.notes: No code change. Only the corpus cases were added.

findings.id: 6a: Local.caps only grows (false W0313 after a reassignment)
findings.evidence: Probe e1_fp reassigned gave a false W0313 at base; now it is clean. Corpus 89_abort_paths.wf: reassigned and reassigned_in_loop are clean, while abort_keeps_closure and branch_keeps_closure are W0313.
findings.notes: The W0313 check of locals now follows new values to the end of the handle. To make that sound I fixed a root cause found here: abort paths were missing. A clause that can end with no resume now gives each node that runs it an edge to the end of the handle. Corpus 89 abort_keeps_reference (W0301) and abort_keeps_linear (W0601) were missed at base. scratchpad/s5/p/abort_lin.wf showed the interpreter leaking the linear Tx.

findings.id: 6b: overwriting None of an inferred local is W0601
findings.evidence: Repro i6b.wf and S4 probe v1_infer/v2_none gave false 'overwritten' at base. Now clean, and real W0601, W0602 and W0503 still fire. Corpus 88 has none_then_some, none_in_loop and none_by_path as clean cases; none_then_left, some_then_some, some_then_none, none_then_payload and none_if are bad cases.
findings.notes: New spec input relation `empty_at`, through the full 8-step checklist; random agreement passes. Only a variant with no payload counts as empty. Vec.new() does not, because push can add to it without a new value.

findings.id: 6c: W0304 read inside a handler clause reported on the resume line
findings.evidence: Probe da1.wf a12: at base the error was on the line of the operation; now it is on the line of the read, with a note at the node that runs the clause. Corpus 89 has clause_reads_unset (W0304 on the read line) and clause_reads_set (clean).
findings.notes: Changed in diagnose.rs only. The facts do not change.

design_decisions: Kept marks such as NONPORTABLE and NOT_MANY in the capability sets, and added three more: ESCAPES(effect), PARAM(i) and UNKNOWN_FN. Through them, W0314 follows function values through stores, parameters and callees, using the same paths that W0313 uses.

A by-value or reference parameter of the function that can hold function values gets a PARAM mark. A closure or clause parameter of that kind, and a result from a caller's handler, get UNKNOWN_FN instead, which is conservative: a task that runs one is W0314.
Callee-made closures given to a caller's operation are recorded per effect (`op_effects`) and checked by the caller's clauses. A function parameter given inside data goes to op_fns.
Operation result references are resolved after the body by moving facts from a placeholder root onto the places that each resume gives, the reverse of clause_refs_onto_args.
References behind reference parameters get a separate root `*p`, written in signatures as SigStep::Held. Places with and without Held never cover each other when rows are joined or reduced.

empty_at was added to the spec rather than handled only in sema, so that the checker and the spec still agree. `overwrites` now also starts live_linear, which keeps a part write after an empty bind sound.
Abort edges are added only from nodes in the handle's own part of the graph, and only when a clause can end with no resume. On that edge, the non-linear owners of the body go out of scope.

The W0313 check of locals follows only new values of the whole local in the local's own part of the graph. Stores into parts and new values made in closures or clauses stay in the grow-only (sticky) set.

findings.title: Loop fixpoint stops after 8 passes; a chain of locals loses references, function values and tasks
findings.description: lower_loop (crates/weft-sema/src/body/stmt.rs:806, MAX_LOOP_PASSES = 8) keeps the values of the last pass when the carried values are not stable. Its own comment says a chain of locals needs one pass per local. ADR 0003 argues soundness only for a reference that goes deeper each pass. Ten locals that rotate their values (r0 = r1 ... r9 = &world.entities[0].hp) never give r0 the new place: W0301 is missed after world.entities.clear(). The same holds for function values (W0301) and task closures (W0405). With 7 locals the error is found; with 8 or more it is not. The file checks with 0 errors; all three tests fault with the instrumented interpreter (dangling reference, data race).
findings.suggested_fix: Iterate to the fixpoint (the lattice of places, closures and tasks of the body is finite), or report an error like W0704/W0706 when a bound is reached instead of keeping partial values.

findings.title: A function type carries one closure summary; later closures in arrays, Vecs, Option and generic fields are lost
findings.description: FnTy.summary (crates/weft-sema/src/types.rs:75) is a single Option<usize>. When closures unify in one type, only the first summary survives. Missed with 0 errors: the second element of an array literal or a Vec, an element assignment a[0] = || ..., a new value of an Option local, a new value of a generic struct field (Wrap<T>). The lost closure loses its mutations (W0301), task writes (W0405) and once mode (W0502). Putting the mutating closure first makes the checker find the error. 6/7 tests fault with the stock interpreter, 7/7 with the instrumented one.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep a set of summaries (and joined modes) for a function value, as join_val does for if/match, or keep summaries on the Val and on each container holder instead of in the unified type.

findings.title: A closure that resumes a continuation can leave its clause
findings.description: let k = || print(0); handle Note { fn note(x) { k = || resume(()) } } in note(1); k() is accepted. The closure also escapes through a generic struct field, an Option, or as the value of the handle. The clause does not resume, the handler drops the continuation, and the later call resumes a dropped continuation. W0313 checks handler capabilities only; W0501/W0502 count calls only. All 4 tests fault in both interpreters: 'a continuation was resumed after it was dropped'.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat the continuation as a capability of its clause and apply the W0313 escape rules with the clause as the body.

findings.title: A closure that captures the scope capability s can leave the scope
findings.description: scope { s => keep = || { s.spawn(|| st.count += 1); () } }; keep() is accepted. The facts show the closure local points only into st, not into the root of s, so the end of s does not invalidate it (a closure that captures &s does get W0301). The task starts after its scope ended, no scope joins it, and it outlives the frame: the stock interpreter prints 'task runs, count 1' after the caller's local ended; the instrumented one reports a dangling reference. Same for the scope value and for a field of an outer local. Breaks 'children can't outlive the scope'.
findings.suggested_fix: Make a capture of s point into the root of s (as a capture of &s does), so scope_end of s invalidates the closure (W0301).

findings.title: resume carries mutations of the handled body to the clause, but not frees
findings.description: A clause takes r = &world.entities[0], calls resume(()), then reads r. The handled body moves world (take_w(world)). No W0301. The control with world.entities.clear() in the handled body gets W0301. The test faults in both interpreters (dangling reference).
findings.suggested_fix: Make the resume node carry the frees_at (moves, scope ends) of the handled computation, as it carries its mutations.

findings.title: A function value that a clause gives with resume is called with no summary
findings.description: handle Get { fn get() { resume(|| world.entities.clear()) } } in { let f = get(); f(); print(first.hp) } is accepted; the same inside a tuple. ADR 0005 records only the reference case as open and claims the capabilities are carried; the mutations, effects and modes of the closure are lost at the call in the handled body. Both tests fault in both interpreters.
findings.suggested_fix: Lower the resume values of the clauses before (or iterate with) the handled body, or treat the operation result as an unknown function value that can run each closure the clauses give; record it in ADR 0005.

findings.title: A closure keeps the places, summary and modes of a captured variable from where it is made
findings.description: ADR 0003 says a closure refers to the captured variable cell, but the lowering snapshots its places/summary/modes at creation. A later new value is lost. Missed with 0 errors: W0301 for a captured reference rebound then cleared (also via a higher-order callee), W0405 for a task that reads a rebound captured reference, W0301 for a captured fn variable rebound to a mutating closure, W0502 for one rebound to a once closure, W0402 for a reference rebound to a @shared place, W0406 for a uniq variable rebound to an aliased value. Same cause as oracle OR2 (moves), different shape. 5/5 runtime tests fault in both interpreters.
findings.suggested_fix: At each node where a closure runs, join the current places, summaries and modes of its captured variables (or make captured variables flow-insensitive for the closure).

findings.title: Vec.clear drops linear elements silently
findings.description: fn reset(v: &Vec<Tx>) / mut(v) { v.clear() } is accepted; so is a generic clear_any<T>(v: &Vec<T>) used with Vec<Tx>. The prelude clear(self) / mut(self) has no parameter of the element type, so the ADR 0007 drops rules do not apply (v.pop() as a statement does get W0601). A caller that hands the Vec on (here to an extern fn) is accepted. The instrumented interpreter reports a linear leak at the clear.
findings.suggested_fix: Give clear (and any prelude function that drops elements) a drops part for the element type parameter, so a call on a Vec of a linear type is W0601.

findings.title: A generic function item used as a function value skips its drops part
findings.description: fn sink<T>(x: T) {} drops its argument. sink(begin()) and let g = sink; g(begin()) get W0601, but feed(begin(), sink), feed_tx(begin(), sink) with f: fn(Tx), and let g = sink; feed_tx(begin(), g) are accepted. All three tests fault with the instrumented interpreter (linear leak).
findings.suggested_fix: When a generic item becomes a function value, check its drops part against the inferred type arguments (W0601 at the item value), as at a direct call.

findings.title: Named arguments: sema binds by name, the interpreter by position (method calls on values, function item values)
findings.description: Sema binds named arguments by name for x.method(b: .., a: ..) and for a call of a function item value (let h = show; h(n: 5, e: &y)). The interpreter compiles both with args() in written order and Op::CallMethod / Op::CallValue, ignoring names (compile.rs method_call, call). The program checks with 0 errors; x.diff(b: 10, a: 3) prints 7 instead of -7, and h(n: 5, e: &y) faults with 'this value has no field hp' (an &Entity parameter gets an i32). W0301/W0312 also reason about an order and binding the run does not use. Direct item calls and operations agree (RT24 fix).
findings.suggested_fix: Compile these calls with the slot logic of call_fn when the callee is statically known, or reject named arguments where it is not.

findings.title: An effect declared in another module or package cannot be named for handle or a row
findings.description: handle takes one NAME and a row item is one NAME, resolved in the current module; handle a.Note and / a.Note do not parse. So mod a { pub effect Note ..; pub fn f() / Note } cannot be handled by main (W0101 + W0805) or stated by a caller with a signature (W0101 + W0702). The same for a dependency package (util.noting()). ADR 0005 says a dependency's user effect needs a handler of the caller, which cannot be written. Hints suggest uncompilable fixes ('add Note to the effects', 'handle main.a.Log in main').
findings.suggested_fix: Allow a path in handle and in effect rows (handle util.Note, / util.Note) resolved like type paths, or record the limit in ADR 0005 and fix the hints.

findings.title: W0304 false positive when a closure, clause or task gives a let x: T local its value
findings.description: let x: u64; let f = || { x = 1 }; f(); print(x) gets W0304 twice (at the closure and at print); same for a handler clause and a joined task. The program runs and prints 1, 7, 3. Rust also rejects the closure form, so this may be a choice, but ADR 0007 documents it only for place fields.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the limit for locals, or treat the closure/clause/task as an assignment at each node where it runs.

findings.title: Named arguments to a positional constructor or a closure bind by position, unknown names accepted
findings.description: Range(hi: 10, lo: 2) makes lo = 10, hi = 2; Range(nope: 2, other: 10) is accepted; a closure f(b: 10, a: 3) gives a = 10. Sema and the interpreter agree, so nothing faults, but the same syntax binds by name for function calls.
findings.suggested_fix: Bind by name, or reject named arguments (W0103/W0104) where the callee has no parameter names.

findings.title: Interpreter does not check unsigned widths of locals and results
findings.description: print(a - b) with a: u64 = 2, b: u64 = 10 prints -8; 250 + 10 on u8 prints 260. The range check exists only when a field or parameter gets the value (exec.rs:653, exec.rs:899). The reference interpreter is a weaker oracle for integer code.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the declared integer type on each arithmetic result (or on each store to a typed local), as for fields and parameters.

findings.title: An operation named like a prelude function is shadowed silently
findings.description: effect Nap { fn sleep(d: Duration) }: a bare sleep(1.ms) resolves to the prelude sleep (Clock) in sema and in the interpreter; the clause never runs and a function stating / Nap gets W0702 for Clock. Same for print. No diagnostic says the operation name is hidden.
findings.suggested_fix: Report W0107 (or a warning) for an operation whose name a prelude function hides.

review2: redteam.summary: Red-team round 2 on commit 328a39b (/home/user/wt-edge, read-only). About 60 probe files (~400 functions) under scratchpad/r2/redteam/p, compared with //~ markers by cmp.py, and each unsound case confirmed at run time with the stock interpreter and the oracle lens's instrumented interpreter. weft agree passes on every probe, so all defects are in fact generation (weft-sema) or the interpreter. Found 10 blockers: RR1 loop fixpoint capped at 8 passes loses chained references/function values/tasks; RR2 one closure summary per function type loses later closures in arrays, Vecs, Option and generic fields (W0301/W0405/W0502); RR3 continuation-resuming closures escape their clause; RR4 the scope capability s escapes in a closure so a task outlives its scope; RR5 resume does not carry frees of the handled body; RR6 function values given by resume have no summary; RR7 closures snapshot captured variables at creation, so later rebinding is missed (W0301/W0405/W0502/W0402/W0406; same cause as OR2); RR8 Vec.clear drops linear elements; RR9 generic item values skip their drops part; RR10 named arguments bind by name in sema but by position in the interpreter for method calls on values and item-value calls (type confusion at run time). 1 major: RR11 effects of other modules/packages cannot be named in handle or rows. 4 minors: RR12 W0304 false positive for closure/clause/task assignment, RR13 named args to constructors/closures bind by position, RR14 interpreter ignores unsigned widths for locals/results, RR15 operations shadowed by prelude functions. Round-1 fixes hold for owner invalidation, reads through references, argument order of direct calls, jumps, W0313, suspension points, forwarding, effect identity, pub, !Move and type properties, overwrites, W0120 and references inside values. Repros in scratchpad/r2/redteam/repro, results in scratchpad/r2/redteam/verify.txt.

findings.title: Loop fixpoint stops after 8 passes with no diagnostic; W0301 and W0703 are lost
findings.description: In crates/weft-sema/src/body/stmt.rs:805-835, `lower_loop` stops after MAX_LOOP_PASSES = 8. Then it keeps the values of the last pass and gives no diagnostic. A chain of k locals in one loop needs k+1 passes. With a chain of 8 locals, the last value never gets to the loop head. Example: g0 = g1; ...; g7 = grow. The 9th iteration calls `grow`, which invalidates `first`, but there is no W0301. The same occurs for references: c0 = c1; ...; c7 = b. The 9th iteration clears b.entities, but there is no W0703. With 7 locals the checker reports both errors. ADR 0003 states the limit only for a reference that goes deeper in each iteration, and it says that case stays sound. The chain case is not sound. The S5 branch keeps the same code.
findings.repro: SCRATCH/r2/quality/repro/QA1_loop_pass_cap.wf: `weft check` gives 0 errors, and 2 are expected. QA1_control_chain7.wf has the same code with 7 locals and gives W0301 and W0703.
findings.suggested_fix: Iterate to the fixpoint, because the joined state only grows. Widen a value that still changes after N passes: a place becomes the wildcard of its base, and a function value becomes unknown. If a bound is hit, give an internal error, as W0706 does. Never keep the last values silently.

findings.title: Effects of an `on abort` function are not counted; the checker accepts a program that faults at run time
findings.description: `check_on_aborts` (crates/weft-sema/src/program.rs:594) checks only the parameter of the `on abort` function. At a node that can abort while a value with `on abort` is live, the lowering does not add the row of that function. In the repro, f holds a Tx across work(), which can fail. The unwind runs rollback, and rollback performs Note. No signature states Note, and no handler handles it. This shape is not in the open lists of ADR 0005 or ADR 0007.
findings.repro: SCRATCH/r2/quality/repro/QA2_on_abort_effects.wf: `weft check` gives 0 errors. `weft run` stops with "runtime error: no handler for `Note.note` on this task" at rollback (exit 1).
findings.suggested_fix: At each may_abort node where a value with `on abort` is live, perform the row and the mutations of the `on abort` function (perform_at). Also add that function as an edge of infer::NameGraph. Another option: require the `on abort` function to have no effects that an unwind cannot perform, and report a violation with W0118.

findings.title: An `in` place that names a later parameter with its own `in` place gets no places
findings.description: `lower_fn` (crates/weft-sema/src/body/stmt.rs:48-52) substitutes the `in` places in the order of the parameters. Take `fn h(v: &Vec<E>, a: &E in b, b: &E in v[])`. When the loop does `a`, `bases[2]` (for b) is still empty. So `a` has no points_into, and no mutation can invalidate it. h2 has the same meaning with the parameters in the other order, and it gets W0301. The code is older than round 1. But round 1 added the W0201 cycle check for these chains, and the round-1 test the_in_place_check_is_fast_on_a_long_chain uses this forward shape (see QA13).
findings.repro: SCRATCH/r2/quality/repro/QA3_param_place_order.wf: `weft check` gives W0301 for h2 only, and 2 errors are expected. `weft facts QA3_param_place_order.wf h` shows no points_into for `a` (v1).
findings.suggested_fix: Substitute the `in` places in topological order. The W0201 cycle check already has the dependency graph. Another fix: repeat the loop until no base changes. Because there are no cycles, this stops after at most n rounds.

findings.title: Ctx::overlaps is exponential in nested wildcard places; a 20-line program does not finish
findings.description: Each result of an unknown function value points into the wildcard of its argument. So `cur = step(cur)` makes head.. .. .., one level for each call, and a loop adds 8 levels (8 passes). In crates/weft-check/src/rules.rs, `bases[p]` already holds every wildcard ancestor of p. But `Ctx::overlaps`, which round 1 added, calls itself for each base of both sides, and so do mutation_kills and free_kills. The cost is about 2^depth for each pair of places. Straight-line walk: 24 calls 0.18 s, 26 calls 0.73 s, 28 calls 2.8 s, 30 calls 12 s, 32 calls 47 s. Three loops of `while .. { cur = step(cur) }` take 1.6 s. Four loops give no result after 300 s. Callgrind puts 99.9% of the time in Ctx::overlaps. The Datalog spec runs the same program quickly.
findings.repro: SCRATCH/r2/quality/repro/QA4_wild_walk_4loops.wf does not finish (timeout at 300 s). QA4_wild_walk_3loops.wf takes 1.6 s. `python3 QA4_wild_walk_gen.py K` makes the straight-line walk.
findings.suggested_fix: `p.. ..` is the same set of places as `p..`. Make FnFacts::wildcard(p) return the outermost wildcard when p is already below one. In the checker, compare only the outermost bases. Overlap is closed under prefixes, so this is exact. Or iterate over ({a} ∪ bases[a]) × ({b} ∪ bases[b]) with no recursion. Add a scale test with 4 such loops.

findings.title: A dependency named `main` shares the effect identities of the root; W0701 is lost
findings.description: effects::identity gives a user effect of the root the identity `main.<Name>`. A dependency module gets its manifest name. With [dependencies.main], the `Note` of the dependency and the `Note` of the root both become `main.Note`. The root handler of its own Note then handles the effect of the dependency. The library function `quiet` gets no W0701. Two different effects become one effect, so effect tracking is wrong. The trigger (a dependency named main) is narrow.
findings.repro: SCRATCH/r2/quality/repro/QA5_dep_named_main/: `weft check` gives 0 errors. QA5_control_dep/ is the same package with the dependency named `dep`, and it gives W0701 for `quiet`.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the root a prefix that a manifest name cannot be (for example `<root>`). Or reject the dependency name `main` with W0107. Check that `weft deps` and the interpreter use the same identities.

findings.title: A write through a wildcard reference invalidates that reference (false W0301 on common code)
findings.description: A call result with no stated place points into `v..`. Examples are `-> Option<&Entity>` and the result of a function parameter. The round-1 wildcard rules (spec/weft.dl:123-125,131-132 and rules.rs mutation_kills) cause two false positives. First: a write through the reference itself overlaps v, so the reference becomes invalid. This is also so for a scalar field through a stable step, so `e.hp -= 1; e.hp -= 1` is W0301. Second: the rule `wild_at(M, B), prefix(B, Path)` uses prefix where strict_prefix is correct. So `b.items.push(1); print(boxes.len())` invalidates the reference `boxes` itself. ADR 0003 states the wildcard rule, but its list of imprecisions does not name this effect. This is a spec-level item, so the spec lens must agree.
findings.repro: SCRATCH/r2/quality/repro/QA6_wildcard_self_write.wf: `weft check` gives 3 errors at lines 17, 25 and 32, and 0 are expected. With `-> Option<&Entity in v[]>`, the same body gives no error.
findings.suggested_fix: Use strict_prefix(B, Path) in the wild_at(M, B) rules. Give each call result its own wildcard instance (a fresh split). Then a write at or below that instance through stable steps can use rule 3 for references into the same instance. A plain !prefix(Path, M) guard is not sound while two results share one interned `v..` place.

findings.title: Each loop pass clones the whole lowering state; many loops in one function are quadratic
findings.description: In lower_loop (crates/weft-sema/src/body/stmt.rs:805-1033), each pass does `let head = self.clone()`. That clones all 60 fields of Lower: the facts so far, the locals, the `scope` map with String keys, and the summaries. `carried` formats a BTreeSet<String> key for each local outside the loop, twice in each pass. So one loop costs O(size of the function so far). With typed integers: 250 loops 0.09 s, 500 loops 0.31 s, 1000 loops 1.25 s, 2000 loops 5.7 s. With 4000 locals before 200 small loops, the time is 1.3 s. Callgrind on 500 loops: the clone and drop of Lower take more than 50% of the time, and String clones take 38%.
findings.repro: SCRATCH/r2/quality/repro/QA7_seq_loops_gen.py N, and the sample QA7_seq_loops_1000.wf (1.3 s in release).
findings.suggested_fix: Save and restore only the loop-carried state: locals[..outer], the part holders and the branch state. For the fact vectors, which only grow, keep their lengths at the head and cut them back on rewind. Make the key only for the locals that the loop body assigns. Find them once.

findings.title: The integer type-variable chain makes repeated `s += 1` quadratic
findings.description: `Infer::unify(IntVar a, IntVar b)` binds the end of the old chain to the new variable of the literal (crates/weft-sema/src/types.rs:145-246). So each update of an untyped integer local adds one link. Then `shallow` and `occurs` walk the whole chain. There is no path compression and no union by rank. Round 1 keeps integer literals open (c710ad0), so the chain grows. Untyped: 2000 updates 0.17 s, 4000 updates 0.66 s, 8000 updates 2.8 s, 16000 updates 10.9 s. With `let s: i64 = 0`, 16000 updates take 0.06 s. 4000 `if` blocks with `s += 1` take 1.2 s, and callgrind gives 80% of that time in Infer::shallow.
findings.repro: SCRATCH/r2/quality/repro/QA8_int_chain_gen.py N [typed], and the sample QA8_int_chain_8000.wf (2.6 s in release).
findings.suggested_fix: When both sides are variables, bind the newer variable to the older one, with union by rank. Compress paths in shallow (&mut self, or Cell entries). A bind of a variable to a variable needs no occurs walk.

findings.title: Functions and lowering state too large to read; implicit invariants
findings.description: call_fn_as has 548 lines (call.rs:264). Round 1 reported call_fn at 324 lines. diagnose has 462 lines (it had 253). handle has 266 lines, call_value 255 and closure 219. Lower has 60 fields, and lower_loop clones all of them. rewind keeps 8 tables, and the struct doc tells the next author to add each new field to lower_loop by hand. Nothing enforces this rule. CapId also carries mode marks in its high bits (RESUMED, NONPORTABLE, NOT_MANY), so each user of a capability set must filter them. The workspace-wide `too_many_lines = "allow"` hides all of this.
findings.suggested_fix: Split call_fn_as into argument ordering, argument evaluation, call node, place checks and function-value effects. Split diagnose into one function for each rule. Put the loop-carried state into one struct that lower_loop saves and restores. Use a separate type for the mode marks.

findings.title: The corpus runner compares sets, so `//~ W0601 W0601` cannot count errors
findings.description: crates/weft-check/tests/programs.rs collects (line, code) into a BTreeSet. 72_linear_drops.wf:259 is marked `//~ W0601 W0601`, but one error also passes. Six other corpus lines give two errors with the same code today, and their markers name the code once. The second error is not tested.
findings.repro: SCRATCH/r2/quality/repro/QA10_find_dups.sh lists 7 lines with duplicate codes. The analysis is in QA10_corpus_set_compare.txt.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare sorted multisets (a Vec of (line, code)).

findings.title: One invalid use gives two W0301 errors, and one names a hidden variable
findings.description: `print(w.x.hp)` after `clear` gives two errors: "`w` used after it was invalidated" and "the value in `w.x` used after it was invalidated". In 45_stored.wf:47, the internal name `{stored closure}`, with braces, is in the user text.
findings.suggested_fix: Group W0301 by (use node, invalidating node). Show the user variable, and put the hidden holder in a note.

findings.title: The public diagnose() returns notes with raw `{line:N}` markers
findings.description: weft_check::diagnose::diagnose is public. Its notes hold in-band markers ({line:OFFSET}, {lines:...}). Only check_analysis resolves them, with resolve_lines, and the doc comment of diagnose does not say this. A library user gets the text "invalidated at line {line:54}". The markers are plain text, so a label or a place display that contains `{line:` would also be changed.
findings.repro: SCRATCH/r2/quality/repro/QA12_raw_note_markers.rs is a harness binary. It prints "v is a strict prefix of v[], through an unstable step  →  invalidated at line {line:54}" and "used at line {line:68}".
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the node offsets in a typed field of the note (for example Note { text, lines }). Or make diagnose take the SourceFile and resolve the lines itself.

findings.title: Tests assert too little (QA3 hides in one) or depend on the clock
findings.description: First: the_in_place_check_is_fast_on_a_long_chain uses the forward `in` chain of QA3. It checks only the codes and the time. The facts of x0 to x(n-2) are empty, and the test does not see this. Second: these tests have wall-clock limits that can fail on a loaded CI machine: scale.rs:39,133 (< 1 s), weft-sema tests.rs:1059,1080,1097 (< 2 s) and tests.rs:1208 (< 10 s). Third: no scale test covers QA4, QA7 or QA8, and scale.rs times only check(), not sema.
findings.repro: SCRATCH/r2/quality/repro/QA13_in_chain.wf: `weft facts QA13_in_chain.wf f` shows points_into only for the last two of 7 parameters. Details are in QA13_tests.txt.
findings.suggested_fix: Assert the facts (points_into for each parameter) in the in-chain test. Replace the wall-clock limits with counts of work: lowerings, loop passes or overlaps calls. Add scale tests for nested wildcards, many loops and long untyped integer chains.

review2: quality.summary:
Quality lens, commit 328a39b: 13 findings (3 blockers, 5 majors, 5 minors).

Blockers:
- QA1: the loop fixpoint in sema stops silently after 8 passes. A chain of 8 locals in a loop loses W0301 and W0703.
- QA2: the effects of an `on abort` function are not counted. The checker accepts the program, and the interpreter stops with "no handler for Note.note".
- QA3: an `in` place that names a later `in` parameter gets no places, so W0301 is lost. This is older code, but a round-1 test hides it.

Majors:
- QA4: Ctx::overlaps is exponential in nested wildcard places. A 20-line program with 4 loops of `cur = step(cur)` does not finish in 300 s.
- QA5: a dependency named `main` shares the effect identities of the root, so W0701 is lost.
- QA6: a write through a wildcard reference invalidates that reference. This gives false W0301 on `e.hp -= 1; e.hp -= 1` after `find() -> Option<&T>`.
- QA7: each loop pass clones all 60 fields of Lower, so many loops in one function are quadratic.
- QA8: the type-variable chain of an untyped integer makes repeated `s += 1` quadratic.

Minors:
- QA9: call_fn_as has 548 lines and diagnose 462 lines. Lower has implicit invariants.
- QA10: the corpus runner compares sets, so it cannot count errors.
- QA11: one invalid use gives two W0301 errors, and one names a hidden variable.
- QA12: the public diagnose() returns raw {line:N} markers.
- QA13: weak tests and wall-clock limits.

The round-1 quality fixes hold:
- All 11 round-1 repros give no crash and are fast.
- Fuzzing found no panic and no checker/spec disagreement: 275k mutated corpus programs (80k also through --explain) and 6k generated programs, in a build with overflow checks.
- The S5 branch does not change the code of QA1, QA3, QA4, QA7 or QA8.

The worktree /home/user/wt-edge is not changed. The repro files are in SCRATCH/r2/quality/repro/.

review2: fidelity.summary: Fidelity lens, commit 328a39b. 15 findings: 3 blockers, 2 majors, 10 minors. All three blockers come from proof rules or model assumptions that the checker does not mirror. FD1: the effects of an `on abort` function are never checked. A user-effect perform there faults with "no handler", and an `rc`-group mutation there invalidates nothing, which leaves a dangling reference (the oracle's instrumented interpreter confirms it). FD2: nested `multi` continuations share one exec record, so an accepted program faults with "resumed after it was dropped". FD3: a reference stored into an `rc` object outlives its owner; the borrowing proof's "no stored references" assumption is not mirrored for `rc` groups. Majors: FD4, the multi rule ignores affine and `!Move` values (the interpreter deep-copies them; no ADR records this; it conflicts with `!Move`). FD5, proofs/README.md says the agreement tests check the link's sema-fact hypotheses; they do not. Minors: stale ADR 0009 derivation-printer claim; stale per-module proof counts; spec rule r29 never fires on the corpus; `forwards(H)` has two meanings and an architecture diagram edge has no spec rule; the `env`, `@ shared` and global-root design statements have no enforcement and no ADR; traceability.md is still missing; the effects README names an exec checker that does not exist; W0109, W0110 and W0113 have no test; the borrowing and effects mutation tables have no script. Agreement holds: about 20 000 programs (corpus, examples and interpreter programs under each profile, 8 041 mutated programs that parse, 11 997 programs from the other lenses) give 0 disagreements and 0 crashes. The proof counts hold at Verus 1888846b (169/122/233/66, 0 errors), and all 26 link mutations are caught. The round-1 fixes hold. Repros are in scratchpad/r2/fidelity/repro (FD1_run.sh to FD15_run.sh plus .wf files).

findings.title: The effects of an `on abort` function are not checked
findings.description: The effects proof models `on abort` as atomic: it cannot perform or fail. No ADR records the gap, and the checker does not mirror the assumption. No rule rejects an `on abort` function with effects. No node gets the named effects or the `mut` places of the `on abort` functions that the unwinder can run there. Result 1: an `on abort` function performs a user effect. The interpreter stops with 'no handler for Ask.ask on this task'. This happens when an `Ask` handler is in scope around the whole computation, and also when no handler exists anywhere (no W0805, no W0702). Result 2: an `on abort` function mutates an `rc` group (`/ mut(Node)`, pushes). The caller holds `r = &a.items[0]` across the `handle` whose body aborts. No caller node has `mutates_at` for `Node`, so W0301 is missing. The oracle lens's instrumented interpreter reports 'access to a freed cell'.
findings.suggested_fix: Choose one option and record it in ADR 0007. Option 1: reject `on abort` functions that have user effects or `mut` places (a sema check next to W0118). This matches the proof. Option 2: treat each `may_abort` node as a call of the `on abort` function of each live linear value: add its effects to `escapes_at` and its `mut` places to `mutates_at` at that node and at the caller node that sees the abort; run it in the frame's handler environment; then extend the effects model or list the gap in its README.

findings.title: Nested `multi` continuations share one exec record, so an accepted program faults
findings.description: A clause of the multi operation `pick` holds its fresh continuation k. While it holds k, it performs the outer multi operation `choose`. The checker accepts this, because rule 2 covers only fresh `once` continuations. The outer clause resumes twice. `copy_frames` copies the code frames, but each copied `Frame::Clause { cont }` keeps the same record for k. The first copy returns without a resume, so `drop_now` marks k as `Dropped` and drops its frames. The second copy resumes k, and the interpreter stops with 'a continuation was resumed after it was dropped'. The effects model allows this run. `proofs/link/README.md` (`ex_multi_dropped_resume`) records only the exec/model difference. No ADR and no interpreter doc says that accepted programs fault. The interpreter doc says that it supports multi-shot continuations.
findings.repro: SCRATCH/r2/fidelity/repro/FD2_run.sh (FD2_multi_nested_drop.wf faults; FD2_control_resume_first.wf, with the branches swapped, runs)
findings.suggested_fix: Give each copied Clause frame its own continuation record (copy the nested continuation and its frames), or do not drop the frames of a fresh `multi` continuation that another copy can resume. Add the program to crates/weft-interp/tests/programs.

findings.title: A reference stored into an `rc` object outlives its owner
findings.description: The borrowing proof assumes that no reference is stored in the heap (it calls this 'no back channels'). Weft lets a generic container hold references, and an `rc` group can be reached from any function that has a handle. In the repro, `stash(c: Rc<Cache>, x: &u64) / mut(Cache)` pushes x into `c.refs`. `fill` calls it with `&v[0]` of its own local v, and v goes out of scope at the end of `fill`. Later, `read` uses `c.refs[0]`. The checker accepts the program. The stock interpreter stops with 'a place does not exist', and the instrumented interpreter reports a dangling reference. The known ADR 0003 item names only reference parameters. This channel goes through an `rc` group and has no parameter, so the callers cannot follow it.
findings.repro: SCRATCH/r2/fidelity/repro/FD3_run.sh (FD3_rc_backchannel.wf; FD3_known_ref_param_backchannel.wf shows the known shape)
findings.suggested_fix: Treat a store into a place under an `rc` group root, or under a reference parameter, as an escape. The stored references must not point into a local, a by-value parameter or a temporary of the function (a check like W0204). Record the rule in ADR 0003.

findings.title: The multi rule does not count affine or `!Move` values, and the interpreter copies them at each resume
findings.description: The design says that every value live across a multi perform must be `@ many`, and that values are affine by default. `once_var` covers only linear values, `uniq` values, `once` closures and continuations. The checker therefore accepts an owned Vec that the code moves after `choose()`. It also accepts a `!Move` struct with a self-reference live across `choose()`. The interpreter keeps these programs safe because it deep-copies the owned cells at each resume (`copy_frames`). This semantics exists only in the interpreter: no ADR records it. It gives a `!Move` value a new address in each copy, which conflicts with ADR 0007 and the design. The E5 proof does not cover it, and a native runtime cannot copy an arbitrary owned value.
findings.repro: SCRATCH/r2/fidelity/repro/FD4_run.sh (FD4_multi_affine.wf, FD4_multi_immovable.wf: 0 errors; the facts show immovable(v0) and multi_at)
findings.suggested_fix: At minimum, treat `immovable(V)` as not `many` in `live_across_multi`. Then decide the rule for affine values (either not `many`, or a defined copy) and record it in ADR 0005 and ADR 0007.

findings.title: proofs/README.md says that the agreement tests check the sema-fact hypotheses of the link
findings.description: proofs/README.md says: 'The facts that sema emits and the glue in rules.rs are hypotheses of the link: tests check them (agreement with the Datalog spec).' Agreement (`driver::agreement_with`) runs the checker and the spec on the same facts. It tests the glue in rules.rs, but it cannot test `facts_ok`, `bound_before_use` or `ret_ok`. ADR 0002 says this too. As an example, the OR1 repro violates `facts_ok`, faults at run time, and still agrees.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the sentence to say that agreement tests only the glue in rules.rs. The facts are tested only by the sema unit tests and the corpus diagnostics, and `ret_ok` and `bound_before_use` have no test.

findings.title: ADR 0009 has a stale claim that the derivation printer recurses
findings.description: ADR 0009 says that the derivation printer of `check --explain` recurses once for each step and that the limit tests do not cover it. In fact, `bridge::render` uses a stack, and limits.rs tests it on a 2 MiB thread. docs/architecture.md describes this correctly.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the sentence from ADR 0009.

findings.title: The per-module proof counts are stale
findings.description: crates/weft-verified/README.md gives `places` 25, but Verus gives 27. proofs/link/README.md gives `places` 25 and `examples` 22, but Verus gives 27 and 23. The totals (66 and 233) are correct.
findings.repro: SCRATCH/r2/fidelity/repro/FD7_run.sh (the script verifies a copy with --verify-module)
findings.suggested_fix: Update the two tables.

findings.title: No corpus program fires spec rule r29, and the coverage test checks only sinks
findings.description: I wrote one lint for each of the 76 spec rules. 75 of them fire on tests/programs. The rule `invalidated_at(R,P) :- points_into(R,Path), lends_mut(P,M), wild_at(M,B), prefix(B,Path)` never fires. A probe fires it, and the checker agrees with the spec. `corpus_exercises_every_rule` checks only the sink relations. So only the random agreement test finds a change of r29 in one of the two implementations, and no test finds the same wrong change in both.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the probe to the corpus. Extend the corpus coverage test to each spec rule, for example with the lint method.

findings.title: `forwards(H)` has two meanings, and a diagram edge has no spec rule
findings.description: The spec header lists an input `forwards(H)` that means 'H is a root handler of sim.run'. The spec also derives `forwards(H)` with the meaning 'a clause performs the effect outward'. A user lint over `forwards` therefore also sees the sim.run handlers. Separately, docs/architecture.md draws `spawn → task_writes → mutates_at`, but no spec rule exists for that edge: sema writes `mutates_at` at the spawn node.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the input to `sim_root(H)` and add `forwards(H) :- sim_root(H).` Redraw the diagram edge as spawn → mutates_at, labelled 'sema'.

findings.title: '`main` receives the root capabilities through env' has no enforcement and no ADR
findings.description: In Phase 1 the effect row is the capability. A `main` with no `env` parameter, and a helper that it calls, perform Rand and Clock. The checker accepts the program and it runs. No ADR records this departure from the design.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one line to ADR 0005: rows are the capabilities, and `env` holds only handles.

findings.title: Two design statements have no enforcement and no ADR: `@ shared` and global roots
findings.description: The design says that data that several threads see must be `shared` or split. Two fork branches read through one aliased reference that is not `@ shared`, and the checker accepts this. It is safe, because W0403 and W0405 cover writes, but ADR 0006 does not say so. The design also lists a global as a place root. The grammar has no global item, and ADR 0003 does not say that globals are out of scope.
findings.suggested_fix: Record both decisions: the read rule in ADR 0006, and 'no globals in Phase 1' in ADR 0003.

findings.title: docs/traceability.md is still missing
findings.description: The design header and plan item W10 name docs/traceability.md, but the file does not exist. Round 1 reported this as F11.
findings.suggested_fix: Write the matrix. The tables in section (1) of the report can be its seed.

findings.title: The effects README names an exec effects checker in weft-verified that does not exist
findings.description: proofs/effects/README.md says that the exec checker in crates/weft-verified is not linked to the Verus spec checker. weft-verified has no effects checker. The production effects rules are the sema facts (`may_abort`, `multi_at`, `clause_multi`, `body_multi`, `resumes_at`) and the spec rules for W0602 and W0503. Those are the real unlinked part.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the sentence to name the real unlinked part: the sema suspension facts and the spec rules W0602 and W0503.

findings.title: W0109, W0110 and W0113 have no test
findings.description: The code emits these three diagnostics, and `weft explain` has a text for each. No corpus program, unit test or CLI test names them.
findings.suggested_fix: Add negative cases, for example in tests/programs/50_items_bad.wf.

findings.title: The borrowing and effects mutation tables have no script
findings.description: ADR 0008 asks for a documented mutation test for each theorem. Only proofs/link has mutations/run.sh. The 9 borrowing rows and the 8 effects rows cannot be re-run from the tree. I re-ran two effects rows by hand, and they give the documented result (121 verified, 1 error).
findings.suggested_fix: Add mutations/ scripts to proofs/borrowing and proofs/effects, in the same form as proofs/link/mutations.

review2: interp.summary:
I found 11 problems in the interp lens: 2 blockers, 6 majors and 3 minors. All proofs verify with the counts in the READMEs: borrowing 169, effects 122, link 233, weft-verified 66, 0 errors. No proof file uses assume, admit, external_body or a verifier attribute, and the vacuity guards apply the theorems to real accepted runs. cargo test -p weft-interp passes, and the round-1 fixes I checked still hold.

Blockers:
- IP1: a Fail handler can resume a failure that the runtime raises (join, scope end, fork, with_timeout, the child-failure interrupt). The resumed () then stands where a value of type T is needed. Seven accepted programs fault at run time; one hits an internal fault ("a value reached a fork mark"). The effects model assumes that a fail clause never resumes, and nothing enforces this.
- IP3: a stealable task makes an Rc and shares it with a pinned child. The scheduler steals the parent, so the parent and the child change one Rc count on two workers at the same virtual instant.

Majors:
- IP2: a child failure goes to whatever handler is current where the owner is suspended. A callee's private handler can catch it, and the result depends on timing.
- IP4: a multi-shot copy keeps the cells of a handler clause inside the continuation. The program prints [0, 1]; the correct output is [1, 1].
- IP5: a with_timeout deadline is lost when the block waits in an outer clause or runs inside a multi continuation.
- IP6: fork gives () when every branch returns (). A generic caller that expects a tuple faults.
- IP7: every HTTP request task is stealable, whatever the checker says.
- IP8: the B6 link hypotheses fail on what sema emits for accepted programs. bound_before_use breaks in 76_ref_flow loop_replaces_part, and ret_ok breaks through the in-form of a parameter. no_gen_kill holds on the whole corpus.

Minors:
- IP9: sim.run output changes with --workers.
- IP10: the simulation is global state, so tasks and clauses outside it see its clock, which can go backward.
- IP11: ADR 0010 claims a simulated network, but sim.net.partition changes nothing.

Each finding has a repro file. repro/run_all.sh runs all of them.

findings.title: A Fail handler can resume a failure that the runtime raises
findings.description: effect Fail { fn fail(msg: String) } returns (), so a clause can resume(()). The checker accepts it. The interpreter raises runtime failures through this resumable operation: t.join() of a failed or cancelled task (natives.rs join), the scope end with a failed child (exec.rs raise_scope_failure), a fork with a failed branch (fork_step), a with_timeout deadline (After::Fail) and fs.read errors. It also raises the child-failure interrupt at the owner's next suspension point (check_interrupt). When the clause resumes, () becomes the value of an expression typed T. At a retried suspension point (join, scope wait, fork), the resume pushes () on the operand stack and the retried instruction reads wrong operands. Seven accepted programs (0 errors) fault: 'Add cannot apply to () and 1', 'not a tuple of that size', 'this value has no method join', and 'internal: a value reached a fork mark'. The effects model assumes that 'fail is an operation whose clause does not resume' (proofs/effects/README.md). Neither the checker nor the interpreter enforces this.
findings.suggested_fix: Type fail as -> Never (the checker rejects resume in a Fail clause), or raise runtime failures as non-resumable aborts. Deliver child failures by unwinding to the Scope/Fork frame (see IP2), not at the retried instruction. Record the decision in ADR 0005 and add the programs to crates/weft-interp/tests/programs.

findings.title: A stealable task shares an Rc with a pinned child; two workers touch it at one instant
findings.description: Task a captures nothing, so the checker marks it stealable. Its body makes an Rc and spawns child b, which captures the Rc and is pinned to a's worker at spawn time. The scheduler then steals a to another worker. Trace with seed 2: 'steal t1 w2 -> w0', 'run t1 on w0', 'run t2 on w2', both at 5 ms; seeds 2 to 8 all do this. Both tasks then change one Rc count from two workers. The design says that a shared-mutable value cannot be captured by anything that runs on another thread. The stealing rule looks only at a task's captures, not at the nonportable values that the task makes and shares with pinned tasks. A native runtime would race on the count. The interpreter cannot show the race (one thread, no race detector). This shape differs from OR7.
findings.repro: SCRATCH/r2/interp/repro/ip_steal_shares_rc.wf; harness: ipharness ip_steal_shares_rc.wf --trace --workers 4 --seed 2; run_all.sh section IP3
findings.suggested_fix: Pin a task that spawns a pinned task that captures one of its locals, or pin it while such a child lives. Add the program to tests/programs/33_stealable.wf with //~ pinned.

findings.title: A child failure goes to the handler at the owner's current suspension point (dynamic, not lexical)
findings.description: child_failed sets Interrupt::Fail on the scope owner. check_interrupt then performs fail with top_henv(), which gives the handlers of the innermost code frame at that moment. A private Fail handler of a callee (or an inner handle that does not enclose the spawn) gets the failure, resumes, and the scope returns normally with a failed child. The handler choice depends on timing: with the child failing at 5 ms the callee handler swallows it; at 15 ms the main handler gets it and aborts the scope. This contradicts the design ('Handlers are lexical') and ADR 0006 ('A failure of a task goes to the task that joins it').
findings.suggested_fix: Store the handler environment of the scope in ScopeRec. At the owner's next suspension point, unwind the frames above the Scope frame (as timeout_unwind does for Timeout), cancel the siblings, then perform fail with the scope's environment.

findings.title: A multi copy keeps the captured cells of a handler clause inside the continuation
findings.description: copy_frames (machine/effects.rs) gives fresh cells to the copied slots, temporaries and owned buffers, and it remaps closures and CodeFrame.caps. It clones Frame::Handle unchanged, so a handler that the continuation installed still has clauses that capture the template's cells. A clause that changes a local changes the template, not the copy. Later resumes then start from the changed template. Expected [1, 1]; the interpreter prints [0, 1]. The control program, with a closure in place of the clause, prints [1, 1]. This is a different defect from FD2 (the shared Clause record).
findings.suggested_fix: In copy_frames, rebuild each Frame::Handle with clause cells mapped through the copy map. Add the program to the interpreter corpus.

findings.title: A with_timeout deadline is lost when the Timeout frame is not on the task stack
findings.description: fire_timers handles a Timer::Timeout only if the Timeout frame is on the task's frames; otherwise it drops the timer silently. Case 1: the block performs an operation whose handler is outside with_timeout. The clause sleeps past the deadline, and after the resume the block runs to the end ('block finished after its deadline', v = 1). The control program times out. Case 2: the block is inside a multi continuation. The copies share the timeout id, and the first copy's return removes the timer, so the second copy finishes after the deadline. The design says that cancellation aborts at the next suspension point.
findings.suggested_fix: Record the expiry of the timeout id and check it when a resume restores the frame, or at the next suspension point. Give each multi copy its own timeout id, or keep the timer until the last copy ends. If a with_timeout block cannot hold a multi operation (ADR 0007: the block runs once), reject ip_multi_timeout.wf in the checker.

findings.title: fork returns () when every branch value is (); a generic caller faults
findings.description: fork_step returns Value::Unit if every branch result is Unit, else a tuple. The checker also types a fork of unit closure literals as () (ip_fork_unit.wf gets W0102 for let (a, b) = fork(...)). But in fn both<T>(f: fn() -> T, g: fn() -> T) -> (T, T) / par { fork(f, g) }, the checker types the result as (T, T). With T = () the interpreter returns (), and 'let (c, d) = both(...)' faults with 'this value is not a tuple of that size' in a program with 0 errors.
findings.suggested_fix: Always give a tuple of the branch results, in both the checker and the interpreter (the design writes let (a, b) = fork(...)).

findings.title: Every HTTP request task is stealable; the interpreter ignores the checker
findings.description: http_poll (machine/http.rs) adds each request task with stealable: true. The checker has no stealable fact for these tasks. A handler closure that captures an Rc (nonportable) is stolen to another worker: the trace shows 'spawn t2 from t0 on w0 (stealable)' and 'steal t2 w0 -> w3'. The program has 0 errors. This contradicts lib.rs ('steals only a task that the checker marked stealable') and the design rule that work stealing follows modes. Today only one request is in flight at a time. A runtime with several requests in flight would race on the count.
findings.suggested_fix: Pin request tasks unless the checker proves that the handler value is portable. Add W0401 for a nonportable capture in a function argument of http.serve, and give the interpreter a stealable fact for it.

findings.title: B6: sema facts break bound_before_use and ret_ok in accepted programs
findings.description: thm_w0301_no_ub needs facts_ok (with ret_ok) and bound_before_use. proofs/link/README.md says that sema gives bound_before_use 'through lexical scope', and that W0312 'probably gives' ret_ok. Both are false for accepted programs. (1) The lint unbound_use.dl finds 7 uses of a reference where it can be unbound. One is in an accepted function: tests/programs/76_ref_flow.wf loop_replaces_part, line 312. The hidden part variable of w.x has points_into and uses but no rebound_at, and the loop variable is unbound when the loop runs 0 times. (2) ret_ok.wf is accepted: pick(&w, x) mutates w.entities and returns a reference derived from x in w.entities[]. The in-form lets the arguments overlap, so W0312 does not fire, and in B1 the call kills x's group. The checker is not unsound here, because a missing rebind only adds invalid nodes. But the B6 theorem covers fewer programs than the README says, and no test checks these hypotheses (FD5 says only 'no test'). no_gen_kill does hold: gen_kill.dl finds no such node in the corpus.
findings.repro: SCRATCH/r2/interp/repro/unbound_use.dl (weft lint --rules unbound_use.dl tests/programs/76_ref_flow.wf), ret_ok.wf, gen_kill.dl; run_all.sh section IP8
findings.suggested_fix: Emit rebound_at for hidden part variables at the node that gives their first value, or list them as a gap. Correct the two README sentences. Add unbound_use.dl and gen_kill.dl as a corpus test: no lint output for each accepted function.

findings.title: The output of sim.run(seed: N) changes with --workers
findings.description: enter_sim replaces the scheduler RNG, but pick() draws from a candidate list whose length depends on the number of workers. So the interleaving inside sim.run(seed: 7) differs for --workers 1, 2 and 8. It does not change with --seed. A failing simulation seed does not replay with another worker count, which conflicts with 'a failing seed replays exactly'.
findings.suggested_fix: Let sim.run fix the worker count (for example a workers: argument with a default), or document that a replay needs the same --workers.

findings.title: The simulation is global state, not lexical: other tasks and outer clauses see its clock
findings.description: Machine.sim is one global field. While a sim.run body runs, a sibling task outside the simulation reads Clock.now() relative to the simulation start, so its clock goes back from 12 ms to 7 ms. The clause of a handler outside sim.run reads the simulated clock (5 ms) while the virtual time is 15 ms. Handlers are lexical, and sim.run should replace the root handlers only for its body.
findings.suggested_fix: Find the simulation from the nearest Sim frame of the task, and give spawned tasks the simulation of their spawn site. Or reject a task outside a simulation that runs at the same time.
