findings.title: ADR 0010 claims a simulated network; sim.net.partition changes nothing
findings.description: ADR 0010 says that sim.run replaces the 'simulated network'. sim.net.partition and sim.net.heal only write SimState.partition and a trace event. No code reads the field, and http.serve inside sim.run binds a real TCP socket. The round-1 interpreter report said this, but the ADR still makes the claim.
findings.suggested_fix: Say in ADR 0010 (and in the sim.wf comment) that Phase 1 does not simulate the network. Or make Net operations and http.serve read the partition under sim.run.

issues.finding: 6b regression: a handle takes `empty` from its body value, so a linear value from a clause leaks
issues.description: `handle` (crates/weft-sema/src/body/expr.rs, end of fn handle) starts from the body Val, `out = v`. It joins only those clause values that hold references or function values, so `Val.empty` from a body ending in `None` stays true. `assign_local` then emits `empty_at` and `live_linear` never starts. The clause value (for example `Some(lock())`) becomes the value of the handle when the clause does not resume, or when it returns after `resume`. Base reports W0601 here; head accepts the program, and the Lock is never consumed. The interpreter prints 'locked' but never 'unlocked'.
issues.repro: verify/s5/S5a/x/p/b6_handle_none2.wf (`let o = handle Op { fn op() { Some(lock()) } } in { op(); None }`); also b6_handle_none.wf and b6_handle_none3.wf (a clause that resumes and then returns `Some(lock())`). Run x/t.sh FILE: head is clean, base gives W0601, and run --unchecked prints 'locked' with no unlock.
issues.suggested_fix: In handle(), AND `empty` over every clause value that can return, or set `out.empty = false` when any clause can return a value. Add a bad case to corpus 88.

issues.finding: 6a regression: W0313 now follows new values, but abort paths are missing for several node kinds, so escapes that base caught are now accepted
issues.description: `check_local_keeps` trusts that `abort_paths` covers every node that can run an aborting clause. `note_abort_path` is called only from perform nodes, closure-summary performs and perform_at. These node kinds get no abort edge: a callee that runs a stored value (run_once(&h), a Vec of closures), a local `let g = j.f; g()`, a node that runs an inner clause that performs the outer op, and a call of a function value from an operation result. In each case the later `f = || print(1)` is treated as covering every path. On the abort path, `f` still holds `|| lg("x")`. Base flagged all of these through the sticky caps. ADR 0005 names only the stored-value case as open and does not say that W0313 depends on it.
issues.repro: x/p/l6a_stored_abort.wf, x/p/l6a_stored_abort_vec.wf, x/p/l6a_more.wf (o_clause_in_clause line 8, o_local_stored line 29), x/p/l6a_more2.wf (r_op_result line 16). Head is clean and base gives W0313. run --unchecked fails with 'no handler for Lg.lg on this task'.
issues.suggested_fix: Give an abort edge to every node that can run the clause (apply_stored nodes, clause_performs nodes, unknown fn-value calls). Until then, keep W0313 sticky for a handler that has any such node. Add these shapes to corpus 89.

issues.finding: 1a missed shapes: a task still runs fn values through a generic T, through references stored behind a reference, and through a callee result copied out of a reference
issues.description: A parameter of generic type (`x: T` or `x: &T`) given to a task never gets a PARAM mark, so the closure passes through unchecked. A `&Vec<&Job>` parameter whose task spawns `v[0].f` is missed. `s.spawn(get(j))`, where `get(j: &Job) -> fn()` copies the value out of j, is missed too. The fn_stores result does not feed `tasks`. Base and head both accept these, and each one faults at run time.
issues.repro: x/p/a1_gen.wf, a1_gen_byval.wf and a1_gen_fn.wf (`start_gen(|| note(7), |g: fn()| g())`); x/p/a1_refs.wf; x/p/a1_get.wf. Each is clean at head, and run --unchecked fails with 'no handler for Note.note on this task'.
issues.suggested_fix: Treat a type-parameter parameter (by value or behind a reference) as able to hold fn values: mark it PARAM. Follow Held places for caps. Feed the caps of fn_stores results into the task check.

issues.finding: 1b missed shapes: fn_stores ignores references stored behind references
issues.description: A callee that copies a fn value into a Job reached through `dsts: &Vec<&Job>` is missed. So is one that copies a fn value out of `srcs: &Vec<&Job>` into its result or into another argument. The same read done locally (`v.push(&j); let s = v[0]; g = s.f`) is missed too; that one is pre-existing. W0313 does not fire, and the closure escapes its handler.
issues.repro: x/p/b1_into.wf, x/p/b1_from_held.wf (p_take, and p_copy via b1h_copy.wf), x/p/b1_from_held_local.wf (p_take). Head is clean, and run fails with 'no handler for Note.note on this task'.
issues.suggested_fix: When an argument holds references, put the caps of the pointees in fn_stores sources and targets (the Held places). Locals that the stored references point to must get the caps.

issues.finding: 1c missed shape: a clause with a reference parameter keeps a fn value read through it
issues.description: In `effect RegR { fn regr(j: &Job) }`, a clause `fn regr(j) { keep = j.f; resume(()) }` with `regr(&j)` (j.f performs Note) is not W0313. op_fn_args.held does not include the pointee's fn values. The UNKNOWN_FN mark applies only to non-Fn types that has_fn finds directly, and not through `&`.
issues.repro: x/p/c1_ref_param.wf (field version also included). Head and base are clean, and run fails with 'no handler for Note.note on this task'.
issues.suggested_fix: For a reference argument of an operation, give the clause parameter the caps of what the argument points to, or mark it UNKNOWN_FN conservatively.

issues.finding: 1d unsound: the result of a caller's handler operation can point outside the parameters
issues.description: op_result_refs(None, _) returns wildcards of param_bases. A function with no parameters gets a result with no places at all. The resume value of a caller's handler can point into the handler's locals, which another caller-handler operation, the same operation again, or a callback can mutate. The callee then reads a dangling reference. ADR 0005 says 'A result from a handler of a caller can point into any place of the parameters', which is false.
issues.repro: x/p/d1_cross_op.wf (d_caller_handler: pick(), then clear(), then print(r)), x/p/d1_same_op3.wf (pick(0) then pick(1) clears v), x/p/d1_same_op.wf (d_cb: the callback clears v). Head is clean, and run prints <dangling>. The local-handler versions in the same files do get W0301.
issues.suggested_fix: Make a caller-handler result point into an opaque 'handler environment' root. Treat each perform of a caller's handler and each call of an unknown fn value as mutating that root.

issues.finding: 1d false positive: W0204 when a function returns a local-handler op result that points into a declared parameter place
issues.description: The W0204 return check runs before op_refs moves facts from the placeholder root. `fn ret_ok(u: &Vec<u64>) -> &u64 in u[] { handle Pick { fn pick() { resume(&u[0]) } } in pick() }` is rejected with "returned reference points into `operation result`: the local `operation result` ... goes out of scope". The message also shows the internal placeholder root name. Base was clean, and the program runs correctly.
issues.repro: x/p/d1_return_ok.wf (ret_ok, ret_ok_wild, ret_ok_arg): head gives 3x W0204 and base is clean. run --unchecked prints 6 6.
issues.suggested_fix: Resolve op_results before the return/W0204 checks, or check returned refs again after op_refs. Add a clean case to corpus 86.

issues.finding: 2a missed shape: a stored spawning closure read from a field and passed by value to a callee that calls it twice
issues.description: `twice(j.f)` and `let g = j.f; twice(g)` (twice calls g twice), with j.f a closure that spawns a task mutating st.count, give no W0405. `run_cb(&j, |g: fn()| { g(); g() })` is missed too. The same shape through a local closure (`twice(c)`) or `twice(v[0])` is flagged. Two tasks mutate st.count at the same time.
issues.repro: x/p/e2a_direct.wf (s_field), x/p/e2a_field2.wf (s_field_local), x/p/e2a_cb.wf. Head and base are clean, and run shows two increments per call.
issues.suggested_fix: A fn value read from a field or element should keep its spawn summary, or count as repeating, when it goes to a multi-calling parameter. Apply reach_repeats to by-value stored values.

issues.finding: 3a missed shape: a generic function in `holds` passed as a function value
issues.description: `apply(lock(), hold_fail)` with `fn apply<T>(x: T, f: fn(T) -> T / fail) -> T { f(x) }`, or `apply_lock(lock(), hold_fail)` with a concrete `fn(Lock) -> Lock / fail` parameter, gives no W0602. held_params ends the value at the move into `f(x)`, and the holds of an item taken as a value are never checked. A direct `h(lock())` with `let h = hold_fail` is flagged.
issues.repro: x/p/f3a_fnval.wf (g_apply line 12, g_apply_lock line 16), x/p/f3a_fnval_lock.wf. run fails with 'a linear value of type Lock has no on abort, so the unwinder cannot finish it'.
issues.suggested_fix: When a generic item goes to a parameter of fn type, instantiate it and check its `holds` against the type arguments, as at a direct call. Treat a move into an unknown fn value at a node that can abort as a hold.

issues.finding: Item 5 missed shape: a once closure that holds a fresh continuation goes to a callee that keeps it across a multi op
issues.description: In a clause, `let k = || resume(()); run_after_choose(k)`, where `fn run_after_choose(f: fn()) / Choice { let b = choose(); f() }`, or `hold_multi(k)` (generic), gives no W0503. The callee holds the once value across a multi suspension and calls it on each resumption. S4's closure modes cover only the same-function case. The same gap exists for affine once closures (k5_affine_closure.wf m_aff).
issues.repro: x/p/k5_variants.wf (m_callee) and x/p/k5_generic.wf (m_generic). Head and base are clean, and run fails with "a `once` continuation was resumed twice".
issues.suggested_fix: Add a signature part for fn and type-parameter parameters that are live across a multi node. The caller checks that the argument is many (W0503). Add the cases to corpus 63.

issues.finding: New false positive from abort edges: a linear owner of the body in a loop gets W0601 'overwritten'
issues.description: note_abort_path ends only the non-linear owners of the body on the abort edge. A linear body local (Tx with `on abort`) stays live past `end handle`, and the next loop pass's `let` reports 'overwritten before it is consumed'. At run time `on abort` runs (rollback), so nothing leaks. This is the retry-loop pattern. It is found in r2 oracle programs that were clean at base (p41296, p22246) and in others (p42293, p42282, p31457). This contradicts the report's claim that the only differences are the expected fixes.
issues.repro: x/p/l6a_loop_fp.wf (`for i in 0..n { handle Fail { fn fail(m) { print(m) } } in { let t = begin(); fail("x"); commit(t) } }`). Head gives W0601 x2 and base is clean. run prints 'rollback'. Also scratchpad/r2/oracle/runs/g7/p41296.wf and g5/p22246.wf.
issues.suggested_fix: On the abort edge, end the scope of linear body owners too. may_abort/W0602 already covers their unwinding.

issues.finding: New false positive from abort edges: the edge skips the scope end, so W0405 fires after the handle
issues.description: An abort edge from a node inside `scope { s => ... }` in the handled body goes straight to `end handle` and bypasses the node where the scope's tasks end. Accesses after the handle are then reported as conflicting with tasks that the abort has already cancelled. The interpreter shows the tasks never ran.
issues.repro: x/p/l6a_scope_fp.wf: head gives 4x W0405 and base is clean. run with seeds 1-5 prints 'stop 1 stop 2'. Also found in r2/oracle/runs/g7/p43194.wf, p41253.wf, p41844.wf, p43990.wf, p42123.wf, p42894.wf and g4/p10117.wf.
issues.suggested_fix: Route the abort edge through the end nodes of the enclosing scopes and handles (task end, clause-local ends), or emit task-end facts on the abort node.

issues.finding: New false positive: W0703 on a bogus `*v..` place when a slice from split_at or split_mut goes through a generic identity
issues.description: `let (l, r) = v.split_at(1); bump(id(l))` with `fn bump(es: &[u64]) / mut(es)` and `fn f(v: &Vec<u64>) / mut(v)` reports "`bump` mutates `*v..`, which the signature does not allow". v points to Vec<u64>, which holds no references, so the Held root should not exist. Base is clean. The same error shows on r2/redteam/p/x_uniq.wf.
issues.repro: x/p/held_fp3.wf (via_id) and x/p/held_fp.wf (f, h). run --unchecked runs fine.
issues.suggested_fix: Create and substitute Held places only for parameters whose pointee holds references. Check that the generic pass-through of tuple-part slices does not map to SigStep::Held.

issues.finding: Abort paths still miss clause-in-clause and local stored calls for W0601 and W0304
issues.description: These are pre-existing, but corpus 89 now claims abort paths are covered. With an outer Fail handler that does not resume, a Tx outside the body is never committed or rolled back. This happens when the failing perform is inside an inner clause (`handle Other { fn other() { fail("q"); resume(()) } } in other()`) or behind a local field call (`let g = j.f; g()`). W0304 after a stored-value abort path is missed too. Only the stored-value case is listed as open in ADR 0005.
issues.repro: x/p/l6a_lin.wf (head and base clean; run prints 'q q' with no commit or rollback), x/p/l6a_unset.wf (abort_unset_stored prints <moved>).
issues.suggested_fix: Use the same fix as the W0313 blocker: abort edges for every node that runs the clause.

issues.finding: Adjacent to 4a (pre-existing): a callee can store a reference to its own local in a reference parameter's pointee
issues.description: `fn put_local(rs: &Vec<&u64>) / mut(rs) { let w = Vec.new(); w.push(3); rs.push(&w[0]) }` is accepted, and so is the op-result version. The caller then reads a dangling reference. This is the write side of 'references stored behind a reference parameter'. ADR 0003 does not record it as open.
issues.repro: x/p/d1_store_local.wf: head and base are clean, and run prints <dangling> twice.
issues.suggested_fix: Report W0204 when a reference into a callee local (or op-result placeholder) flows into the pointee of a parameter (`lent` or `stores` into a parameter).

issues.finding: Corpus 84 from_closure_param marks a program that runs cleanly as a bad case and does not label it as a known imprecision
issues.description: `let c = |j: &Job| scope { s => s.spawn(j.f) }` with a quiet `Job { f: || print(1) }` is //~ W0314, but it is a false positive by design (UNKNOWN_FN). The corpus comment does not say so, unlike corpus 88's known-gap comment.
issues.repro: tests/programs/84_task_stores.wf:92
issues.suggested_fix: Add a 'known imprecision' comment, or make the case perform through a local handler.

issues.finding: Extern (bodiless) generic functions get no `holds`, and the dataflow does not cover them
issues.description: `extern fn hold_ext<T>(x: T) -> T / fail` called with lock() gives no W0602, and a `/ Choice` (multi) version gives no W0503. This is consistent with `drops`, which is also empty for extern generics, so it is pre-existing. Prelude generics do not hit it today.
issues.repro: x/p/f3a_extern2.wf
issues.suggested_fix: Default holds and drops of a bodiless generic with an abort or multi row to all type parameters, or document it in ADR 0007.

issues.finding: Lowering is slower with many reference-returning ops in one handle
issues.description: 1500 performs of an op that returns a reference, with a clause that can abort: head 6.5 s against base 4.3 s (debug build). It is not a blocker, but it grows faster than the 20% stated.
issues.repro: x/p/scale_ops.wf
issues.suggested_fix: Index the abort_paths and op_results facts by root instead of filtering all facts for each result.

confirmed_fixed: 1a: every corpus 84 shape and my variants with fork, Option field, tuple, nested struct, Box/Rc/Option by value, and a closure that runs the store (a1_variants*.wf, a1_rc.wf, a1_fork.wf)
1b: copy_through, take_opt, take_job, apply(copy, ...) and local-closure copy (b1_variants.wf, b1_more.wf)
1c: resume(f) echo, store via callee, wrap in closure, Vec param, clause value pair/closure (c1_variants.wf, c1_wrap_value.wf)
1d: local-handler results in Wrap, captured by a closure, and in a loop; caller-handler result returned through a signature (d1_variants.wf, d1_ret_caller.wf)
2a: recursion, two caller calls, apply with a closure, while loop, caller loop (e2a_variants.wf)
2b: captured param given to op, maker returning a struct, op with a Job argument, maker making a Job (e2b_variants.wf)
3a: user-op abort, multi through param, Option<T>, Cell/method, closure capture, tuple, second type param (f3a_variants.wf, f3a_more.wf)
3c: match, nested call, array, enum variant, method receiver, perform, inner loop, two linear, while/continue (g3c_variants.wf)
4a: put, mv, clone_refs, two-level &Vec<&Vec<&C>>, tuple, Option result, W0703/W0204 signature checks (i4a_variants.wf, i4a_sig.wf)
4b: copy before replacement, continue, stale then restore, match, closure, break (j4b_variants.wf); no soundness loss found
6a: reassigned and reassigned_in_loop are clean; nested fail, zero-trip loop, copy out, callee abort, closure call, conditional resume still give W0313 (l6a_variants.wf)
6b: None of a part, unit enum variant, join, loop, scope/block values (n6b_variants.wf); spec/rules/facts/bridge/codes/agreement_random checklist complete; agree passes
6c: W0304 now on the read line, also in a nested closure and through a callee (m6c_variants.wf)
3b: kept and documented in ADR 0007 with known-gap cases in corpus 88
S5a: verify probe.summary:
I found 2 blockers. Both are soundness regressions that S5a introduced; base rejects both programs and head accepts them. I also found 13 majors and 3 minors. Gates pass: a gate run on HEAD 963ed0f reported fmt, clippy, test and doc all OK, and I re-ran the corpus test myself (2 passed). I did not edit or commit anything in the worktree.

Blocker 1 (item 6b): the value of a `handle` keeps the `empty` flag of its body value. So `let o = handle Op { fn op() { Some(lock()) } } in { op(); None }` gets `empty_at`, and the Lock that the clause gives is never consumed.

Blocker 2 (item 6a): W0313 now follows new values of a local and trusts the abort paths to cover every node that runs an aborting clause. These node kinds get no abort edge:
- a callee that runs a stored value;
- a local `let g = j.f; g()`;
- a node that runs an inner clause which performs the outer op;
- a call of a fn value from an operation result.
A closure that performs through the handler then escapes. Base caught all of these, and the interpreter fails with 'no handler for Lg.lg'.

Missed shapes in items claimed as fixed. Each was accepted at head and failed at run time:
- 1a: generic T into a task; `&Vec<&Job>`; `spawn(get(j))`.
- 1b: fn_stores through stored references.
- 1c: a clause with a `&Job` parameter.
- 1d: a caller's handler result invalidated by another operation or a callback.
- 2a: `twice(j.f)`.
- 3a: a generic item passed as a fn value.
- 5: a once closure held across a multi op by a callee.

New false positives:
- W0204 when a function returns a local-handler op result that points into a declared parameter place. The message also shows the internal placeholder name.
- W0601 'overwritten' for a linear body local in a loop with an aborting handler.
- W0405 after a handle whose abort edge skips the end of a scope.
- W0703 on a bogus `*v..` place for `id(l)` with `split_at`.

I compared base and head on about 11,000 files: the corpus, examples, every probe outside the r2 oracle, and about 6,300 r2 oracle programs. The false-positive families above appear in real oracle programs, for example p41296 and p22246, which were clean at base. So the implementer's claim that only the expected fixes differ is wrong.

Items that held up under 3 to 9 variants each: 2b, 3c, 4a, 4b and 6c. 3b is correctly kept and documented.

All repros are in SCRATCH/verify/s5/S5a/x/p/. Run them with x/t.sh FILE, which checks with head and base and then runs head --unchecked. The comparison diffs are in x/cmp_part1.txt and x/cmp_part2.txt.

issues.finding: W0313 regression: a local outside an inner handle is checked only on paths to that handle's own end, but an abort can leave to an outer handle's end
issues.description: check_local_keeps (caps.rs) now drops the grow-only (sticky) caps for whole-local binds. It reports only when a bind reaches the inner handle's `end` node. An abort from a non-resuming clause of an OUTER handle adds an edge from the node to the outer handle's end (expr.rs handle lowering). That edge skips the inner handle's end. So the local keeps a closure that performs through the inner handler, but the reachability check never sees it. Base caught this with sticky caps. The program faults at runtime.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/diff/p/nest_abort.wf: `let f = || print(0); handle Op { fn op() { print(9) } } in { handle Log { fn log(m) { resume(()) } } in { f = || log("x"); op(); f = || print(1) } }; f()`. Head: no diagnostic. Base: W0313 at 7:9. `weft run --unchecked`: 'no handler for `Log.log` on this task'.
issues.suggested_fix: In check_local_keeps, also count a path from the bind to any abort node (an abort edge to any handle end, or a may_abort node) inside the inner body that leaves the inner handle. Or keep the bind sticky when an abort edge of an enclosing handle starts inside the inner body. Add nest_abort to corpus 89.

issues.finding: W0313 regression: abort nodes that note_abort_path does not record (a clause inside a clause, or a node found only by the stored-value pass) make the new W0313 check unsound
issues.description: note_abort_path runs at only three sites: a perform in call.rs, a closure call in fnval.rs, and perform_at. Two cases have no abort edge. (1) A node runs a clause that performs an operation whose clause does not resume. (2) apply_stored runs a stored value after the body. ADR 0005 lists case (2) as open for abort edges. But the 6a change uses abort edges to decide W0313, so both cases are now W0313 false negatives. Base reported them, because of sticky caps. Both programs fault at runtime.
issues.repro: (a) SCRATCH/verify/s5/diff/p/stored_abort.wf, fn stored_abort_same: `handle Note { fn note() { print(8) } } in { let j = Job { f: || note() }; f = || note(); run_it(&j); f = || print(1) }; f()`. Head: clean. Base: W0313. Run: 'no handler for `Note.note`'. (b) SCRATCH/verify/s5/diff/p/cic_clo.wf: the Log clause calls op(), and the Op clause does not resume. Head: clean. Base: W0313. Run: 'no handler for `Note.note`'.
issues.suggested_fix: Get the abort sources from the may_abort facts, which already cover callees, clause-in-clause and stored runs (see body_raw2.wf: W0602 fires for all of them). Or keep W0313 sticky for any local when the handle body has a may_abort node that has no recorded abort path. Add both shapes to corpus 89.

issues.finding: Abort-path fix misses a clause inside a clause: a linear value or a reference outside the body is still unchecked
issues.description: The fix adds an edge to the handle end only from nodes that run the aborting clause directly. Take an inner clause that performs an operation of an outer local handler whose clause does not resume. The node that runs the inner clause gets no abort edge. So the claimed abort_keeps_linear and abort_keeps_reference fixes miss this shape: the interpreter leaks the Tx, or prints <dangling>, and the checker accepts the program. Base also missed it, but the stage claims to fix the root cause.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/diff/p/cic_lin.wf: `let t = begin(); handle Op { fn op() { print(9) } } in { handle Log { fn log(m) { op(); resume(()) } } in { log("x"); commit(t) } }`. The checker is clean and the run prints only 9: no commit and no rollback. SCRATCH/verify/s5/diff/p/cic_ref.wf: the checker is clean and the run prints <dangling>.
issues.suggested_fix: Give an abort path to a node that runs a clause, for each local handler cap that the clause performs and whose clause can end with no resume (follow clause performs transitively). Or use may_abort nodes. Add the shape to corpus 89.

issues.finding: New W0405 false positive after a handle whose clause does not resume, around a `scope` with tasks
issues.description: The new abort edge goes from the node straight to the handle end. It does not pass the end of an enclosing `scope`, so its tasks still look active after the handle. At runtime, the unwinder cancels the scope's children and waits for them ('Tasks that must finish before unwinding goes on'). So no task is active after the handle. Fail handlers around concurrent work are a common pattern. Base accepted the program, and it runs correctly.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/diff/p/scope_fail.wf, fn guarded: `handle Fail { fn fail(m) { print(m) } } in { scope { s => s.spawn(|| st.count += 1); fail("stop") } }; st.count += 1`. Head: W0405 at 16:5 and 17:5. Base: clean (except the unrelated true positive at 5:12). The run prints 'stop', then 1. scope_abort.wf has the same result with a user effect.
issues.suggested_fix: On the abort edge, end the scopes that the body opened between the node and the handle: add the scope-join or task-end facts on `u`, as for the non-linear owners. Add a clean case to corpus 89.

issues.finding: New W0204 false positive: a function that returns the result of a local handler's operation
issues.description: op_result_refs gives the operation result a placeholder root of kind Local named 'operation result'. op_refs moves the facts onto the resumed places only at the end of the body, but finish_return checks the returned refs before that. So a valid program gets 'returned reference points into `operation result`...goes out of scope'. Base accepted the program, and it runs correctly.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/diff/p/v1d3.wf: `fn ret_pick(v: &Vec<u64>) -> &u64 in v.. { handle Pick { fn pick() { resume(&v[0]) } } in pick() }`. Head: W0204 at 3:5. Base: clean. The run prints 1.
issues.suggested_fix: Exclude the operation-result roots from the W0204 local check. Or resolve the returned refs and signature places after op_refs runs. Add a clean case to corpus 86.

issues.finding: Operation-result references given to a function parameter are lost: Summary.lent and op_args are not rebased by op_refs
issues.description: op_refs moves points_into, mutates_at, reads_at, call_mut, call_arg, lends_mut, task_reads/writes and sums[0].muts/lends. It does not move sums[0].lent (the places given to function parameters) or op_args. A body can give an op result (which points into a parameter) to a function parameter, and that parameter can mutate it. The signature then omits the place, so the caller misses W0301. The direct version without the operation is detected.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/diff/p/v1d2.wf: `fn lent_param(v: &Vec<u64>, k: fn(&Vec<u64>)) { handle PickV { fn pick_v() { resume(v) } } in { let r = pick_v(); k(r) } }`. Caller: `let first = &v[0]; lent_param(&v, |x| x.clear()); print(first)`. No W0301; the run prints <dangling>. use_direct (`k(v)`) gets W0301 at 32:5.
issues.suggested_fix: Rebase sums[0].lent (and op_args and binds) in op_refs, as muts and lends are rebased. Add the case to corpus 86.

issues.finding: 3a missed shape: a generic function item used as a function value with a linear type argument, which aborts while it holds it
issues.description: hold_generic runs only on direct item calls. A generic item with `holds`, given as a value (here to a function parameter typed fn(Lock) -> Lock / fail), gets T=Lock. A call through the parameter then aborts while it holds the Lock. Nothing checks this. ADR 0007 now says 'What stays open: no known gap'. The same gap exists for `drops` (gen_hof_drop.wf, from S4).
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/diff/p/gen_hof.wf: `fn hold_fail<T>(x: T) -> T / fail { fail("boom"); x }`, `fn via_hof(k: fn(Lock) -> Lock / fail) / fail { let m = k(lock()); unlock(m) }`, `via_hof(hold_fail)`. Head and base: clean. Run: 'a linear value of type `Lock` has no `on abort`, so the unwinder cannot finish it'.
issues.suggested_fix: Where a generic item becomes a value with inferred type arguments, check `holds` (and `drops`) against the type arguments: W0602 or W0503 if the item can abort or is multi, and W0601 for drops. Or record the gap in ADR 0007 and add a known-gap test.

issues.finding: W0304 clause-read location picks the smallest unreachable use, which can be in an unrelated closure
issues.description: diagnose.rs clause_read returns the minimum node among all uses of the variable that the entry does not reach. That includes uses inside any closure, not only inside the clause that node `n` runs. The diagnostic then points at an unrelated closure and says that a clause reads the variable there.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/diff/p/v6c.wf, fn two_reads: `let k = || print(x)` comes before a clause that reads x. The clause's W0304 is reported at 5:16 (the closure), not at line 7 (the clause read).
issues.suggested_fix: Limit the search to the nodes of the clause component that node n runs, from the clause entry node or the cap_calls/clause mapping.

issues.finding: reach_repeats counts two nodes on different branches as a repeat: a new W0405 false positive
issues.description: reach_runs.0 > 1 makes reach_repeats true when a callee runs a stored value at two nodes, also on exclusive if/else branches. A caller then gets a 'spawn again' node and W0405. ADR 0006 records 'at two nodes', and the same imprecision exists for `repeats`. But this is a new false positive for a simple pattern.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/diff/p/v2a.wf, fn branch_ok: `fn run_branch(j: &Job, c: bool) { if c { run_once(j) } else { run_once(j) } }`. Head: W0405 at 48:9. Base: clean.
issues.suggested_fix: Use path-based repetition (one node reaches another, or the node is in a loop) instead of a count of nodes. Or state the branch case explicitly in the ADR 0006 imprecision list.

issues.finding: The `handle` W0204 check compares the handle value with the results of every operation of the handler
issues.description: In expr.rs the check is `v_refs_result(&self.facts, &results, &v.refs)`, where `results` holds every op_results root for the cap. So a handle value from op A gets W0204 when the clause of op B resumes with a reference into its own local, although op_refs maps A precisely.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/diff/p/v1d4.wf: pick_local resumes &w[0] (a clause local), pick_param resumes &v[0], and the body value is pick_param(). Head: W0204. Base: clean. The run prints 2 and 1.
issues.suggested_fix: Compare only with the op_results keys whose resumed_refs contain the clause-local place.

issues.finding: retire_stale scans every cfg edge at each join: if-heavy functions now take quadratic time
issues.description: retire_stale (mod.rs) and retire_loop_stale scan all cfg_edge entries for each join that has a stale holder. insert_after and reaches_without do the same. With 8,000 sequential ifs that replace a part holder, check time is 8.98 s (head) against 1.74 s (base). At 2,000 ifs it is 0.94 s against 0.38 s. The report gives only the handle slowdown. retire_stale also adds an orphan node when no (from, to) edge is found.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/diff/p/stress_if8.wf (generated: 8,000 `if c { w.x = &a.entities[0] } else { w.x = &b.entities[0] }`).
issues.suggested_fix: Insert the stale node when the join edge is created, or keep an index from edge to position. Create the node only after the edge is found.

issues.finding: W0314 for unknown callees now also covers function values in holders: new false positives for non-spawning higher-order helpers
issues.description: call.rs runs check_task_value for each argument that holds function values (a field, a container or a pointee) when the callee is a function parameter or an unknown value. A helper such as `each(v: &Vec<Job>, k: fn(&Job)) { for j in v { k(j) } }` gets v in `tasks`. Its callers then get W0314 for closures that perform a local handler, also when no task exists. This follows the documented rule for direct function values, but extends it to a common iteration pattern.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/diff/p/fp1.wf: user() and user2() get W0314 at 10:14 and 17:15. Base: clean. The run is fine.

S5a: fix+commit.summary:
I committed 758a229 on review/s5 in /home/user/wt-core, on top of 963ed0f. Nothing was pushed. I reproduced every verifier blocker and major with the repros in scratchpad/verify/s5/S5a/x/p and scratchpad/verify/s5/diff/p, using SCRATCH/s5r/t.sh against the base binary and the interpreter. All of them are fixed, and each has a regression test with bad and clean cases in corpus 63 and 81–89. I checked every new marker against the old head binary: it misses each new bad case or reports the new control cases as errors (SCRATCH/s5r/marks.sh).

The main design change is in the abort paths. They are now built after the whole body (new crates/weft-sema/src/body/aborts.rs). Each node that can run a clause records its abort context: the eligible handlers, the values in scope, the open scopes, and the inner handlers. A node that runs an inner clause also runs the clauses of the outer local handlers that clause performs through. A resume value that holds a function value is now a stored value. The W0313 local check runs after the edges exist and counts every exit of the body.

There is a spec change: the new input relation `unwound_at`, put through all 8 steps of ADR 0002. On an abort path it finishes the values of the body, which removes the loop W0601 false positive. The abort node also joins the tasks of scopes opened in the body, which removes the W0405 false positive.

Other fixes:
- The value of a `handle` now joins the clause values: `empty` and moves.
- An op result from a caller's handler gets a "place of a caller" root, which code of a caller can change.
- Return checks run after op-result resolution.
- `lent` is rebased onto op results.
- A reference to a callee local stored behind a reference parameter is now W0204.
- Function values are followed behind references, through type parameters, generic item values and extern generics.
- Function parameters live across a multi node now count as `repeats`.
- Held roots apply only to pointees that hold references.
- Minors fixed: m1, m2, m4, m5, m6, m7, m9 and m10. m8 is documented as an imprecision, and m3 is accepted because the extra time is checker dataflow over the new abort nodes.

ADR 0003, 0005, 0006 and 0007, architecture.md and the code texts are updated, and no sentence in the diff is longer than 25 words.

All gates pass: fmt, clippy -D warnings, test (483 passed, 0 failed) and doc -D warnings. verify-all.sh was not needed. I ran about 8,200 probe and corpus files against the old head: every difference is an intended fix or a moved diagnostic. I deleted the scratch binaries, and 11 GB of disk is free.

stages.title: R2a: loops, places and wildcard rules (foundation, speed, test harness)
stages.tasks:
Context. Worktree /home/user/wt-core (branch review/s5). Start from its HEAD (758a229 = S5a). R2 = SCRATCH/r2. Reports: R2/{oracle,redteam,fidelity,quality,interp}.md. Tools: R2/triage/cmp.py FILE (compares //~ markers with `weft check --json` of /home/user/wt-core/target/release/weft; rebuild it with `cargo build --release -p weft-cli` after each change), R2/triage/verify.sh FILE (check, then each `fn x()` run alone with the stock and the oracle interpreter). Oracle interpreter: R2/oracle/weft-inst/target/release/weft (328a39b + R2/oracle/interp_oracle.patch; weft-interp has not changed since). For one at HEAD: R2/triage/build_inst.sh SCRATCH/s5/inst (delete it when done). New corpus programs: tests/programs/100_*.wf to 109_*.wf, each with a bad case and a clean case. A rule change follows the 8-step checklist of CLAUDE.md, and `weft agree` and the agreement tests must pass. Record each decision in the named ADR. Do the items in this order.

1. QA10 (minor, do first). crates/weft-check/tests/programs.rs compares BTreeSet<(line, code)>, so `//~ W0601 W0601` cannot count. Compare sorted multisets (a Vec). At HEAD these corpus lines give one code twice: 18_polymorphism.wf:21 W0702, 45_stored.wf:47 W0301, 61_task_paths.wf:63 W0314, 65_call_forms.wf:46 W0103, 72_linear_drops.wf:178 W0601, 72_linear_drops.wf:259 W0601 (already marked twice), 76_ref_flow.wf:285 W0301, 80_operand_jumps.wf:24 W0601. Mark each count (R2b item QA11 removes the W0301 duplicates later).

2. FD14 (minor). W0109, W0110 and W0113 have no test. Add bad cases (for example in tests/programs/50_items_bad.wf).

3. QA4 (major). Ctx::overlaps in crates/weft-check/src/rules.rs calls itself for each base of both sides, and so do mutation_kills and free_kills. A result of an unknown function value points into the wildcard of its argument, so `cur = step(cur)` makes `head.. .. ..`. Cost is about 2^depth. Repro: R2/quality/repro/QA4_wild_walk_4loops.wf does not finish in 60 s at HEAD; QA4_wild_walk_3loops.wf takes 1.5 s; QA4_wild_walk_gen.py K makes a straight-line walk (32 calls: 47 s). Fix: `p.. ..` is the same set as `p..`, so make FnFacts::wildcard (crates/weft-facts) return the outermost wildcard when p is already below one, and compare only the outermost bases without recursion. Expected: each repro well under 1 s. Item 4 needs this normal form, else a fixpoint loop over `cur = step(cur)` never becomes stable.

4. RR1 (blocker; QA1 is the same finding). lower_loop (crates/weft-sema/src/body/stmt.rs, MAX_LOOP_PASSES = 8, near line 841) keeps the values of the last pass when the carried values are not stable. A chain of 8 or more locals that pass a value along loses references, function values and tasks. Repros: R2/redteam/repro/RR1_loop_chain.wf, expected W0301 at line 37 (ref_chain), W0301 at 56 (fn_chain), W0405 at 87 (task_chain); 0 errors at HEAD; all three tests fault with the oracle interpreter. R2/quality/repro/QA1_loop_pass_cap.wf, expected W0301 and W0703 (QA1_control_chain7.wf, with 7 locals, gives both); 0 errors at HEAD. Decision (sound): iterate until the carried values are stable. Widen after N passes: a place that still changes becomes the wildcard of its base, a function value that still changes becomes an unknown function value, and task sets join. If a hard bound is still reached, report an internal error as W0706 does. Never keep partial values. Replace the ADR 0003 loop sentence 'After eight passes the values of the last pass stay' with the widening rule and its soundness argument.

5. QA7 (major), with the loop-state part of QA9. Each pass does `let head = self.clone()` of Lower (77 fields at HEAD), and `carried` formats a BTreeSet<String> key for each outer local twice per pass. Repro: R2/quality/repro/QA7_seq_loops_gen.py N (N = 1000: 1.3 s at HEAD, 2000: 5.7 s). Fix: put the loop-carried state in one struct that lower_loop saves and restores (so a new field cannot be forgotten), cut the fact vectors back to their saved lengths on rewind, and make the key only for the locals that the body assigns (find them once). Expected: about linear time.

6. QA8 (major). Infer::unify of two IntVars (crates/weft-sema/src/types.rs) binds the end of the old chain to the new variable, and shallow and occurs walk the whole chain. Repro: R2/quality/repro/QA8_int_chain_gen.py N (16000 untyped updates: 10.9 s; typed: 0.06 s); QA8_int_chain_8000.wf takes 2.7 s at HEAD. Fix: bind the newer variable to the older one with union by rank, compress paths, and skip occurs for a variable-to-variable bind.

7. QA3 (blocker) and the first part of QA13. lower_fn (stmt.rs, near lines 48-52) substitutes `in` places in parameter order, so a parameter whose `in` place names a later parameter with its own `in` place gets no points_into. Repros: R2/quality/repro/QA3_param_place_order.wf, expected W0301 in h (line 12) and in h2 (line 16); HEAD gives h2 only, and `weft facts ... h` has no points_into for `a`. R2/quality/repro/QA13_in_chain.wf: `weft facts QA13_in_chain.wf f` must show points_into for each of x0 to x5 (HEAD: only the last two). Fix: substitute in topological order (the W0201 cycle check has the graph). Make the test the_in_place_check_is_fast_on_a_long_chain (crates/weft-sema/src/tests.rs) assert the facts.

8. QA6 (major false positive, spec change). The wildcard rules (spec/weft.dl near lines 123-133 and rules.rs mutation_kills) give false W0301. Repro: R2/quality/repro/QA6_wildcard_self_write.wf gives W0301 at lines 17, 25 and 32; 0 are expected (with `-> Option<&Entity in v[]>` the same body is clean). (a) The rule `mutates_at(P, M), wild_at(M, B), prefix(B, Path)` must use strict_prefix: a write below B never invalidates a reference to B itself. (b) A write through a reference into `v..` invalidates that same reference, also for a scalar field through a stable step. Give each call result its own wildcard instance (a fresh split), so that a write at or below that instance through stable steps uses rule 3 for references into the same instance. A plain !prefix(Path, M) guard is not sound while two results share one interned `v..`. Keep every existing wildcard bad case. Full 8-step checklist. Record the rules and the soundness argument in ADR 0003 and update its imprecision list.

9. FD8 (minor). Spec rule r29 (`invalidated_at(R, P) :- points_into(R, Path), lends_mut(P, M), wild_at(M, B), prefix(B, Path).`) fires on no corpus program (checked at HEAD with R2/fidelity/repro/FD8_rulecov.dl: 75 of 76 rules fire, r29 never). 10. QA13, rest (minor). stages.title: R2b: closures, function values and stored references
stages.tasks:
Context. Worktree /home/user/wt-core (branch review/s5), on top of R2a. R2 = SCRATCH/r2. Reports: R2/oracle.md, R2/redteam.md, R2/fidelity.md, R2/quality.md. Tools: R2/triage/cmp.py FILE (markers against /home/user/wt-core/target/release/weft; rebuild it after each change), R2/triage/verify.sh FILE (check, then each `fn x()` alone with the stock and the oracle interpreter). Oracle interpreter: R2/oracle/weft-inst/target/release/weft, or build one at HEAD with R2/triage/build_inst.sh SCRATCH/s5/inst (delete it when done). Corpus: tests/programs/110_*.wf to 119_*.wf, bad and clean cases; interpreter programs in crates/weft-interp/tests/programs (.wf and .out). Record each decision in the named ADR. Order: items 1 and 2 first (they set the capture semantics).

1. OR2 (blocker; OR2b is its false-positive side; RR7 has the same root cause). The facts put moved_at(v) of a captured variable at the node that makes the closure. The interpreter takes the value from the cell when the closure runs, as ADR 0003 says ('it takes the value only when it runs'). A new value of v between the two points goes into the closure. Repros: R2/oracle/repro/OR2_closure_move_timing.wf (closure_form, task_form: 0 errors; stock 'a value is used after it was moved' on every seed); R2/oracle/repro/OR2b_fp_closure_never_called.wf (W0302 at `v.push(2)`, but it runs cleanly); reduced R2/oracle/fp/W0302_p1066.wf and R2/oracle/fp/W0502_p3681.wf. Decision (sound; it matches the facts and ADR 0006 for tasks): a closure that moves a captured variable takes the value when the closure is made (a by-value capture, as Rust infers). Change the interpreter: at closure creation, move each such variable into a cell of the closure. Take the set of by-value captures from sema (the captured variables with moved_at at the closure node), exported per closure span as crates/weft-interp/src/lib.rs stealable_spans does, so both sides agree by construction. Correct ADR 0003 and make ADR 0006 say the same for closures and tasks. Expected: both OR2 functions have 0 errors and run cleanly with the stock and the oracle interpreter (seeds 1 2 3 7); OR2b keeps W0302 and now faults at run time with --unchecked (a true error; use it as the bad case); the two fp/ programs become true errors too. Run every corpus and interpreter program with main or test blocks again.

2. RR7 (blocker). A closure keeps the places, summary and modes of a captured variable from where it is made, so a later new value is lost. Repro: R2/redteam/repro/RR7_late_capture.wf, expected W0301 at lines 18 (late_ref), 26 (late_ref_hof), 45 (late_fn); W0405 at 35 (late_ref_task); W0502 at 54 (late_once); W0402 at 62 (late_shared); W0406 at 71 (late_alias). 0 errors at HEAD; all 5 run tests fault. Decision (ADR 0003: a closure refers to the cells of the variables that it captures by reference): at each node where a closure runs (a call, a call that takes it, a spawn, a stored-call application), join the current places, summaries and modes of those variables into the closure. Record it in ADR 0003.

3. RR12 (minor). `let x: u64; let f = || { x = 1 }; f(); print(x)` gets W0304 twice; the same for a clause and a joined task (R2/redteam/repro/RR12_unset_closure.wf: 6 W0304; it runs and prints 1, 7, 3). Decision: keep the error (a capture reads the variable; Rust rejects the closure form too). Record the limit for locals in ADR 0007, which states it only for place fields. Add the file as a documented bad case.

4. OR1 (blocker). A call result of type fn() carries the effects of the closure but has no points_into for the places that it captured from reference arguments. Repros: R2/oracle/repro/OR1_returned_closure.wf (moved, scope_ended, cleared: 0 errors; each faults with the stock interpreter); R2/oracle/probes/a3_ret_closure_elem.wf and a6_ret_closure_scope.wf (0 errors). Expected: W0301 at `f()` in each function. Fix: a call result whose type can hold a function value points into the places of the reference arguments (the wildcard of each, as for a reference result with no stated place), and a call of it uses those places. ADR 0003 ('a call result points where the arguments can flow'). Clean case: `f()` before the move or the clear.

5. OR3 (blocker). A callee that calls a callback more than once is not checked against the references that the callback captures. Repro: R2/oracle/repro/OR3_repeated_callback.wf (via_twice, via_loop_callee, via_two_levels, via_returned: 0 errors; each faults 'a place does not exist'). `g(); g()` and a loop already give W0301. Expected: W0301 at the call that gives the closure (at `g()` for via_returned). Fix: a closure at a parameter in `repeats` runs twice in a row at the call; apply its effects for a second run after the first, so that a mutation in it invalidates the references that it captures. A returned closure that calls a captured function value more than once puts that value in its own `repeats`. Clean case: the same callees with a closure that does not clear. ADR 0006 (repeats).

6. RR2 (blocker). FnTy.summary (crates/weft-sema/src/types.rs near line 75) is one Option<usize>, so the closures that unify into one type keep only the first summary. Repro: R2/redteam/repro/RR2_one_summary.wf, expected W0301 at lines 20, 29, 37, 44, 52; W0405 at 61; W0502 at 68 (0 errors at HEAD; 6 of 7 fault with the stock interpreter, 7 of 7 with the oracle). Fix: keep a set of summaries, with joined modes (once, linear, nonportable, uniq), for a function value and for each container holder, as join_val does for if and match, not one summary in the unified type. Clean case: the same programs with the mutating closure first (already found) or alone. ADR 0005 (function values).

7. FD3 (blocker). A reference stored into an `rc` object outlives its owner. Repro: R2/fidelity/repro/FD3_rc_backchannel.wf (0 errors; stock 'a place does not exist', oracle dangling). The reference-parameter shape (FD3_known_ref_param_backchannel.wf) is W0204 since S5a (check_stored_behind). Expected: W0204 at `stash(c, &v[0])` in fill (line 12), and at a direct `c.refs.push(&v[0])`. Fix: a store into a place under an rc group root is an escape, as a store behind a reference parameter is: the stored reference must not point into a local, a by-value parameter or a temporary; follow callee stores through call_flows as check_stored_behind does. Clean case: a stored reference into the group itself. Record in ADR 0003 that the 'no stored references' assumption of the borrowing proof is now mirrored for rc groups.

8. QA11 (minor). One use gives two W0301 ('`w` used after it was invalidated' and 'the value in `w.x` ...'), and 45_stored.wf:47 shows the hidden name `{stored closure}`. Repro: R2/quality/repro/QA11_duplicate_w0301.wf (2 errors at 13:5; expected 1). Group W0301 by (use node, invalidating node), name the user variable, and put the hidden holder in a note. Update the duplicate markers that R2a added.

9. QA12 (minor). The public weft_check::diagnose::diagnose returns notes with raw `{line:N}` markers; only check_analysis resolves them (resolve_lines). Repro: R2/quality/repro/QA12_raw_note_markers.rs. Keep the node offsets in a typed field of the note, or make diagnose take the SourceFile.

stages.title: R2c: effects, continuations, on abort and drops
stages.tasks:
Context. Worktree /home/user/wt-core (branch review/s5), on top of R2b. R2 = SCRATCH/r2. Reports: R2/fidelity.md, R2/quality.md, R2/oracle.md, R2/redteam.md, R2/interp.md. Tools: R2/triage/cmp.py, R2/triage/verify.sh, oracle interpreter R2/oracle/weft-inst/target/release/weft (or R2/triage/build_inst.sh SCRATCH/s5/inst at HEAD; delete it when done). Corpus: tests/programs/120_*.wf to 129_*.wf, bad and clean cases; interpreter programs in crates/weft-interp/tests/programs. A new code needs codes.rs text and a corpus program (8-step checklist for a rule change). Record each decision in the named ADR.

1. FD1 (blocker; QA2 is the same finding). The effects of an `on abort` function are not checked. The unwinder runs it with the root handlers only. Repros: R2/fidelity/repro/FD1_onabort_perform_outer_handler.wf and FD1_onabort_perform_no_handler.wf (0 errors; stock 'no handler for `Ask.ask` on this task'); FD1_onabort_mutates_group.wf (0 errors; oracle 'access to a freed cell'); R2/quality/repro/QA2_on_abort_effects.wf (0 errors; 'no handler for `Note.note`'); new shape R2/triage/FD1_onabort_fail.wf (a `fail` in the on abort function does not reach the Fail handler around the computation; the run ends with 'failed: in undo'). Control: R2/triage/FD1_control_onabort_std.wf (an on abort function with `/ clock` prints and sleeps correctly). Decision (sound; it mirrors the effects proof assumption that on abort is atomic): an on abort function may perform only standard effects that the root handlers serve; no `fail`, no user effect, and no `mut` place (an rc group) beyond its by-value parameter. Check the inferred row after inference (program.rs check_on_aborts, next to W0118); use W0118 with a new text or a new 06xx code. Expected: an error for each of the five bad on abort functions; the control stays clean. Record in ADR 0007 and say in proofs/effects/README.md that the assumption is mirrored.

2. IP1 (blocker). A Fail clause can resume a failure that the runtime raises (join, scope end, fork, with_timeout, the child-failure interrupt, fs.read); () then stands for a value of type T. Repros: R2/interp/repro/ip_fail_resume_{join,scope,fork,timeout}.wf and ip_fail_interrupt_{join,scope_wait,fork}.wf (0 errors; each faults on every seed: '`Add` cannot apply to `()` and `1`', 'not a tuple of that size', 'no method `join`', 'internal: a value reached a fork mark'). Decision (sound; it mirrors the effects proof 'fail is an operation whose clause does not resume'): a clause of Fail.fail cannot resume. Add a sema check with a new code (W0504 is free) for a `resume`, or a closure that resumes, in a clause of `fail`. Rewrite the two controls in tests/programs/89_abort_paths.wf that resume a Fail clause (resumed_keeps_reference near line 193, resumed_consumes near 201) with a user effect. Expected: W0504 at the resume of each of the 7 repros. Record in ADR 0005 and proofs/effects/README.md. (R2d IP2 moves the delivery point of child failures.)

3. RR3 (blocker) and OR9 (blocker): a continuation leaves its clause. RR3: R2/redteam/repro/RR3_continuation_escape.wf, expected W0313 at lines 14, 19, 25 and 31 (as_handle_value); 0 errors at HEAD; all 4 tests fault 'a continuation was resumed after it was dropped'. OR9: R2/oracle/repro/OR9_resume_in_task.wf: lost_handler faults with the stock interpreter ('no handler for `Note.note` on this task'); race has a data race on c.k (oracle). Decision: the continuation is a capability of its clause. A closure that calls `resume` cannot leave the clause body (the W0313 rules with the clause as the handled computation: not as the clause value, not through a local outside the clause, not into a field, an Option or a generic holder that can keep it). It cannot run as a spawned task or a fork branch either (W0314: the rest of the handled body would run on another task). Expected: W0313 at the RR3 markers; W0314 at the spawn in both OR9 functions. Clean case: a clause that calls a resuming closure in place. ADR 0005.

4. RR5 (blocker). A resume carries the mutations of the handled body to the clause, but not its frees. Repro: R2/redteam/repro/RR5_resume_free.wf, expected W0301 at line 18; both interpreters fault. Fix: the resume node gets the frees_at (moves, owner scope ends) of the handled computation, as it gets its mutations. ADR 0005.

5. FD2 (blocker, interpreter). Nested multi continuations share one exec record: copy_frames (crates/weft-interp/src/machine/effects.rs) copies a Frame::Clause with the same continuation record, so the first copy's drop_now drops the frames that the second copy resumes. Repro: R2/fidelity/repro/FD2_multi_nested_drop.wf (0 errors; 'a continuation was resumed after it was dropped' on every seed); control FD2_control_resume_first.wf runs. Fix: give each copied Clause frame its own record (copy the nested continuation and its frames). Add the program to the interpreter programs and update the ex_multi_dropped_resume text in proofs/link/README.md.

6. IP4 (major, interpreter). copy_frames clones Frame::Handle unchanged, so the clauses of a handler inside the continuation still capture the template cells. Repro: R2/interp/repro/ip_multi_clause_caps.wf prints [0, 1]; expected [1, 1], as ip_multi_clause_caps_ctl.wf prints. Map the clause cells of each copied Frame::Handle through the copy map. Interpreter program.

7. OR4 (major false positive). W0602 and W0503 for a linear value that lives outside the handle. Repro: R2/oracle/repro/OR4_fp_outside_handle.wf: W0602 at `ask()` in inline_abort, W0503 and W0602 at `pick()` in inline_multi; all forms run cleanly; the same code in a function (call_forms) is accepted. Fix: for a perform that a local handle handles, W0602 and W0503 count only the values live inside its handled body; outer values meet the handle node, which is a suspension point only for what the outer handlers can do (rule 1 of proofs/effects). Expected: 0 errors; keep a bad case with the linear value inside the handled body. Update the W0602/W0503 rule text in ADR 0005 and ADR 0007.

8. FD4 (major). The multi rule does not count affine or !Move values; the interpreter deep-copies owned cells at each resume. Repros: R2/fidelity/repro/FD4_multi_immovable.wf and FD4_multi_affine.wf (0 errors; `weft facts ... pick` shows immovable(v0) and multi_at). Decision: a !Move value is not `many`: add immovable(V) to once_var (spec and rules.rs, 8-step), so FD4_multi_immovable.wf gets W0503. For other owned values keep the deep copy, and record it in ADR 0005 and ADR 0007 as the Phase 1 meaning of a multi resume (owned cells are copied, rc objects are shared), with the cost for a native runtime and the E5 gap. A value that the copy cannot duplicate (a Task, a Scope, an extern resource; check heap.owned_cells) is not many either.

9. RR8 (blocker). Vec.clear drops linear elements silently: the prelude `clear(self) / mut(self)` has no parameter of the element type. Repro: R2/redteam/repro/RR8_vec_clear.wf, expected W0601 at line 14 (reset) and 18 (reset_generic); the oracle reports a linear leak. Fix: give the prelude functions that drop elements the impl type parameter in `drops` (check each prelude function), so a call on a Vec of a linear type is W0601. ADR 0007.

10. OR6 (blocker). The interpreter compiles a bare place in statement position (`v` on its own line) as Read and Pop, so it moves and drops the value; sema sees no move. Repros: R2/oracle/repro/OR6_expr_statement_move.wf (use_after_drop, dangling, linear_dropped: 0 errors; each faults with the stock interpreter), R2/oracle/probes/n8_immov_expr_stmt.wf. Decision: a place in statement position (not the tail of a block) moves nothing and drops nothing; the interpreter evaluates its operands only, and sema keeps it a plain use. Expected: the three functions and the probe run cleanly with 0 errors. Record in ADR 0003. Interpreter program.

11. Message fix from the dropped RR9: W0601 for a generic item value names the type parameter ('linear value `T` is dropped', note 'T : _ (linear)' at R2/redteam/repro/RR9_generic_item_drops.wf lines 16, 19, 22). Name the item and the type argument, for example '`sink` drops a value of the linear type `Tx`'.

12. FD9 (minor). The spec input forwards(H) ('H is a root handler of sim.run') has the name of the derived forwards. Rename the input to sim_root(H) and add `forwards(H) :- sim_root(H).` (spec, rules.rs, bridge each_fact, agreement_random generator). In docs/architecture.md, draw the `s.spawn -> task_writes -> mutates_at` edge as spawn -> mutates_at, labelled sema.

13. FD10 (minor). Add one line to ADR 0005: in Phase 1 the effect rows are the capabilities, and `env` holds only handles (R2/fidelity/repro/FD10_env_capabilities.wf is accepted and runs).

14. FD13 (minor). proofs/effects/README.md names an exec effects checker in crates/weft-verified that does not exist. Name the real unlinked part: the sema suspension facts (may_abort, multi_at, clause_multi, body_multi, resumes_at) and the spec rules for W0602 and W0503.

stages.title: R2d: tasks, scopes, fork and the scheduler
stages.tasks:
Context. Worktree /home/user/wt-core (branch review/s5), on top of R2c. R2 = SCRATCH/r2. Reports: R2/oracle.md, R2/redteam.md, R2/interp.md, R2/fidelity.md. Tools: R2/triage/cmp.py, R2/triage/verify.sh. The stock interpreter has no race detector: use the oracle interpreter R2/oracle/weft-inst/target/release/weft, or build one at HEAD with R2/triage/build_inst.sh SCRATCH/s5/inst (its `stealable` marks come from the sema it is built with; delete the build when done). Trace harness: R2/interp/harness (copy it to the scratchpad s5 folder and point its Cargo.toml at the worktree crates; delete it when done). Corpus: tests/programs/130_*.wf to 139_*.wf (task markers `//~ pinned` and `//~ stealable` work); interpreter programs in crates/weft-interp/tests/programs. 8-step checklist for a rule change. Record each decision in ADR 0006 or ADR 0010.

1. OR8 (blocker). A use or a new value of a whole local is not an access for W0405: name() in crates/weft-sema/src/body/expr.rs reads only the places that a reference local points into, and a new value is only rebound_at. Repro: R2/oracle/repro/OR8_task_whole_local.wf (parent_reads, task_reads, whole_vec, ref_rebind: 0 errors; the oracle reports a race on every seed). Expected W0405 at `print(count)`, `count += 5`, `print(v)` and `r = &v[1]`. Fix: a use of a local as a value reads its root place; a new value of a local writes its root place. Keep the ADR 0006 rule that a use of a reference does not read every place that it can reach.

2. OR5 (blocker). A reference made while a task is active stays valid after the join, because the task's mutation is only at the spawn node. Repro: R2/oracle/repro/OR5_borrow_during_task.wf (use_after_join, use_after_scope: 0 errors; stock 'a place does not exist'). Expected: W0405 at the borrow `&v[1]` (an index reads the length and the buffer of v, as `v.get(1)` does; record a borrow through an index as a read of the indexed place) and W0301 at `print(r + 1)` after the join or the scope end. Fix: at each join node and scope end, apply the writes of the task again as mutations (and its frees as frees). Update the ADR 0006 sentence 'A spawn is a mutation at the spawn node'.

3. OR7 (blocker). A function parameter that runs as a task or a fork branch gets no W0401, W0403, W0405 or pinning check; the `tasks` part of a signature is used only for W0314. Repro: R2/oracle/repro/OR7_tasks_of_fn_params.wf (0 errors; oracle races in via_fork, via_spawn_twice, via_spawn_and_call; stealable_rc: 'a stealable task reaches a nonportable value (Rc)'). Expected: W0405 at the call `par(...)` in via_fork, at `bg(...)` in via_spawn_twice and at `bg_and_call(...)` in via_spawn_and_call; the spawn in bg_one is `//~ pinned`. Fix: let the `tasks` part say, for each function parameter, whether the callee can run it on another thread (a fork branch), more than once (two spawns, a loop, or also in repeats), and at the same time as which other function parameters. At the call, check each closure argument as a spawn there: W0401 and W0403 if it can run on another thread, W0405 against itself if it can run twice, and against the other function arguments that can run at the same time. A spawn of a function value that is not known to be portable (a parameter, a field, an unknown value) is pinned.

4. RR4 (blocker). A closure that captures the scope capability s can leave the scope; its task starts after the scope ended. Repro: R2/redteam/repro/RR4_scope_escape.wf, expected W0301 at lines 22 (escape), 27 (as_value), 34 (as_field); the stock run prints 'task runs, count 1' after the caller's local ended; the oracle reports a dangling reference. Fix: a capture of s points into the root of s, as a capture of &s does, so the scope end invalidates the closure.

5. IP3 (blocker). A stealable task makes an Rc and shares it with a pinned child; the scheduler steals the parent, so two workers change one Rc count at one instant. Repro: R2/interp/repro/ip_steal_shares_rc.wf (0 errors; harness --trace --workers 4 --seed 2 shows 'steal t1 w2 -> w0', then t1 and t2 run on two workers at 5 ms; seeds 2 and 3 do it at HEAD). Fix: a task whose body can spawn a pinned task that captures a local of the task is pinned (for example `pinned(T) :- spawns_in(T, U), pinned(U), captures_local_of(U, T)`, or more simply a task that can spawn a pinned task). Expected: `//~ pinned` on the outer spawn.

6. IP7 (major). http_poll (crates/weft-interp/src/machine/http.rs) makes each request task stealable, and the checker has no stealable fact for it. Repro: R2/interp/repro/ip_http_pinned.wf; harness --trace --http 127.0.0.1:18431 2 shows 'spawn t2 from t0 on w0 (stealable)' and 'steal t2 w0 -> w3' for a handler that captures an Rc. Fix: a request task is stealable only if the checker marks the handler value portable; else pin it to the worker of the server.

7. IP6 (major). fork_step returns () when every branch value is (), and sema types a fork of unit closures as (), but a generic fork is typed (T, T). Repro: R2/interp/repro/ip_fork_generic_unit.wf (0 errors; 'this value is not a tuple of that size'); ip_fork_unit.wf gets W0102. Decision: fork always gives a tuple of the branch values, in sema and in the interpreter (a unit function can still end with `fork(...)`; its tail value is discarded). Expected: both programs are accepted and run.

8. IP2 (major, interpreter). A child failure goes to the handler of the owner's current suspension point (check_interrupt uses top_henv), not to the handler of the scope. Repros: R2/interp/repro/ip_child_fail_callee_handler.wf and ip_child_fail_inner_handler.wf (after R2c their resuming Fail clauses are W0504: remove the resume; the defect stays, because the callee's or the inner Fail clause still catches the failure and the scope returns normally). Fix: keep the handler environment of the scope in ScopeRec; at the owner's next suspension point, unwind the frames above the Scope frame (this cancels the siblings), then perform fail with the scope's environment, as timeout_unwind does. Expected on every seed and timing: 'main handler: child failed' / 'outer handler: child failed', and never 'scope returned normally'. Interpreter programs.

9. IP5 (major, interpreter). fire_timers drops a Timer::Timeout when the Timeout frame is not on the task stack. Repros: R2/interp/repro/ip_timeout_lost.wf prints 'block finished after its deadline' and 'v = 1' (control ip_timeout_ctl.wf prints 'caught: timeout'); ip_multi_timeout.wf prints 'slow finished after its deadline'. Fix: record the expiry when the frame is not on the stack and check it when a resume puts the frame back (or at the task's next suspension point); give each multi copy its own timeout id, or keep the timer until the last copy ends. Expected: 'caught: timeout', 'end'; and 'fast', 'caught timeout', 'end'. Interpreter programs.

10. IP9 (minor). The order inside sim.run(seed: N) changes with --workers, because pick() draws from a list whose length depends on the worker count. Repro: R2/interp/repro/ip_sim_determinism.wf with `weft test --seed 1 --workers 1`, 2 and 8 (three orders at HEAD). Decision: sim.run uses a fixed number of simulated workers (an argument with a default) that does not depend on --workers, so a failing seed replays. ADR 0010.

11. IP10 (minor). Machine.sim is global, so a task or a clause outside the simulation sees its clock. Repros: R2/interp/repro/ip_clock_outside_sim.wf (the outside clock goes from 12ms to 7ms), ip_clause_outside_sim.wf (the clause reads 5ms at virtual time 15 ms). Fix: find the simulation from the nearest Sim frame of the task; a spawned task takes the simulation of its spawn site. ADR 0010.

12. IP11 (minor). ADR 0010 says sim.run replaces a simulated network; sim.net.partition only writes SimState.partition (natives.rs near line 330), nothing reads it, and http.serve binds a real socket. Say in ADR 0010 and in the sim.wf comment that Phase 1 does not simulate the network.

13. OR10 (minor false positive). `s.spawn(|| grow_w(&w)); w.score += 1` gets W0405 although grow_w writes only w.es (R2/oracle/repro/OR10_fp_call_reads_all.wf and R2/oracle/fp2/W0405_p40989.wf; both run cleanly). Add the cost of 'a call reads its reference arguments' to the ADR 0006 imprecisions; no code change. Pin it as a documented corpus case.

14. FD11 (minor). Record in ADR 0006 that reads from several threads need no `@ shared` (W0403 and W0405 cover writes; R2/fidelity/repro/FD11_shared_not_required.wf is accepted), and in ADR 0003 that Phase 1 has no globals as place roots.

stages.title: R2e: names, interpreter fidelity, proof claims and refactor
stages.tasks:
Context. Worktree /home/user/wt-core (branch review/s5), on top of R2d. R2 = SCRATCH/r2. Reports: R2/redteam.md, R2/quality.md, R2/oracle.md, R2/fidelity.md, R2/interp.md. Tools: R2/triage/cmp.py, R2/triage/verify.sh. Corpus: tests/programs/140_*.wf to 149_*.wf, bad and clean cases; interpreter programs in crates/weft-interp/tests/programs. Verus: PATH=/home/user/verus-lang/verus/source/target-verus/release:$PATH proofs/verify-all.sh for any proof or count change. Record each decision in the named ADR. Do QA9 last.

1. RR10 (blocker). Sema binds named arguments by name for a method call on a value receiver and for a call of a function item value; the interpreter compiles both with args in written order (compile.rs method_call and call; Op::CallMethod, Op::CallValue). Repro: R2/redteam/repro/RR10_named_args.wf (0 errors; prints -7, 7, 7, then faults 'this value has no field `hp`'). Expected: -7, -7, -7 and 'e.hp = 2, n = 5'. Fix: compile these calls with the slot logic of call_fn when the callee is known (an item value, a method of a known receiver type), or reject a named argument where it is not known. Interpreter program.

2. RR13 (minor). Named arguments to a positional constructor or to a closure bind by position, and unknown names are accepted. Repro: R2/redteam/repro/RR13_named_ctor.wf prints 8, -8, 8, 7. Decision: one rule in sema and in the interpreter: a named argument binds by name where the callee has names (functions, methods, operations, struct constructors); an unknown name is W0104; a named argument to a callee with no names (a closure value, a function parameter) is W0104. Expected: line 13 prints 8; line 14 and line 16 are errors. Record in ADR 0009.

3. RR11 (major). An effect of another module or package cannot be named: `handle` and a row item take one NAME resolved in the current module. Repros: R2/redteam/repro/RR11_module_effect.wf (W0101 at lines 11 and 15, W0805 at 12, W0702 at 15, with hints that do not compile) and the package R2/redteam/repro/RR11_pkg/ (W0101, W0805). Decision: allow a path in `handle` and in an effect row (`handle a.Note`, `/ util.Note`), resolved like a type path, with the pub rules of items (docs/grammar.md, parser, sema effect identity in effects.rs, interpreter). Fix the W0101, W0702 and W0805 hints so that they print a name that the user can write. Expected: both repros, written with the path, check with 0 errors and run. ADR 0005.

4. QA5 (major). A dependency named `main` gets the effect identities of the root (`main.Note`), so the root handler handles the dependency's effect and W0701 is lost. Repro: R2/quality/repro/QA5_dep_named_main/ (0 errors); control R2/quality/repro/QA5_control_dep/ gives W0701 for `quiet`. Decision: reject a dependency named `main` with W0107 (W0107 already forbids a dependency name that hides a root name). Check that `weft deps` and the interpreter use the same identities.

5. RR15 (minor). An operation with the name of a prelude function (sleep, print) is hidden silently: a bare call goes to the prelude function. Repro: R2/redteam/repro/RR15_op_shadowed.wf (W0702 for Clock at napper; the clause never runs). Expected: W0107 at the operation whose name a prelude function hides.

6. RR14 (minor). The interpreter checks the range of an unsigned value only where a field or a parameter gets it (exec.rs near lines 653 and 899). Repro: R2/redteam/repro/RR14_int_width.wf prints -8, -8, 260. Expected: an underflow or overflow runtime error at `a - b` (line 11), at the result of `sub(2, 10)` and at `c + 10` on u8. Check the declared integer type on each arithmetic result, or on each store to a typed local and on each return.

7. OR11 (minor). The stock interpreter is a weak oracle: dangling prints `<dangling>`, dead-local references stay readable, Vec.push never moves the buffer, linear leaks are silent, and there is no race detector. Repro: R2/oracle/repro/OR11_weak_oracle.wf (each function: stock clean, oracle fault). Port the checks of R2/oracle/interp_oracle.patch (freed-cell faults, buffer move on push, pop and clear, dead-local references, linear leaks, vector-clock races, stealable portability) into weft-interp behind an option that is off by default, with no unwrap, expect or unsafe. Turn it on in the interpreter program tests and in the runs of corpus programs with main or test blocks. It must give no false alarm on accepted programs (none at 328a39b; check corpus 80 to 149).

8. FD5 (major, docs) and IP8 (major). proofs/README.md says that the agreement tests check the sema-fact hypotheses of the link; agreement checks only the glue in rules.rs. proofs/link/README.md says that sema gives bound_before_use 'through lexical scope' and that W0312 'probably gives' ret_ok. At HEAD: the lint R2/interp/repro/unbound_use.dl fires only in functions with an expected error (tests/programs/37_fn_values.wf stored_in_loop and kept; the accepted loop_replaces_part of 76_ref_flow.wf no longer fires since S5a); R2/interp/repro/gen_kill.dl fires nowhere; R2/interp/repro/ret_ok.wf is still accepted although the call kills the group of x. Fix: correct the three sentences (the facts are tested only by the sema unit tests and the corpus diagnostics; ret_ok fails for the `in` form of ret_ok.wf; bound_before_use holds on the corpus but has no proof). design_decisions: QA4 normal form: FnFacts::wildcard(p) returns the outermost wildcard place when p is already below one. The checker keeps only the outermost wildcard base of each place. Overlap is closed under prefixes, so comparing the outermost bases is exact also for nested facts.

RR1 widening (ADR 0003): the head value of each pass is the join of the head and end values (places, function values, task sets). After 8 passes a new place below a known head place becomes the wildcard place of the deepest such place. After outer+16 passes any other new place becomes the wildcard place of its root. A function value that still changes becomes an unknown value (Summary.unknown, may_abort, row). The hard bound is 2*(outer+16)+32 passes, then W0707. Local.task/Val.task became task sets, and a join records joined_at for each task in the set.

QA7: LoopHead names every field of Lower by exhaustive destructuring in loop_head and in rewind, so a new field fails to compile until it gets a decision. Tables stay across passes. Lists are cut back to their saved length. Maps by node, task or capability are split off. FnFacts gets mark()/rewind() (also exhaustive). Locals is a newtype with no IndexMut: every change goes through get_mut or set_uniq, which keeps an undo log. Summary sets became Grow (a boxed set plus insertion order, one pointer in size) with SumMark/cut. The @uniq marks are kept as a set in Locals.

QA7 keys deviate from the literal wording: 'the locals that the body assigns' are found per pass from the undo log (the locals that the pass really changed). A static scan of the body would miss changes through calls and stores.

QA8: Infer is a union-find. Its vars table is a RefCell for path compression (the meaning of the table does not change). Var-var unions use rank, and on a tie the newer variable links to the older one. A var-var bind skips occurs. A plain Var never takes the place of an IntVar as the representative.
QA3: program::in_place_order gives the topological order and the cycles. One walk serves both the W0201 check and lower_fn.

QA6 (spec, ADR 0003): one_place(P) marks a wildcard place that stands for one place. in_one/same_one exempt a change and a reference inside one instance from the five wildcard rules, so rule 3 and the free rule apply to them. Sema makes an instance only where it is sound: the result is &T or Option<&T> and T holds no reference; the call is not in a closure or clause body (one lowering stands for many calls there); loop passes make new instance ids (the split counter), and loop keys hide the id. A caller sees a returned instance as `..`. A local that gets a second result in the same base gets the shared wildcard place, so `cur = step(cur)` stays linear. Places below an instance display as `(b..).x`.

issues.finding: QA6(a) strict_prefix makes the resume miss references held by a clause parameter (regression)
issues.description: The new wildcard rules (spec r27/r29, rules.rs mutation_kills) use strict_prefix(B, Path), so a change in `x..` no longer invalidates a reference to `x` itself. This is sound for real writes. But sema also uses `x..` to mean "something above the argument changed". `onto_param` (crates/weft-sema/src/body/expr.rs, about lines 2228-2256, called from resume_through_params) maps a change above the operation's argument place to `mutates_at(resume, x..)`, where x is the root of the clause parameter. Under the new rule, a clause parameter that the clause uses after `resume` is no longer invalid when the handled body frees what it points to. The R2 file R2/redteam/p/zz_resume_inv.wf marks this case `//~ W0301` at line 55. The base build reports it. HEAD drops it. The implementer's check of 86 repro files did not include this file. A differential run over 28,196 .wf files (corpus, examples, all of R2) found no other unintended change.
