issues.suggested_fix: Keep strict_prefix for real changes. Make onto_param encode 'a change above the argument place' (and the pos=None case) with a fact that also invalidates a reference to x itself, for example a free of x or a change of a place strictly above x. Do not use x.. for this. Add the cp1/cp3 shapes to the corpus as bad cases, and record in ADR 0003 that x.. never stands for a change above x.

issues.finding: Task handles carried by a loop: a `join` now joins every task in the handle's may-set (regression)
issues.description: RR1 changed Local/Val.task into task sets. next_carry joins the head and end sets, and `join` pushes joined_at for each task in the set (call.rs, join path). In the spec, joined_at(T, P) is a must fact (`active` stops at it). A handle that only may hold a task must not end it. When two live handles can hold instances of the same tasks (rotation or swap in a loop), `h.join()` marks the task of the other handle as finished, and races are missed. The base build reported both repros below. The sema test task_handles_that_a_loop_swaps_join_each_task asserts this unsound behaviour. The ADR 0003 sentence 'A join of the handle joins each of them' calls it sound. (The `if`/`match` union of fresh spawns is sound: only one branch spawns.)
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/r2a/t/tk1.wf (h.join(); print(st.count); h = g; g = s.spawn(|| st.count += 1) in a while loop): HEAD 0 errors, base W0405 at 13:13 and 15:25, oracle 'ORACLE data race ... with no join between' on seeds 1, 2, 3 and 7. t/tk3.wf (swap t0/t1 in the loop, then t0.join(); print(st.count); t1.join()): HEAD 0 errors, base W0405 at 17:9, oracle data race. `weft facts tk3.wf swaps` at HEAD shows joined_at(t1, n25) at t0.join().
issues.suggested_fix: Push joined_at at a join only for a task that no other live handle can hold, for example when the handle's set is a singleton or the other locals' sets do not contain it. Keep the precision of `h.join(); h = s.spawn(..)` by noting that only one instance of each spawn site is live. Add tk1/tk3 as corpus bad cases and the plain rotation as a clean case. Fix the sema test and the ADR 0003 (and ADR 0006, lines 46-47) text.

issues.finding: One-place call instances assume one lowering is one execution, but code after a `multi` operation runs once per resume
issues.description: one_result excludes closures and clauses because one lowering stands for many runs. A handled body after a `multi` perform also runs more than once, and it shares the cells of the function's locals across the runs. A local set in the first run (`last = e`) and the result of the second run then share one instance W. same_one exempts the pair from the wildcard rules, so rule 3 alone decides and the push is missed. The base build rejected this program, but only through the old self-write rule, and the base also misses the close variant mu3. So the gap in multi-shot re-execution existed before. The new soundness argument in ADR 0003 does not cover it, and HEAD now accepts a program that faults.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/r2a/t/mu1.wf: HEAD 0 errors, base W0301 at 23:17, oracle 'access to a freed cell' at 22:17. Variant t/mu3.wf: base and HEAD both give 0 errors, and the oracle faults (pre-existing).
issues.suggested_fix: In one_result, use the shared wildcard place for a call in a handled body whose handler has a multi operation (or after any multi perform). Add mu1 to the corpus. Separately, model re-runs of a handled body after a multi resume as a loop for the locals it carries (pre-existing).

issues.finding: Pre-existing (not from R2a): a reference in a tuple part is treated as an owned place when it is mutated through
issues.description: `t.0.kids.push(..)`, where t: (&Entity, &Entity), records a mutation of `t.0.kids` (a place of the local t), not of the place that t.0 points to. A reference into that place is not invalidated. The base build and HEAD both accept these programs, and the oracle faults. A tuple of task handles has the same shape: after `let (a, b) = if c { (h1, h2) } else { (h2, h1) }; a.join(); print(..)` both builds miss the race. Report this so a later stage tracks it. issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/r2a/t/x5.wf fn s3: 0 W0301 (only s1 gets one), and the oracle gives 'freed cell' at 24:5. t/x3.wf: the same in a loop, 0 errors, oracle dangling at 15:9. t/tk2.wf fn swap: no W0405 in either build, and the oracle shows a data race.

issues.finding: Kept imprecision W0312/W0405 inside one instance can be fixed soundly

Inside one instance, the steps below W decide overlap exactly, by the same argument that same_one uses for rule 3. So this is not an item that cannot be fixed without false positives. R2a: loops, places and wildcard rules (f.summary:
I checked HEAD df61532 against base 758a229 in /home/user/wt-core and changed nothing there. All gates pass. Clippy at -D warnings covers pedantic and nursery, because the workspace lints enable them. The gates were fmt --check, clippy, cargo test --workspace (499 tests) and rustdoc -D warnings. Verus did not need to run, because weft-verified and proofs are unchanged. No unwrap/expect was added to production code. `weft agree` passes on all my repros.

I built 758a229 in scratch and ran a check differential over 28,196 .wf files: the corpus, the examples and all of R2, including 27k oracle fuzz programs. There were 37 differences. All of them are intended, except R2/redteam/p/zz_resume_inv.wf:55.

Two blocker regressions, both confirmed with the oracle interpreter:
1. The strict_prefix change for wildcards (QA6a) breaks sema's resume encoding. `onto_param` writes 'a change above the argument' as a mutation of `x..`, where x is the root of the clause parameter. A clause parameter used after `resume` is therefore no longer invalidated when the handled body clears the vector. Repros: cp1.wf and cp3.wf. HEAD gives 0 errors, base gives W0301, and the oracle reports a dangling read.
2. The RR1 task sets make `join` push joined_at, a must fact, for every task that a handle may hold. When handles rotate or swap in a loop, a still-running task counts as joined. Repros: tk1.wf and tk3.wf. HEAD gives 0 errors, base gives W0405, and the oracle reports a data race. A sema unit test asserts this behaviour, and ADR 0003 calls it sound.

One major gap: one-place instances do not cover code after a `multi` perform. mu1.wf is now accepted, and it faults in the oracle. Base rejected it only through the old false positive, so the gap itself is older.

I also found a pre-existing unsoundness that R2a did not cause. A reference in a tuple part is mutated as if it were an owned place (x5.wf, x3.wf, and tk2.wf for tuples of handles).

Two minor items:
- The W0405/W0312 imprecision inside one instance is listed as kept, but it can be fixed soundly (ws1.wf).
- Some tests and docs are missing: clean cases in corpus 100, a corpus case for task handles in loops, and an update to ADR 0006.

The performance fixes (QA4, QA7, QA8), QA3, QA10, FD14, FD8 and QA13 are confirmed.

All repros are in SCRATCH/verify/s5/r2a/t/. The differential list is SCRATCH/verify/s5/r2a/diff_all.txt. I deleted the base build directory, and 9.4 GB of disk is free.

issues.finding: QA6 item 8(a) (strict_prefix): a clause parameter held across `resume` is no longer invalidated when the handled body changes a place above the argument (regression)
issues.description: `resume_through_params` (crates/weft-sema/src/body/expr.rs, `onto_param` near line 2254) encodes 'a change above the argument place, or one that can alias it' as a mutation of `x..`, where x is the clause parameter root. The resume node gets `mutates_at(resume, e..)`. The clause reference `e` points into `e` itself. Before this stage, `prefix(B, Path)` invalidated it. With the new `strict_prefix(B, Path)` it survives. So the handled body can free the referent (push, clear, assign the vector, call a mutating callee), and the clause still uses `e` after `resume`. The corpus has no such case, and the R2 red-team probe `redteam/p/zz_resume_inv.wf` lost its `//~ W0301` at line 55. The implementer's repro comparison did not include `redteam/p`. A reference strictly below the parameter (`let k = &e.kids[0]`) is still found. Pre-existing and separate: a move of the owner after the operation (moved_owner in Q3) is missed by both base and HEAD.
issues.repro: P='SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2a: loops, places and wildcard rules (foundation, speed, test harness)'; "$P/t.sh" "$P/Q2_clause_param.wf"  -> head: no errors; base (758a229): W0301 `e` at line 11; oracle: 'access to a freed cell (a dangling reference)', and the stock interpreter faults too. "$P/t.sh" "$P/Q3_clause_param_shapes.wf": push_after, callee_after, local_vec and nested_vec are rejected by base (lines 13, 24, 37, 52) and accepted by HEAD. All 5 tests fault under the oracle. Also SCRATCH/r2/redteam/p/zz_resume_inv.wf: the line 55 marker is now missing. `weft facts` shows `mutates_at(resume, e..)` and `points_into(e, e)`.
issues.suggested_fix: Model a change above or aliasing the argument place as a change that also invalidates a reference to x itself. For example, emit a free (frees_at) of the clause parameter root at the resume, or keep a non-strict rule for this encoding. Then add corpus cases with a bad and a clean form: push or clear after the op, a callee, assigning the vector, and a field-only change that stays clean. Also look for other uses of `x..` that mean 'overlaps x'.

issues.finding: RR1 task sets: a `join` of a handle that can hold several tasks records joined_at for every task in the set, but at run time it joins only one (unsound; partly a regression)
issues.description: Local.task/Val.task became task sets. `join` (call.rs near line 2236) pushes joined_at for each task in the set. The if/else join of values (fnval.rs:335) and the loop carry union the sets. ADR 0003 now states the rule: 'A `join` of the handle joins each of them.' At run time a handle holds one task. The other task stays active, so an access after the first join races with it. Base kept one task (`a.task.or(b.task)`), so base rejected swap_b; HEAD accepts it. The sema test task_handles_that_a_loop_swaps_join_each_task passes only because it has no access between the two joins.
issues.repro: P='SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2a: loops, places and wildcard rules (foundation, speed, test harness)'; "$P/t.sh" "$P/T2_join_swap.wf" '1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8' -> head: no errors; base: W0405 at line 20 (swap_b); oracle on every seed: 'ORACLE data race: task 0 reads cell 0 ... task 1 wrote path [0] with no join between' for swap_a and swap_b. `weft facts T2_join_swap.wf swap_b`: HEAD has joined_at(t0, n24) and joined_at(t1, n24); base has joined_at(t1, n24) only. "$P/t.sh" "$P/T4_loop_swap_access.wf" (the sema test's loop plus `print(st.count)` between the joins) and "$P/t.sh" "$P/T3_loop_handles.wf" (a 2-local handle chain, `h0.join()` then an access): both are accepted, and the oracle reports a race.
issues.suggested_fix: Keep the task set for spawn and active state. Count a join as joined_at only when the handle's set is a single task (a must-join). Otherwise leave the tasks active until a definite join or the end of the scope. Fix the ADR 0003 sentence. Add a corpus case with an access between two joins of swapped handles.

issues.finding: RR1 widening adds new false W0301 to common walk-then-write code (linked list tail, BST lookup)
issues.description: Any loop such as `while .. { cur = &cur.next[0] }` never becomes stable on concrete places, so after 8 passes `cur` gets the wildcard place `q..`. Then a write through `cur` (`cur.val = x`, `cur.hits += 1`) is a change in `q..`. The wildcard rules then invalidate `cur` itself: rule 2, because the Path `q..` and M overlaps q. Base had no error on these programs. This is the same false-positive class that QA6 fixes for call results, now created by the widening for the most common list and tree pattern. The ADR imprecision list mentions it only in general terms. Corpus 100 deep_walk_clean only reads, so it does not show this.
issues.repro: P='SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2a: loops, places and wildcard rules (foundation, speed, test harness)'; "$P/t.sh" "$P/R1_walk_then_write.wf" -> head: W0301 at lines 11 (set_last) and 17 (bump_all); base: none on those lines; both report line 27 (append). Oracle and stock: clean. "$P/t.sh" "$P/R2_bst.wf" -> head: W0301 `cur` at line 19; base: clean; oracle: clean.
issues.suggested_fix: Widen a walked reference so that a write through the same reference keeps it valid. For example, use a one-place instance for the widened place of one local (the walk value is one place per iteration), or exempt a change made through the same holder. Add the walk-then-write programs to corpus 100 as clean cases.

issues.finding: Loop lowering grows exponentially with branching or nested deep walks: widening only after 8 passes lets the place sets multiply (QA4/QA7 shape not covered)
issues.description: Until pass 8 the carried place set is exact. With k branches that each deepen, it reaches about k^8 places. With nested loops, each outer pass multiplies the set by the size of the inner loop's result. The time goes to sema lower_loop (gdb shows nested lower_loop frames), and memory grows about 10 MB/s. Base also hangs, so this is pre-existing. But RR1/QA4/QA7 promised stable, fast loop lowering ('each repro well under 1 s', 'about linear'), and these are natural programs: a ternary search tree walk, and nested loops over a tree. The hard bound does not help, because each pass is already huge.
issues.repro: P='SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2a: loops, places and wildcard rules (foundation, speed, test harness)'; VS=SCRATCH/verify/s5. timeout 60 $VS/r2a_weft_head check "$P/L8g.wf" (one loop with a 3-way branch: `x = &x.a[0]` / `&x.b[0]` / `&x.c[0]`) -> killed at 60 s, base also > 60 s. timeout 300 $VS/r2a_weft_head check "$P/L8d.wf" (2 nested loops: inner `a = &a.next[0]`, outer `a = &a.kids[0]`) -> rc=124 after 300 s with RSS > 1.2 GB; base > 50 s. L8a.wf (3 nested) > 60 s on both. The 2-way BST walk R2_bst.wf takes 2.4 s on HEAD.
issues.suggested_fix: Widen by place shape before the set explodes. For example, cap the number of places of one value (or of new places below one base) and replace them by the wildcard place of their common base. Or widen at once when a pass adds a place below a place that the same pass added. Add scale tests for k-way branching walks and nested walks.

issues.finding: Widened unknown function values add new false W0301 for benign closure chains

issues.suggested_fix: Make the widened value keep the union of the known summaries without the unknown lend, when every joined value is a known closure. Or document the case in the corpus as a known imprecision.

issues.finding: Sema is about 2x slower than base on deep straight-line walks (point_local walks to the root)
issues.description: point_local now calls one_place_of(p) and two_results, and each walks the whole path of the place for every point. On deep places this doubles the existing super-linear cost. gdb samples show point_local as the hot frame. Pre-existing cubic growth; the 2x factor is new.

R2a: loops, places and wildcard rules (f.summary:
I compared HEAD df61532 with base 758a229 (built from git archive) and used the R2 oracle interpreter. Check output is byte-identical to base on all 91 corpus files, the examples, the packages, the interp/syntax test programs, 11 doc snippets and 26,400 oracle fuzz programs. The output changes on 34 targeted R2 files. Gates pass in my own run: fmt, clippy, 499 tests and rustdoc. QA10, FD14, QA3, QA7, QA8 and QA13 hold. QA4 and the reference and function-value parts of RR1 hold under the probe variants.

I found two blockers.
(1) The QA6 strict_prefix change breaks the resume encoding. onto_param maps a change above a clause argument to `x..`, so a clause parameter held across `resume` is no longer invalidated when the handled body pushes to, clears or replaces the container. Four shapes are now accepted and fault under the oracle. Base rejected them, and the R2 probe redteam/p/zz_resume_inv.wf lost its marker at line 55.
(2) RR1 task sets: a join of a handle that can hold several tasks marks every task joined. This is unsound: the oracle reports data races on T2, T3 and T4. T2/swap_b is a direct regression from base, and the ADR now states the unsound rule.

Majors:
- The widened `q..` place gives new false W0301 on common walk-then-write code (list tail, BST lookup). Base had none.
- The lowering of loops with branching or nested deep walks grows exponentially before the widening at pass 8. A 3-way tree walk takes more than 60 s, and 2 nested walks take more than 300 s with over 1.2 GB. This is pre-existing in base.

Minors: false positives from widened closure chains, about 2x slower sema on deep straight-line walks, a corpus 103 bad case that does not isolate r29, and a remaining `in v..` parameter false positive.

Probes and the helper t.sh are in 'SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2a: loops, places and wildcard rules (foundation, speed, test harness)/'. The binaries are SCRATCH/verify/s5/r2a_weft_head and SCRATCH/verify/s5/r2a_weft_base. I deleted the base build dir, and 9.6 GB is free.

resolved: BLOCKER (both reports) QA6(a) strict_prefix broke resume of clause parameters: onto_param now returns (place, frees). A change above the argument place that would invalidate a reference to it in the caller, or any change when the op runs in a callee (pos None), adds the new input releases_at(resume, x), and the spec adds frees_at(P,M) :- releases_at(P,M). Moves of locals from outside the handle in the handled body also free at each resume (ContInfo.frees / Handled.frees), which also fixes the pre-existing moved_owner case and R2 RR5. Q2, all 5 shapes of Q3, cp1, cp3, zz_resume_inv:55 and RR5:18 are now reported; field_only, other_place and kids_only stay clean. 8-step checklist done: spec, rules.rs (Cause::Release), Facts field, bridge, diagnose, codes text, corpus 104_resume_frees.wf, agreement generator. ADR 0005 records that x.. never stands for a change above x.

BLOCKER (both reports) a join of a handle that can hold several tasks joined all of them: join() now pushes joined_at(t) only if no other local can hold t. Task sets are path-sensitive (Locals.tasked plus BranchState.tasks, joined at merges), a whole move or a join empties the local's set, and the loop carry unions head, end and continue sets. T2, T3, T4, tk1, tk3 and tk2 (tuple swap) are reported; one_handle, either and moved_handle stay clean. The sema test that asserted the unsound join is replaced by a_join_ends_a_task_only_if_no_other_handle_can_hold_it. Corpus 106_task_join_sets.wf; ADR 0003 and ADR 0006 updated.

MAJOR walk-then-write false W0301 (R1, R2_bst): new input writes_via(P, R) means a mutation through R at or below its place does not invalidate R (rule 4). The mutation rules (rule 3 and both wildcard mutation rules) get !writes_via(P,R). Sema emits it for assignments whose target base is a local holding one reference, and for method calls on a part of it, checked at the end of the body (the method states no effect, runs no function value, mutates only self, and has no performs or rebinding). R1 lines 11 and 17 and R2_bst are clean. The pre-existing R1 append FP (line 27) and Q7 are also fixed. Corpus 105_walk_writes.wf has 6 clean and 4 bad cases; there are 2 checker unit tests.

MAJOR exponential loop lowering (L8a-L8g, branching and nested walks): a place that goes deeper a second time widens at once to the wildcard of the outermost place that an earlier pass added. Places below a shared wildcard collapse to it, in the carry and in point_local. A value with more than 16 places in one root at a loop head (64 for any local) collapses to the wildcard of the common prefix. Loop keys are memoized (key_of). All L8 repros now take under 0.03 s (HEAD-R2a ran past 60 or 300 s); 2-nested 16-way and 6-deep nests take 0.01 s. Sema tests a_reference_that_goes_deeper_becomes_a_wildcard_place (3 passes) and a_walk_in_branches_and_nested_loops_stays_small.

MAJOR one-place instances and multi re-runs (mu1): one_result makes no instance where code can run again (local multi handler, multi effects in the row, unknown multi call, passthrough) or in a loop body. The x3 tuple rotation showed that carried instances alias across iterations. A handled body of a multi handler whose clauses can resume more than once (syntactic check) is lowered with lower_loop, with a back path from its end through a 'resume again' node to the successors of each clause-running node. Locals of the body are rebound with empty_at, which matches the interpreter's frame copy. mu1, mu2 and mu3 are now reported (the pre-existing mu3 too), b6_vec_multi stays clean, and the oracle confirms outer_local faults and inner_local is clean. Corpus 102 and 104, sema test a_call_result_in_a_loop_is_not_one_place, ADR 0003 and ADR 0005.

MAJOR (pre-existing) references held in tuple parts or elements: field_of and Index now dereference a reference that a part holds, through held_refs (deref_lval). x5 (s1, s2, s3), x3 and element/index cases are reported; corpus 107_held_refs.wf has 4 bad and 3 clean cases.
MINOR benign closure chain FP (R4): function values widen to unknown only after the root threshold (outer+16 passes), so known chains stay known. Clean partner fn_chain_clean is in corpus 100.
MINOR sema slowdown on deep straight walks: PlaceInfo now caches wild_base and the outermost one-place ancestor (O(1) one_place_of and wild_base). With the per-root place cap, dl800 takes 0.02 s.
MINOR FD8: corpus 103 has lend_param_wild, a case that only rule r29 catches (verified with explain).

MINOR Q7 param `in v..` self-write FP: fixed by writes_via for assignments and receiver-only method calls. ADR 0003 states the remaining imprecision (writes through another reference, or through a part).

MINOR W0312/W0405 inside one instance: overlaps now compares raw steps when same_one(P,Q) (spec, with a !same_one guard on the wildcard overlap rules, and the checker). This is sound now because instances exist only in code that runs once. ws1 is clean; split_fields is clean and same_field is bad in corpus 102. ADR 0003 updated.

MINOR test and doc gaps: corpus 100 has clean partners fn_chain_clean, clear_one_clean and task_chain_clean. Task-handle loop cases are in 106. ADR 0006 join text is fixed. The before/after comparison ran over all 28,135 files (corpus plus all R2 p, repro, oracle and fuzz files).

not_resolved.issue: A multi operation of a handler of a CALLER can re-run the rest of a function body with locals from the run before (pre-existing, also in base)
not_resolved.reason: The fix models re-runs only for local handlers (handled body lowered as a loop). For a caller's handler the whole function body after the operation would need the same treatment. A call result there is no longer one place (may_run_again), but references held by locals across such re-runs are not followed. This is recorded as open in ADR 0005.

not_resolved.issue: Remaining imprecision from the new sound models
not_resolved.reason: This is accepted as sound-over-precise and documented in ADR 0003 and ADR 0005. A write through a tuple part counts for all the parts' referents, because held_refs does not tell parts apart. The multi re-run model is path-insensitive: oracle fuzz p10871 (clean before) now gets a W0302 when run 1 and run 2 take different branches. In programs that are already rejected, the re-run adds a duplicate W0601 'overwritten' at the handle line for a linear value that is already unconsumed. No corpus or design example got a false positive.

R2a: loops, places and wildcard rules (f.summary:
I fixed all the verifier findings except one open, pre-existing case (a `multi` handler of a caller re-running the function body). Everything is in one commit, 57cce5f, on review/s5. All gates passed on the final tree: fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --workspace (also the 2 MiB stack limits test) and rustdoc -D warnings. Random agreement passed with 20,000 cases. Verus did not run because I did not touch weft-verified or proofs.

Checklist work: two new input relations. `releases_at(P,M)` makes `frees_at` hold when a resume follows a change above a clause parameter, or a move in the handled body. `writes_via(P,R)` means a mutation through R does not invalidate R; it guards rule 3 and both wildcard mutation rules. Overlap inside one instance is now exact (a `!same_one` guard on the wildcard overlap rules). The 8-step checklist is done for these. `corpus_exercises_every_rule` still passes.

Sema changes:
- Join only tasks that no other handle can hold, with path-sensitive task sets.
- Faster loop widening (second deepening, collapse below wildcards, caps of 16 and 64 places per root) and memoized loop keys.
- Function values widen only at the root threshold.
- No one-place instances in loops or in code that can re-run.
- Handled bodies of multi handlers are lowered as loops, with a back path that rebinds the body's own locals.
- References held in tuple parts and elements are dereferenced.
- PlaceInfo caches wild_base and the one-place ancestor.

New corpus: 104_resume_frees, 105_walk_writes, 106_task_join_sets, 107_held_refs, plus additions to 100, 102 and 103. ADR 0003, 0005 and 0006 and architecture.md are updated.

Comparison with the R2a head binary over all 28,135 files (corpus plus every R2 directory): 20 differences.
- 5 are the new or changed corpus files, all intended.
- zz_resume_inv lines 42 and 55, and RR5 line 18, are true errors that are now found.
- 1 previously clean fuzz program (p10871) gets a conservative W0302 from the re-run model.
- 12 are programs that were already rejected. They get duplicate W0601s or W0302s, or the first reported use moves to another line.
- p1114 is ill-typed.

The scratch dir s5 is deleted. 9.5 GB of disk is free.

Sema records the by-value captures (the non-copy moved captures) in FnFacts::by_value. weft_interp::by_value_captures exports them keyed by (unit, span); the interpreter Op::MakeClosure{owned} moves each of them into a cell of the closure. Before the fix, the stock interpreter faulted on closure_form and task_form on every seed. Now both have 0 errors and run clean with the stock and oracle interpreters on seeds 1 2 3 7. OR2b keeps W0302 and now faults in both interpreters ('a value is used after it was moved'). fp/W0502_p3681 now faults (true W0502). W0302_p1066 faults with `if true`; the original uses `if false`, so it is a rejection on a path that does not run. Tests: corpus tests/programs/110_capture_by_value.wf (bad and clean); interpreter program capture_by_value.wf/.out; guards.rs a_closure_takes_a_moved_capture_when_it_is_made. Every corpus and interpreter program with main or test blocks was run again with both interpreters: only the 5 programs that fail by design fail.
findings.notes: ADR 0003 is corrected and ADR 0006/0010 say the same. A closure that took a value still cannot leave the scope of the variable (W0204/W0301, kept as before, recorded as conservative), because fn() cannot carry once/linear across a signature. Follow-up from an oracle-program scan: the other captures are now used after the move node (a capture that points into the moved value is W0301), and clause captures no longer make a closure-local variable a capture.

findings.evidence: Commit 540480c, new crates/weft-sema/src/body/late.rs. Each closure keeps its by-reference capture values (CapValue). apply_summary (direct call, higher-order call, spawn, stored application) runs late_join. For a capture with new places it adds a use and the rebased mutations, reads, lends and op args. For a new function value it applies that value with the places that the closure gave it (Summary::cap_runs). It reports W0406 for uniq_needs. closure_once_now gives W0502. A task joins the end-of-body values (finish_task_values). Result: the RR7 repro has every expected code at lines 18/26/35/45/54/62/71. The only extra is a true W0703 at 62, which the direct write form also gets. All 5 RR7 run tests fault with both interpreters. Corpus 111_late_capture.wf has the bad cases and clean cases, and a main that runs the clean cases.
