findings.evidence: The RR12 repro still gives 6 W0304 and runs, printing 1, 7, 3. Added tests/programs/112_unset_capture.wf as a documented bad case (6 markers) with a clean case and a main. ADR 0007 records the limit for locals in the place-field rule and in its consequences (commit 540480c).
findings.notes: Decision kept: a capture reads the variable, and Rust also rejects the closure form.

findings.evidence: Commit 7cf339b. New inferred signature part EffectSig::ret_refs holds the parameter places that function values in the result point into. Callers substitute it. Function arguments flow into the result. A function with no body, or an unknown value, gives the wildcard of each reference argument. The OR1 repro: moved and cleared get W0301 at f(). scope_ended gets W0301 at the block value, which is the established diagnostic shape for a block value held across its end. a3 gets W0301 at f(); a6 gets W0301 at the block value. Corpus 113_returned_closures.wf has the bad cases and clean cases: call before the move or clear, a value argument, and push (precise, no wildcard false positive). A main runs the clean cases.
findings.notes: I chose precise inferred places over a plain wildcard. The wildcard gave false positives in corpus 83_kept_values (getters that copy a stored fn out of &Job). Copies out of reference arguments stay covered by the stored-value mechanism. Recorded in ADR 0003 and architecture.md.

findings.evidence: Commit d4d0d7d. A call whose callee repeats an argument (callee_repeats, an op clause, or a value with repeat_runs) now gets a 'call again' node that uses the argument again (run_again). A call of a parameter inside a closure counts where the closure runs (Summary::param_calls). Only-returned closures are excluded and put into RetFn::repeats, so a call of the returned value runs again. The OR3 repro now has W0301 at twice(...), each(...), twice2(...) and at g() for via_returned (not at wrap(...)). Corpus 114_repeated_callbacks.wf has 5 bad cases and clean cases (closures that do not clear, push only, a once callee). 46_value_args:54 and 48_lend_alias:17 gained true W0301 (the callee can change the place and then run the closure); their markers were updated with comments.
findings.notes: Recorded in ADR 0006 (repeats bullet and consequences).

findings.evidence: Commit 7468e09. Lower::unify joins function values when a bound function type variable meets another function value (join_fn, with joined modes, through the summary). Infer::unify now links an unbound variable to a bound variable instead of copying its type, and Infer::rebind_fn updates it. Element and field types keep their type variables. Written function types (fn() with no summary) stay unknown (stored values). The RR2 repro has all W0301 (20/29/37/44/52) and W0405 (61). once_second gets W0502 at the second g() call (line 71), not at the push (68); this is semantically right because the push of an inferred-type closure is not a copy. The modes join was checked with probes: linear (W0601) and nonportable (W0401) through containers. Corpus 115_joined_fn_values.wf has bad cases, mutating-first cases and clean cases, with a main. Unit test in types.rs: a_variable_links_to_a_bound_function_type.
findings.notes: Recorded in ADR 0005.

findings.evidence: Commit 4414f4d. A store under an rc group root is now an escape: stored_behind takes Behind::Group, and call_flows treats group roots as behind. Callees infer EffectSig::group_stores (the parameters whose references they put into an rc type), and the caller checks the argument flow (group_stores_of). A foreign fn that mutates a group puts all its arguments there. The FD3 repro now gets W0204 at stash(c, &v[0]) at line 12. Corpus 116_rc_stores.wf has W0204 for the callee, direct push, via a reference parameter, a by-value parameter and two levels. Clean cases: a reference into the group itself, and a callee that changes the object but keeps no reference. A main runs them. The known reference-parameter shape keeps its W0204.
findings.notes: ADR 0003 records that the borrowing proof's 'no stored references' assumption is now mirrored for rc groups. architecture.md lists the new signature part.

findings.evidence: Commit 3e76e99. W0301 entries with the same invalidating node and nested use spans are now one error. It names a program variable, and an 'also ...' note names each hidden holder. Variables with names of the lowering show descriptions ('the closure', 'the stored closure', 'the loop iterator') in all diagnostics. The QA11 repro now gives 1 error with the note 'also the value in `w.x` : &Entity in b.entities[]'. The duplicate markers were updated: 45_stored.wf:47 and 76_ref_flow.wf:285 are now a single W0301. No corpus output contains a braced name. Tests: diagnostics.rs w0301_is_reported_once_for_each_use_and_mutation, and the updated body_texts a_part_holder_is_named_by_its_part.

Commit 3e76e99. The public weft_check::diagnose::diagnose now takes the SourceFile and returns resolved line numbers. The raw variant (diagnose_marked) and resolve_lines are pub(crate). Markers use a private sentinel character ('\u{1}line:N\u{1}'), so no source text can look like a marker. Test: diagnostics.rs the_public_diagnose_resolves_line_numbers checks for 'used at line 4', 'and 1 more use, at line 5', and no marker text.

design_decisions: OR2: a closure that moves a capture takes it by value when it is made. The set comes from sema (FnFacts::by_value), keyed by (unit, span), and the interpreter consumes it, so both sides agree by construction. Such a closure still cannot leave the scope of the variable (kept W0204/W0301, conservative), because a fn() type cannot state once or linear across a signature.

RR7: late values are joined at run nodes by rebasing the places of the closure from old capture places onto new ones (over-approximate), by applying new function values with the recorded inner givens, and by rechecking uniq demands. Tasks get the end-of-body values at their spawn node.

OR1: I used precise inferred ret_refs (callee places substituted at the caller) instead of a plain wildcard for callees with a body. The wildcard caused false positives in corpus 83 for function values copied out of reference arguments. The wildcard is used only with no body and for unknown values.

OR3: a repeating call gets a 'call again' node that only uses the argument again; it does not apply its effects a second time, to avoid duplicate W0703/W0402. A function's own repeats does not count calls in closures that it only returns; those go into RetFn::repeats.

RR2: function values join at type-variable level during unification, and unbound variables link to bound variables. Written fn() types are not joined: they stay values that the body does not know and use stored-value application.
FD3: a new group_stores signature part keeps the rc check precise. A callee that mutates an rc type but stores no reference argument does not cause W0204 at its caller.
QA11: grouping key is (invalidating node, nested use spans) so that a call and its argument merge (45_stored.wf:47). Names of the lowering show as descriptions in every diagnostic.
QA12: diagnose takes the SourceFile, and markers use a private control-character sentinel.
R2b: closures, function values and store.summary:
I fixed all 9 R2b items in /home/user/wt-core (branch review/s5) as 9 commits, from base 57cce5f to b66e040. Before each commit, fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --workspace and the rustdoc -D warnings build passed. I did not touch weft-verified or the proofs, so verify-all.sh was not needed. There are new corpus files tests/programs/110-116, each with bad and clean cases; 111 and 113-116 get mains that run their clean cases, and 110 and 112 have mains that run as well. There is also an interpreter program capture_by_value.wf/.out. ADRs 0003, 0005, 0006, 0007 and 0010 and architecture.md are updated.

Verification beyond the gates:
(1) Every corpus and interpreter program with main or tests was run on seeds 1 2 3 7 with the stock interpreter and with an oracle interpreter rebuilt from the working tree. Only the 5 programs that fail by design fail.
(2) I re-checked the 8,521 oracle programs that 328a39b accepts, and compared the base binary (57cce5f) with HEAD. 68 are newly rejected; 35 of them fault at run time. The 33 that run clean are block values that dangle (the existing rule), W0312 that matches the existing rule for the equivalent local-closure form, a W0301 for a move of an `Rc` handle under the existing rule, and errors on `if false` paths. One real false positive (closure-local captures leaking through clauses, which the new repeat node exposed) was found and fixed in 2864226. That scan also found a by-value soundness gap: a capture that points into a value that the closure takes. It is fixed in the same commit.
(3) Every program that is still accepted runs without faults, except the OR8 whole-local races (not in this stage) and designed failing tests.

Scratch build dirs were deleted. Known limits are recorded in the ADRs: by-value closures still cannot leave the variable scope, the late-join rebasing over-approximates, and repeat nodes also count callee changes."

issues.finding: RR7
issues.description: The late join misses two shapes. (a) It does not follow a captured closure. `late_join` and `late_once` look only at the `cap_values` of the closure that runs. So when f captures g, g captures r, and r gets a new value, nothing is joined: g's value did not change. The direct call, the HOF call, three levels, spawn and once forms all slip. (b) It does not see a new value of a part of a captured local. After `t.0 = &world.entities[0]`, the new value is in a hidden part holder, so `locals[t].refs` does not change and `late_changes` sees no change. The same holds with run(f). Both are missed shapes of the RR7 root cause. They slip at base too.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2b: closures, function values and stored references/V_RR7_nested_and_part.wf: 0 errors at HEAD. With `weft test --unchecked`, all 5 tests fail on seeds 1 2 3 7 with the stock and the oracle interpreter: nested_late, nested_fn_late and nested_task (dangling), nested_once ('used after it was moved') and tuple_part_late (dangling). Expected: W0301 at f() (nested_late), W0301 at print(first.hp) (nested_fn_late), W0405 at clear (nested_task), W0502 at the second j() (nested_once), W0301 at f() (tuple_part_late). More forms are in rr7_nested.wf in the same folder: nested_hof, nested_three and tuple_part_hof.
issues.suggested_fix: In late_join and late_once, for each captured function variable that the closure runs (`Summary::cap_runs`), also run late_join on the summaries of the variable's current value, with the places that the closure gives it. Do this recursively, with late_stack as the cycle guard. Count the hidden part holders of a captured local (the `w.x` holders) as part of its CapValue, so that a new value of a part is a change. Add both shapes to 111_late_capture.wf.

issues.finding: OR1
issues.description: A returned closure whose captured reference variable gets a new value before the return keeps its creation-time places in the inferred `ret_refs`. In mk_late, `let r = d; let f = || print(r.hp); r = &world.entities[0]; f`: the caller sees only d's places. So clearing world.entities and then calling f() is accepted. This is the OR1 x RR7 combination. A function value that is captured cannot escape (W0204), so references are the open hole.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2b: closures, function values and stored references/V_OR1_more.wf test ret_late: 0 errors. It faults on seeds 1 2 3 7 (stock: 'a place does not exist'; oracle: dangling). Expected: W0301 at f(). The control case ret_early in rr7_ret2.wf (reference taken before the closure) gets W0301.
issues.suggested_fix: At the return node (and for a block value), join the current values of the by-reference captures into the returned closure's places before you compute ret_refs or points_into, as late_ret_refs does for a closure call result.

issues.finding: OR1
issues.description: A call result whose type holds a function value inside a container gets no points_into for the places that the closure captured from reference arguments. Two such result types are `-> Vec<fn()>` and `-> (Vec<fn()>, u64)`. Fix 7cf339b handles fn(), tuples with fn, Option<fn()>, structs and generic structs, but not a Vec of function values. A related channel slips too: a callee that pushes a closure which captures a reference argument into a reference parameter (`fn out(v: &Vec<u64>, o: &Vec<fn()>) / mut(o) { o.push(|| print(v.len())) }`). The caller's fs then does not point into v. This also slips at base.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2b: closures, function values and stored references/V_OR1_more.wf tests via_vec, via_tupvec and via_out_param: 0 errors. Each faults with 'a value is used after it was moved' (stock and oracle) on all seeds. Expected: W0301 at the call of the copied-out function value.
issues.suggested_fix: Use the same 'can hold a function value' predicate for ret_refs and the wildcard fallback as for the modes of a call result, recursing through Vec, arrays and tuples. For a function value that a callee stores behind a reference argument, make that argument point into the captured places (call_flows), as `rs.push(&x)` does for references.

issues.finding: OR3
issues.description: A callee that gets a callback inside a container and calls it two times is not checked. Examples are `fn opt_twice(o: Option<fn()>)` and `fn vec_twice(fs: Vec<fn()>)`. Only a parameter whose type is a bare function type takes part in `repeats` and the call-again node. Callbacks inside Option, Vec (and probably tuples and structs) are not covered. This slips at base too.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2b: closures, function values and stored references/V_OR3_container_args.wf: 0 errors. Tests via_opt and via_vec_arg fault on all seeds (stock: 'a place does not exist'; oracle: dangling). Expected: W0301 at opt_twice(...) and vec_twice(fs). The bare fn() forms (twice, while, recursion, inner closure, unknown HOF, struct-stored callee, returned wrappers) are all caught: or3_variants.wf, or3_ret.wf.
issues.suggested_fix: Track repeats for each function value that a parameter can hold: Option, Vec, tuple and struct parts, as the stored-value mechanism does. Give the caller's argument a call-again node when the callee can run any such value more than once.

issues.finding: RR2
issues.description: Two closures that meet inside a tuple type do not join. Examples are `Vec<(u64, fn())>`, an array of tuples, and a tuple local that gets a new value `t = (2, || world.entities.clear())`. The join in 7468e09 happens only when a bound type variable meets a function value, and the fn part of a tuple type has no variable of its own. So the first summary wins. Generic structs in a Vec and Option in a Vec are caught.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2b: closures, function values and stored references/V_RR2_tuple_elems.wf: 0 errors. Tests tuple_elems, tuple_array and tuple_reassign each fault on all seeds (oracle: dangling). Expected: W0301 at print(first.hp). Also rr2_tuple.wf tuple_elems_field (`let g = v[1].1`). tuple_first_mut (mutating closure first) is caught.
issues.suggested_fix: When unify meets two Fn types with different summaries at any depth (tuple elements, also inside Vec, array, Option), join them (join_fn) and update the type in place. Do not keep only the left summary. For the re-assignment of a tuple local, apply join_val to its function parts.

issues.finding: FD3
issues.description: The rc escape check covers only references that the body itself puts under a group root. Four shapes slip. (1) A closure that captures a local is stored into an rc object: `c.fs.push(|| print(v.len()))`. (2) A handler clause stores its operation parameter: `handle Put { fn put(x) { c.refs.push(x) ... } } in put(&v[0])`. (3) A closure stores its reference parameter, and a callee gives it a local: `apply(|r: &u64| c.refs.push(r), &v[0])`. (4) A reference into a local rc object is stored into another rc object: `let d = Rc.new(..); c.refs.push(&d.xs[0])`. The object of d is freed at the return, but the checker treats group places as global. It does find `d.*` dying for block values and returns. The same gaps exist at base in check_stored_behind for reference parameters (a closure pushed into `o: &Vec<fn()>`, and `rs.push(&d.data[0])` with a local Rc d), so the 'no back channels' mirror recorded in ADR 0003 is incomplete.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2b: closures, function values and stored references/V_FD3_more.wf: 0 errors. Tests fn_store_rc ('used after it was moved'), clause_store, fnparam_store and local_rc (dangling) fault on all seeds with both interpreters. Expected: W0204 at each marked store. The behind-reference analogs are fd3_fn.wf t_fn_store_ref and fd3_localrc2.wf t_behind_ref, both in the same folder.
issues.suggested_fix: For a function value stored under a group root or behind a reference parameter, check its captured places, as for a stored reference. Give group_stores to clause parameters (op args) and to closure reference parameters through their call flows. Count a place behind a local `Rc` handle (`d.*`) as a local place in stored_behind, as the block-value and return checks already do.

issues.finding: QA11
issues.description: One use can still give two W0301 when a stored-value callee runs the closure. In qa11_dup.wf, `st(|| { print(r + 1); v.clear() })` with `fn st(f: fn()) { let w = Wrap { f: f }; ... g(); g() }` gives 'the closure used after it was invalidated' (from st) and 'the stored closure used after it was invalidated'. The second names `v.push(1)` at line 8 as the invalidating node, before the closure or r exists. That second error is a flow-insensitive false positive from before this stage. The clean form (clean_struct_callee in or3_clean.wf, a closure that only reads) gets the same W0301 at base and HEAD and runs clean.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2b: closures, function values and stored references/qa11_dup.wf: 2 errors at 10:5. The false positive is in or3_clean.wf in the same folder (W0301 at 22:5; the program runs clean).
issues.suggested_fix: Do not let a stored-value holder be invalidated by a node that comes before the value is stored (use the store node as its birth). Also group W0301 entries for the same use node when one holder is the hidden copy of another.

issues.finding: FD3
issues.description: `weft explain W0204` (codes.rs) does not describe the new rc-object case. It mentions only returns and stores behind a reference parameter. CLAUDE.md step 6 asks for the code text to match the rule.
issues.repro: weft explain W0204 at b66e040: the text has no mention of `rc` objects or group roots.
issues.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to the W0204 text in crates/weft-check/src/codes.rs: a function also cannot put such a reference into an `rc` object.

confirmed_fixed: OR2: the repros are fixed. OR2_closure_move_timing.wf (closure_form, task_form) has 0 errors and runs clean with the stock and the oracle interpreter on seeds 1 2 3 7. OR2b keeps W0302 and now faults with --unchecked. fp/W0502_p3681 faults (a true error). fp/W0302_p1066 rejects an `if false` path, as reported. These variants all agree between the checker and the interpreter: part moves, a closure that returns its capture, a move into a struct literal, a let, Some, shadowing in the closure, a conditional move, a move in a clause inside a closure, an inner closure that is only made, loops, test blocks, methods, generics, a 2-unit package, captures of values that hold references (vec_of_refs, holder_*), and once through stored or copied values.

RR7: all 7 expected codes at lines 18/26/35/45/54/62/71, plus a true W0703. These variants are caught too: a stored closure, a loop, a whole tuple re-assignment, an assignment in another closure, a clause, if and match arms, a closure that returns the reference, a closure with a parameter, spawn after the change, a fn change before spawn, a change inside the scope, and a clause that runs a captured closure. The remaining gaps are in the issues list (nested closures, part assignment, returned closures).
RR12: 112_unset_capture.wf has 6 W0304 markers, a clean case and a main. ADR 0007 records the limit for locals.

OR1: OR1 repro (moved, cleared W0301 at f(); scope_ended at the block value), a3 and a6 are fixed. These variants are caught: two levels, tuple, Option, struct, generic struct, a local reference into an argument, id(), a closure maker, an unknown maker, and getters that copy a stored fn out of a reference (as stored values).

OR3: all 4 repro functions get W0301 (at g() for via_returned). These variants are caught: a struct-stored callee, while, recursion, an inner closure, an unknown HOF (hof(twice, ..)), two closure arguments, a returned loop wrapper, a returned two-level wrapper, a struct result and a closure maker. The clean forms that only read or push stay clean, except one stored-callee false positive from before this stage (see the issues).

RR2: the repro has W0301 at 20/29/37/44/52, W0405 at 61, and W0502 at 71 (the second g()). These variants are caught: generic pick<T>, a written fn field, a written Vec<fn()>, a generic push_it<T>, returned values, a fn item first, a nested Vec, Option in a Vec, closures with parameters, assignment from another variable, and generic structs in a Vec. No false positive appears when two generic instantiations, two Vecs or two Options stay separate. 300 joined closures check in 40 ms.

FD3: FD3_rc_backchannel gets W0204 at line 12, and the reference-parameter shape keeps its W0204. These variants are caught: a store in a closure body, a field holder `h.c.refs`, a generic push_it, Vec<Rc<..>>, a task, a returned local rc (mk_leak), and places derived from reference parameters (outer, outer_direct, outer_field). No new false positive appears for references into the group or into another rc parameter (the W0312 there is pre-existing).
QA11: the repro gives 1 error with an 'also' note. No braced hidden name and no raw \u{1} marker appears in any corpus, interpreter-program or probe output.
QA12: diagnose(f, r, &SourceFile) resolves the lines. diagnose_marked and resolve_lines are pub(crate). The diagnostics test covers it.

No regressions in a scan of 28,000 R2 oracle programs, base 57cce5f against HEAD b66e040. 86 are newly rejected: 46 fault and 40 run clean. The 40 are 30 block values under the existing scope rule, 8 W0312 that match the local-closure form, 2 `if false` paths, 1 Rc handle move and 1 capture into a value that the closure moved. 1 is newly accepted (p31218, a fixed closure-local false positive that runs clean). No function lost its last error, except p41118, which is the same fixed false positive. Every corpus and interpreter program with main or tests was run with both interpreters on seeds 1 and 7: only the 5 programs that fail by design fail.
R2b: closures, function values and store.summary:
The stated repros are fixed, the gates pass and I found no regressions, but 6 of the fixes miss shapes that are still unsound. I checked a scratch copy of HEAD b66e040: fmt, clippy -D warnings, rustdoc -D warnings and `cargo test --workspace --release` all pass. The stage does not touch weft-verified or the proofs. All 9 items fix the repros they were given. The base/HEAD scan of 28,000 oracle programs found no lost true positives and no new kinds of false positive. The one newly accepted program is a fixed false positive.

The adversarial probes found 6 missed shapes. Each is a program with 0 errors that faults with --unchecked on every seed, with the stock and the oracle interpreter. All 6 slip at base too, so these are gaps in the fixes, not regressions:
- RR7: a capture reached through another captured closure, and a new value of a part of a captured local (`t.0 = ...`).
- OR1 x RR7: a returned closure whose captured reference gets a new value before the return.
- OR1: a result of type `Vec<fn()>`, and a closure pushed behind a reference parameter.
- OR3: a callback inside an `Option` or `Vec` argument that the callee calls two times.
- RR2: closures that meet inside a tuple type.
- FD3: a closure that captures a local, a clause parameter or a closure parameter stored into an rc object, and a reference into a local rc object.

There are also 2 minor issues: a duplicate W0301 that comes from a stored-closure false positive that was already there, and W0204 explain text that does not mention rc objects.

Each repro is a .wf file whose name starts with `V_` in SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2b: closures, function values and stored references/, with the probe and scan scripts next to them. I deleted the scratch build directories, and the worktree is clean.

issues.finding: RR7
issues.description: The late join only looks at the direct captures of the closure that runs (late_changes over cap_values of the summary members). A new value of a variable that an inner closure captures is lost when an outer closure runs the inner one. The inner closure's effects were merged into the outer summary where the outer closure was made, and the inner function variable did not change, so no change is found. This affects reference captures, function-valued captures and containers that get a new reference (rs.push).
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/repro/V1_rr7_nested.wf (two_levels_ref, two_levels_hof, two_levels_fn): 0 errors at HEAD. Each faults with the stock interpreter ('a place does not exist') and the oracle ('access to a freed cell') on seeds 1 2 3 7. Also p/rr7e.wf two_levels_task (expected W0405) and p/rr7j.wf push_late2.
issues.suggested_fix: In late_join, recurse through the closures that the running closure can run: for each cap_runs entry whose variable is unchanged, run late_join on that variable's current function value with the mapped givens, guarded by late_stack.

issues.finding: RR7
issues.description: A closure that leaves the function keeps the places of its captures from where it was made. returned_places (and so ret_refs) and check_stored_behind use the refs of the closure value at creation. A by-reference capture that gets a new value before the return or after the store is lost. The cases are: a new place in another parameter (the caller gets no W0301), a new place in a local of the callee (no W0204 at the return), and a closure stored behind a reference parameter whose capture then points into a local (no W0204).
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/repro/V2_rr7_return_store.wf (returned_late, returned_local, stored_param): 0 errors. Each faults with both interpreters. Also p/rr7a.wf returned_late2 (the new value set in a branch).
issues.suggested_fix: Where a closure value leaves (check_returns/returned_places, note_stored_behind, apply_stored), join late_ret-style rebased places from the end-of-body values of its by-reference captures (as finish_task_values does for tasks). Then check them with W0204/ret_refs.

issues.finding: OR1
issues.description: ret_refs comes from the places of the returned value. A closure that goes into a container that is returned does not add its places to the container local: Vec push of a closure, a field set after the struct is made (h.f = closure), or a generic field set later. ret_refs is Some([]) here, so the caller gets no places and no wildcard. The task suggested the wildcard of each reference argument. The precise approach misses every shape where the closure goes through the stored-value mechanism and not through refs.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/repro/V3_or1_containers.wf (in_vec, field_set, wrap_set): 0 errors. Each faults with both interpreters. The local forms (closure in a local Vec<fn()>) are caught as 'the stored closure'.
issues.suggested_fix: In ret_refs_sig, add the places of the closures that the body stores (escaped) or that flow into the result through parts and containers. Or fall back to the wildcard of each reference argument when the body stores a closure value into the result.

issues.finding: OR3
issues.description: The 'call again' node is added only when the callback is a direct function parameter (param_runs/param_calls at depth 0), or for a direct call of a returned value with repeat_runs. A callee that gets the callback inside a tuple, a struct with a fn field, an Option or a generic struct and calls it twice is not seen (single-run effects are applied, see p/or3b.wf). A returned repeating closure (RetFn::repeats) given to a callee (run(g)) or spawned (s.spawn(g)) also does not run twice.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/repro/V4_or3_containers.wf (via_tuple, via_struct, via_option, returned_given, returned_task): 0 errors. Each faults with both interpreters. Also p/or3a.wf via_wrap (Wrap<fn()>).
issues.suggested_fix: Count calls of function values that come out of a parameter (a part, a field or a match binding of the parameter) in param_runs for that parameter. In give_fn, apply_value of an argument and spawn, honour repeat_runs of the given value: add run_again where a value with repeat_runs is given to a callee or a task.

issues.finding: RR2
issues.description: The join happens only in fn_joins for a type variable bound to a Fn type. A tuple literal has concrete Fn element types, not variables. So two closures that meet in a tuple keep the first summary only: a tuple part assignment, a new whole tuple value, a Vec of tuples, or a tuple in a generic field. This is the RR2 root cause (one summary in the unified type) for the tuple container.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/repro/V5_rr2_tuples.wf (tuple_part, tuple_whole, tuple_in_vec, wrap_tuple_part): 0 errors. Each faults with both interpreters.
issues.suggested_fix: Give tuple element types type variables, as the element and field types now do (inf.shallow instead of deep at tuple construction and part access). Or extend fn_joins to rebind a concrete Fn inside a tuple that a local or a container holds (join_val for part holders).

issues.finding: FD3
issues.description: Store into an rc group root is checked for a reference expression (note_stored_behind, group_stores). Two closure shapes are missed. (1) A local closure that puts its own parameter into an rc object: closure params have depth > 0, so neither group_stores nor the call site of the closure check the argument. (2) A closure that captures a local reference, or a local, is pushed into an rc object (c.cbs.push(|| ...)): the closure goes through the stored-value path, not stored_behind. ADR 0003 now states that a reference in an rc object cannot point into a local of a returned function, which is false for these. The same closure push behind a reference parameter (h.cbs.push(closure)) is also missed at base (p/fd3c.wf), so the param mirror is incomplete too.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/repro/V6_fd3_closures.wf (fill_closure, fill_cb, fill_cb_owned): 0 errors. t_closure and t_cb fault 'a place does not exist'/'access to a freed cell'. t_cb_owned faults 'a value is used after it was moved'.
issues.suggested_fix: Treat a closure value stored under an rc group root (or behind a reference parameter) as an escape of its refs, including the local roots of its captures (the W0204 rule for closures stored behind a parameter field). Record stores of closure parameters into rc objects in the closure summary so that the closure call site checks its arguments.

issues.finding: OR3
issues.description: This is a new false positive. repeats_sig adds every param_calls entry of every closure that is not only returned, and it ignores the 'again' flag. So a callee that calls its callback once, in a closure that it runs once, counts as repeating. Before this stage that gave only W0502 for once closures. The new run_again node now gives W0301 for any closure that changes what it captures. Wrappers such as `fn timed(f: fn()) { run(|| f()) }` are common.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/repro/V7_or3_fp.wf: base 57cce5f 0 errors, HEAD W0301 at with_cb(...) line 13. It runs cleanly and prints 2 with both interpreters.
issues.suggested_fix: In repeats_sig, add a parameter from param_calls only when its again flag is set, or when the closure can itself run more than once (in a loop, at two nodes, stored, or given to a repeating callee), as ret_repeats does.

issues.finding: QA11
issues.description: group_uses merges W0301 entries whose use spans nest. A loop node spans its whole body. So the iterators of two nested loops that the same call invalidates become one error at the outer loop line. The inner loop's error (a different variable on another line) is now only an 'also' note. The finding asked for a grouping by (use node, invalidating node).
issues.repro: SCRATCH/r2/oracle/runs/g4/p10989.wf: base has W0301 at lines 71 and 72 (two loop iterators, invalidated by swap_in at 73). HEAD has only line 71, with 'also the loop iterator ... (line 72)'. Many oracle programs lose a W0301 line the same way (scratchpad/verify/s5/diff_all.txt, cmp2.py).
issues.suggested_fix: Group only entries with the same use node, or only nest a hidden holder (part holder, stored closure, temporary) into the entry of a program variable. Do not merge two distinct variables whose use nodes differ.

issues.finding: OR3
issues.description: In crates/weft-sema/src/body/fnval.rs (around line 1140) the new fn ret_repeats was put between the doc comment of ret_sig and ret_sig. ret_repeats now starts with the ret_sig text ('Returns what a call of the returned function value does ... `bases` are the places of the parameters.'), and ret_sig has no doc comment.
issues.repro: sed -n 1138,1160p /home/user/wt-core/crates/weft-sema/src/body/fnval.rs
issues.suggested_fix: Move the first two doc lines back above ret_sig.

issues.finding: RR7
issues.description: Several new ADR sentences exceed the ASD-STE100 sentence length (25 words for descriptive text). An example is the RR7 bullet in ADR 0003: 'For a variable with a place that it did not have where the closure was made, the node uses the variable (W0301), and it mutates, reads and lends the places of the closure below the old places, moved onto the new places (W0301, W0402).' The same is true of parts of the OR2 and OR1 bullets.
issues.repro: git -C /home/user/wt-core diff 57cce5f..HEAD -- docs/adr/0003-place-model.md
issues.suggested_fix: Split the long sentences into short ones.

confirmed_fixed: OR2: by-value captures agree between sema (FnFacts::by_value) and the interpreter. I probed these shapes and each was consistent: assign in the closure, a by-ref closure made first, a field move, a loop, parens, a direct argument, a named task, generics, a shadowed name in nested closures and clauses, a clause move at perform, a once closure stored. Both OR2 repro functions run cleanly. OR2b, fp/W0502_p3681 and W0302_p1066 (with if true) fault as true errors.
RR12: kept_documented is justified. The decision came with the task, Rust rejects the closure form too, and ADR 0007 and corpus 112 document it. The program prints 1, 7, 3.
QA12: the public diagnose takes the SourceFile and resolves the markers. resolve_lines is pub(crate). The marker sentinel is \u{1}.
QA11: the original repro gives 1 error with an 'also' note, and no corpus output has a braced name. See the minor issue about nested-span grouping.
The original repros of RR7, RR2 (W0502 at line 71, explained), OR1, OR3 and FD3 now give the expected codes. The missed shapes are listed as issues.
R2b: closures, function values and store.summary:
Gates pass at b66e040: cargo fmt --check, clippy -D warnings (workspace pedantic and nursery), cargo test --workspace, rustdoc -D warnings and a release build. weft-verified and proofs are not touched, so verify-all.sh was not needed. The added production code has no unwrap/expect/unsafe. No spec, rules or Violations change, so the 8-step checklist does not apply: by_value is an FnFacts field, not a relation.

I rebuilt the oracle interpreter at HEAD and re-ran every corpus and interpreter program with main or tests (seeds 1 2 3 7, both interpreters). Only the 5 programs that fail by design fail.

I compared the base binary 57cce5f and HEAD on all 26,400 R2 oracle programs:
- 1 program is newly accepted. It is the fixed clause-capture false positive, and it runs cleanly.
- 68 are newly rejected. 29 fault. The 39 that run cleanly match the implementer's explanation: dangling block values that are never called, and the W0312 rule.
- The design.md examples and examples/ give the same results as at base.

OR2 is solid, and RR12 and QA12 are fine. RR7, OR1, OR3, RR2 and FD3 pass their original repros, but each misses shapes from the same root cause. These are unsound: 0 errors, and both interpreters fault.
- RR7: nested closures (V1), and closures that are returned or stored behind a parameter after a capture gets a new value (V2).
- OR1: call results that hold closures in a Vec, in a field set after the struct is made, or in a generic field (V3). The precise ret_refs choice misses them; the wildcard approach that the task suggested would catch them.
- OR3: callbacks passed inside a tuple, struct or Option, and returned repeating closures given to a callee or spawned (V4).
- RR2: tuple types, which have no type variable to join (V5).
- FD3: closures that store into rc objects, or closures that capture locals pushed into rc (V6).

OR3 also adds a new W0301 false positive for a callee that runs its callback once inside a closure (V7: base 0 errors, HEAD 1).

Minor issues: QA11 grouping by nested spans merges distinct nested-loop iterator errors; a doc comment in fnval.rs is misplaced (ret_repeats/ret_sig); some ADR sentences are too long for ASD-STE100.

Repros are in SCRATCH/verify/s5/repro/ (V1-V7) and in SCRATCH/verify/s5/p/. The worktree was not changed. I deleted my oracle build dir.

resolved: OR3 major (V7, false positive): `repeats_sig` now counts a parameter call in a closure only if the call is direct and repeats inside the closure, or if the closure itself can run more than once. That covers a closure that is stored, run at two nodes, in a loop, at a repeated node, or inside a closure or clause that repeats (new `closure_runs_again`; `param_calls` now records whether a call is direct; `Applied.in_loop`). `reach_repeats` uses the same test. V7, fp4 and the `with_cb`/`timed`/nested-once wrappers now have 0 errors and run cleanly. The lost W0502s in oracle p33742 and p44047 were false positives (each callee calls its callback once).

RR7 blocker (nested captures and parts): `late_join` and `late_once` now follow captured function variables that keep the same value into the closure they run (guarded by `late_stack`). `cap_refs_now` counts the part holders of a captured local, including a log of past holders at the end of the body, so `t.0 = &x` counts as a change. V1 two_levels_ref, two_levels_hof and two_levels_fn, plus V_RR7 nested_late, nested_fn_late, nested_task (W0405), nested_once (W0502) and tuple_part_late, all have their expected codes. Test: tests/programs/117_late_nested.wf.

RR7 blocker (closure leaving the body) and OR1 (ret_late): a returned value now includes the current places of its captures (`with_fn_refs` / `val_late_refs`). A closure stored behind a reference parameter or into an rc object records `late_stores`, checked with the end-of-body values. V2 now gives returned_late W0301, mk_local W0204 and store_late W0204. V_OR1 ret_late gives W0301. Covered in 117.

OR1 blocker (containers): a local keeps the closures that are pushed into its containers (`held_fns`) and those in its parts (part holders). Tuple, struct and array literals carry those places, so a returned `Vec<fn()>`, `(Vec<fn()>, u64)`, a field set after construction and `Wrap<fn()>` all point into the captures. New signature part `EffectSig::fn_store_refs`: a callee that puts a closure behind a reference argument states the places the closure points into, and the caller gives its local a hidden part variable from the call on (flow-sensitive). V3 in_vec, field_set and wrap_set, and V_OR1 via_vec, via_tupvec and via_out_param, all report W0301. Tests added to tests/programs/113_returned_closures.wf, including a clean case where the container is made before the change.

OR3 blocker (containers and returned repeating values): when a callee can run a stored value more than once (`reach_repeats`), `apply_stored` inserts a 'call again' use of the stored closure. A value whose summary has `repeat_runs` now gets a second run when it is given to an item, a value callee or a spawn (`runs_held_again`). V4 via_tuple, via_struct, via_option, returned_given and returned_task, and V_OR3 via_opt and via_vec_arg, all report W0301. Tests added to 114_repeated_callbacks.wf, with clean container and wrapper cases in main.

RR2 blocker (tuples): a part of a tuple literal that can hold a function gets its own type variable, so the existing join in `unify` applies to a part assignment, a whole-tuple reassignment, a Vec or array of tuples, and a tuple in a generic field. V5 (4 shapes) and V_RR2 (3 shapes) all report W0301. Tests added to 115_joined_fn_values.wf.

FD3 blocker (closures): `call_flows` treats a closure that a callee puts behind a reference or into an rc object as a store of its captures (`note_stored_fn`, message 'a closure that captures'). `group_stores_of` checks closure arguments, and a function parameter put into an rc counts as a group store. Closure and clause parameters stored there are recorded in a new `Summary::param_stores`, so `apply_summary` and `clause_through_params` check the places each run actually gives. A dependency on a local `Rc` handle of a different rc type now counts as local. V6 fill_closure, fill_cb and fill_cb_owned, and V_FD3 fn_store_rc, clause_store, fnparam_store and local_rc, all report W0204. A closure pushed behind a reference parameter is also W0204, and each of these faults at run time. Tests added to 116_rc_stores.wf.

QA11 minor (duplicate W0301 and stored-before-store false positive): `apply_stored` no longer runs or uses a stored value at nodes that come strictly before its store; nodes in other graph parts (for example a handled body) keep it, which preserves RR6. qa11_dup now gives 1 error and or3_clean gives 0.

QA11 minor (grouping): `group_uses` merges entries with different use nodes only when one is a hidden holder and the other a program variable, so two nested loop iterators are reported separately again. Diagnostics tests added.
Minor: the `ret_sig` doc comment is moved back above `ret_sig` in fnval.rs.
Minor: the `weft explain` texts are updated. W0204 now covers rc objects, local Rc handles, and closures with their later capture values. W0301 now covers late capture values and repeated callbacks.
Minor: the long ADR sentences are split. ADR 0003, 0005 and 0006 and architecture.md record the new decisions and limits.

not_resolved.issue: FD3 residual: a closure or clause that stores its own reference parameter into an rc object, or behind a reference parameter, is checked only at the nodes in the body that run it.
not_resolved.reason: A function value does not state where the references it receives live. Unknown code, or a known callee that passes it a reference into its own local, can still hand it a dangling reference. Closing this needs a lifetime-like bound on function types, which is outside this stage. Recorded as a limit in ADR 0003.

not_resolved.issue: FD3 precision: a reference stored into an rc object through a handle of the same rc type is allowed, even when the handle refers to another object.
not_resolved.reason: Kept on purpose so the corpus design example `c.refs.push(&c.data[0])` is not a false positive. Group places cannot tell objects of one type apart. Recorded as a limit in ADR 0003.

not_resolved.issue: Pre-existing false positive (not from this stage): a local that receives a reference from a callee through `holds` (for example `reg_ref(&h, r)`) points into the reference flow-insensitively, so a mutation between its `let` and the call invalidates it.
not_resolved.reason: This is not an R2b item and it is present at the base. The new closure paths avoid it: they use a hidden part variable bound at the call node instead of `point_local`.

R2b: closures, function values and store.summary:
I fixed every verifier blocker and major from the R2b review, and the cheap minors, in one commit: f211d13 on review/s5 in /home/user/wt-core (parent b66e040). All gates passed after the last code change: cargo fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --workspace (debug, 507 passed, 0 failed) and the rustdoc build with -D warnings. weft-verified and proofs/ were not touched, so verify-all.sh was not needed.

Regression tests:
- New corpus file tests/programs/117_late_nested.wf, with bad and clean cases and a main.
- New bad and clean cases in 113, 114, 115 and 116.
- New cases in crates/weft-check/tests/diagnostics.rs.

TDD check: I built the stage head (b66e040) in scratch. With it, every new marker fails: the bad cases give no error, and the clean wrapper and container cases in 114 give false W0301s. All corpus markers match at f211d13. The clean mains of 110 to 117 run without faults on seeds 1, 2, 3 and 7.

Oracle comparison (26,400 programs, b66e040 against the new binary):
- No program is newly rejected.
- The only lost diagnostics are three W0502 false positives.
- The other differences are W0301s for two distinct variables that the stage head had merged into one error.

Probe folders (627 files across the verify, oracle, red-team, fidelity and quality folders): every verifier repro now reports its expected codes. The only lost diagnostics are the known false positives V7, or3_clean, fp1 and fp4.

Soundness run: I ran every accepted oracle program (main and tests, seeds 1, 2, 3 and 7). The only faults are index or split out-of-bounds panics, and use-after-move in m1/m2 programs. Those programs were accepted at b66e040 too and come from the open OR6 expression-statement move. One program, m1/p972, also timed out in `run`.

Known limits are recorded in ADR 0003 and listed under not_resolved. Scratch build directories are deleted.

R2c: effects, continuations, on abort an.summary:
Stage R2c is committed as one commit on review/s5 in /home/user/wt-core: 3af6118, on top of base f211d13. All 14 items are done and each has tests. Every gate passed. cargo fmt --check and clippy -D warnings are clean. cargo test --workspace passes (41 test binaries, 0 failed). cargo doc -D warnings is clean. proofs/verify-all.sh passes: borrowing 169, effects 122, link 233 and weft-verified 66 verified, 0 errors. Random agreement also passed with PROPTEST_CASES=6000.

Oracle check: I built the oracle interpreter twice, once from the base commit and once from the working tree, and ran each over about 27 600 generated R2 programs. The files with ORACLE faults are the same 37 in both runs. They are all task data races, which belong to other stages. Faulting files fell from 361 to 340 on the generated set and from 46 to 39 on the smaller sets. Two programs fail only in the new run: they are newly accepted after the OR4 fix and stop with an ordinary index-out-of-bounds error, not a memory fault.

Corpus: new programs tests/programs/120 to 127. Each has bad cases with //~ markers, clean cases, and a main that runs the clean cases. New interpreter programs: multi_nested_drop, multi_clause_caps and place_statements. Three existing corpus files changed:
- 88_empty_values.wf: a W0602 marker went away. It was the OR4 false positive: the linear value lives outside the handle.
- 89_abort_paths.wf: the two Fail controls that resumed now use the user effect Op.
- body_texts.rs: one expected message changed. A generic drop whose argument cannot be named now names the callee.

The build dirs are deleted. The probe programs and oracle result lists stay in SCRATCH/s5/r2c/.

findings.evidence: New program::check_on_abort_rows (crates/weft-sema/src/program.rs) runs after inference from crates/weft-sema/src/lib.rs. It reads the final row of each on abort function. It gives W0118 for fail, for a user effect, for any effect with no runtime, and for a mut place outside its by-value parameter (an rc group or a Held step). The five bad repros (FD1 outer_handler, no_handler, mutates_group, QA2, triage FD1_onabort_fail) each get one W0118. The control FD1_control_onabort_std stays at 0 errors and runs (undo 1 / slept / end). Corpus: tests/programs/120_on_abort_effects.wf, 5 bad cases, clean clock/log/local cases and a main. Sema tests cover no-runtime and a dependency unit. Recorded in ADR 0007, the design doc, the W0118 explain text, and rule 8 of proofs/effects/README.md (the assumption is mirrored).
findings.notes: Error text: 'on abort function `x` performs `E`, but the unwinder runs it with the root handlers only'. Separate texts for fail and for a mut place.

findings.evidence: New code W0504, set by Lower::fail_resume. It fires at a resume, and at any use of the continuation name, in a clause of the standard Fail.fail; ContInfo.fail marks such a clause. All 7 IP1 repros (ip_fail_resume_{join,scope,fork,timeout}, ip_fail_interrupt_{join,scope_wait,fork}) get W0504 at the resume. Corpus 121_fail_resume.wf covers a direct resume, a closure and a branch. Its clean cases are a Fail clause that returns a value and a user effect that resumes. The two 89_abort_paths controls now use Op. W0504 text added to codes.rs. Recorded in ADR 0005 and rule 7 of proofs/effects/README.md.

Each clause gets a continuation capability (kcap) in the caps of its `resume` local. check_cont_escape (caps.rs) gives W0313 in these cases: the clause value holds kcap; a value kept since the clause start holds it; or a local outside the handle holds it, as a stored part or as a new value from the body through the resume value. keep_conts_for_op covers giving the closure to an outer operation. RR3_continuation_escape.wf now gets W0313 at lines 14, 19, 25 and 31 ('all markers match'). Corpus 122_cont_escape.wf adds a storing callee, an outer operation and the resume value into the body. Clean cases: a resuming closure called in place, given to a callee that only calls it, or held in a clause local. Recorded in ADR 0005 and the W0313 text.

check_task_value treats kcap as a handler on this task. A spawned task or fork branch that holds a resuming closure gets W0314 with the text 'a task cannot resume a continuation of this task: the rest of the handled body would run on another task'. OR9_resume_in_task.wf gets W0314 at the spawn in both lost_handler (10:54) and race (19:50). The corpus also has a fork branch case. Recorded in ADR 0005 and the W0314 text.

At base, RR5_resume_free.wf already gave W0301 at line 18 (moves of outer locals reached the resume through ContInfo.frees, an earlier fix). My probes showed one gap left: owner scope ends in the handled body. A clause parameter could point into a local or temporary of the body that goes out of scope before resume returns. Fix: inner_frees() collects the owners that move or go out of scope in the body, and they go into Handled.frees, which reaches resume_through_params and releases_at. The handled body also gets its own temporary scope, so a temporary in its value goes out of scope at its end (the interpreter runs the body in a frame of its own). Corpus 123_resume_scope_ends.wf (4 bad, 2 clean); 104_resume_frees still matches. Recorded in ADR 0005 and ADR 0003.
findings.notes: The main RR5 repro was already fixed at base. This stage closed the scope-end and temporary shapes of the same finding.

findings.evidence: copy_frames (crates/weft-interp/src/machine/effects.rs) now finds nested Clause frames, also inside nested continuations. It gives each copy its own ContRec in the same state and copies its frames with the shared cell map; remap_conts rewrites Value::Cont. FD2_multi_nested_drop.wf now prints 2 on every seed, where it faulted before. New program crates/weft-interp/tests/programs/multi_nested_drop.wf prints [0, 11, 21, 0]. Updated the ex_multi_dropped_resume text in proofs/link/README.md and the matching doc comment in proofs/link/src/lifecycle_link.rs; verify-all passes.

copy_list maps the clause cells of each copied Frame::Handle through the copy map. ip_multi_clause_caps.wf now prints [1, 1] (it printed [0, 1]); the control also prints [1, 1]. New interpreter program multi_clause_caps.wf with expected output [1, 1, 1, 2] / [1, 1].

New spec input spared_at(V, P), added with the 8-step checklist: FnFacts field with mark, rewind and normalize; spec rules abort_unhandled and live_across_multi get !spared_at(V, P); rules.rs; bridge each_fact; agreement_random generator (relation 35). Sema records each direct operation of a local handler (not a sim.run root) with the variables outside the handled body (outside_vars). finish_spared emits spared_at when nothing else at the node suspends (out_suspends) and no clause node of that handler suspends outward. Resumes do not count. OR4_fp_outside_handle.wf has 0 errors and all forms run cleanly. Bad cases stay: the linear value inside the body (W0602; W0503 with W0602), a clause that fails, and a clause that chooses through an outer multi handler (corpus 124_local_suspends.wf). W0602 and W0503 texts updated in ADR 0005, ADR 0007, codes.rs and the architecture diagram.

Spec rule once_var(V) :- immovable(V) added; rules.rs multi() mirrors it. New property Prop::Resource in props.rs covers Task, Scope, and a non-plain-data extern type other than Vec/Box; Rc/Weak do not pass it on. A variable with this property gets the once flag. FD4_multi_immovable.wf now gets W0503 at choose (10:13), with a note for !Move values. FD4_multi_affine.wf stays at 0 errors and runs (deep copy kept). Corpus 125_multi_values.wf: immovable, scope binder and resource are bad; Vec, Box, Rc and a !Move value made after the operation are clean. The props unit test is extended. ADR 0005 and ADR 0007 record the Phase 1 meaning (owned cells are copied, rc objects are shared), the cost for a native runtime and the E5 gap.

std_drops in program.rs puts type parameter 0 in `drops` for Vec.clear, Task.detach and Response.json (I checked each prelude function). Sema lowers detach itself, so join() also drops the result. RR8_vec_clear.wf gets W0601 at line 14 (reset) and line 18 (reset_generic). Corpus 126_element_drops.wf covers clear, generic clear, detach and json, with clean plain-data versions. Recorded in ADR 0007 and the W0601 text.

A place of a local in statement position (a name, field or element chain) now moves and drops nothing on both sides. Interpreter: compile.rs local_place compiles it as a place and pops the location. Sema: stmt.rs skips drop_value. The three OR6_expr_statement_move functions and n8_immov_expr_stmt now run cleanly with both the stock and the oracle interpreter, with 0 errors. New interpreter program place_statements.wf. Corpus 127_place_statements.wf has a bad case (W0601: the statement does not consume) and 5 clean cases; one of them gave a false W0601 at base. Recorded in ADR 0003.

New VarKind::Dropped. check_item_value and callee_drops (when the argument cannot be named) use it, and finish now shows the resolved type of hidden variables. RR9_generic_item_drops.wf lines 16, 19 and 22 now read '`sink` drops a value of the linear type `Tx`' with a note naming `sink`. The old text was 'linear value `T`' with 'T : _'. New test diagnostics.rs w0601_names_the_generic_item_value_and_the_type; body_texts expectation updated.

The input is renamed sim_root(H) and the spec now has forwards(H) :- sim_root(H). The rename covers the HandlerInfo.forwards field (now sim_root), sema (sim_run and handle), rules.rs, bridge each_fact and the agreement_random generator. The checker unit test w0801 now checks that the facts text has sim_root(h1) and no forwards input, and that the spec derives forwards(h1). The corpus rule-coverage test passes. docs/architecture.md draws spawn -> mutates_at labelled sema.
ADR 0005 has a new line: in Phase 1 the effect rows are the capabilities, and env holds only handles (Env { fs, net, stdout }). FD10_env_capabilities.wf is still accepted and runs cleanly.

proofs/effects/README.md, 'Spec checker': it now says that crates/weft-verified has no effects checker. The part that is not linked is the sema suspension facts (may_abort, multi_at, clause_multi, body_multi, resumes_at, spared_at) and the spec rules of W0602 and W0503.

design_decisions: FD1: on abort rows are checked after inference in a new program::check_on_abort_rows. It reuses code W0118 with new texts, so no new 06xx code is added. With no runtime, any named effect is an error, because the unwinder has no root handlers then.

IP1: new code W0504 for a resume, or any use of the continuation name, in a clause of the standard Fail effect. A user effect called Fail (identity main.Fail) is not affected. The interpreter does not change; R2d IP2 will move child-failure delivery.

RR3/OR9: each clause mints a continuation capability (a fresh CapId) in the caps of its `resume` local. Closures that capture `resume` carry it through the existing W0313/W0314 machinery. A local outside the handle that gets the closure from the handled body (through the resume value) also counts as an escape, which is a little conservative (noted in ADR 0005).

RR5: Handled.frees now holds the owners of the body that move or go out of scope. ContInfo.frees still holds only outer locals. The handled body gets its own temporary scope, the same as the interpreter's separate HandleBody frame.

OR4: spared_at(V, P) is a new spec input, not a sema-only filter, so checker and spec still agree. Only direct operations of a local, non-sim handler spare values. A clause counts as contained when no node in its range is in out_suspends and every local operation there goes to a handler installed inside the clause. Resume nodes do not count. Calls of items or closures that perform the operation do not spare (noted as imprecise in ADR 0005).

FD4: !Move values go through the spec rule once_var(V) :- immovable(V). Tasks, scopes and non-plain-data extern types use a new Prop::Resource and the once flag. Other owned values keep the interpreter's deep copy, recorded as the Phase 1 meaning of a multi resume.

RR8: prelude drops are a small table, std_drops, by owner and name (Vec.clear, Task.detach, Response.json), not prelude syntax. detach is also checked in sema's join(), because sema lowers detach itself.
RR9: a new VarKind::Dropped lets the diagnostic name the callee and the resolved type. The same message is used when callee_drops cannot name the argument, so one body_texts expectation changed.
FD9: HandlerInfo.forwards was renamed to sim_root so that the facts field and the spec input have the same name.
Following the R2b convention, each new corpus file has a main that runs its clean cases, so the static-corpus interpreter test exercises them.

issues.finding: OR4 (spared_at) regression: an outer linear value that a closure or a handler clause in the handled body takes by value is spared at a local operation inside that closure or clause
issues.description: Lower::outside_vars (crates/weft-sema/src/body/mod.rs) treats every local of the frames below the handler as outside the handled body. finish_spared (body/aborts.rs) then emits spared_at(l, op) for those locals. In the cases below, the operation runs inside a closure body or an inner handler clause that took the outer local by value. A closure that moves `l` gets a cell of its own when it is made (OR2), and an inner handler gets its clause cells when it is installed. So at run time the value lives inside the handled body, and the abort unwinds it. Sema reports nothing, because the closure body and the clause name the outer local by its outer VarId. Base f211d13 gave W0602 at each operation. HEAD gives 0 errors, and the oracle reports a linear leak. So this stage made the checker less sound. The multi analogues are still caught through handled_again (W0302/W0503 at the call), so only W0602 is affected.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2c/repro/V1_spared_by_value_capture.wf. HEAD: '0 error(s)'. Base: W0602 at 16:30, 24:43 and 32:44. `weft facts ... closure_captures` shows spared_at(v0, n4) with n4 = ask inside the closure. Oracle (instrumented interpreter at HEAD), with each function run alone: closure_captures and nested_closure give 'ORACLE linear leak: a linear value is still live at the end of the run'. clause_capture gives 'ORACLE linear leak: a live linear value was dropped with no consume and no `on abort`'. Shape: `let l = Lk{..}; handle Ask { fn ask() { 0 } } in { let g = || { let x = ask(); unlock(l); x }; g() }`.
issues.suggested_fix: Do not spare a variable at an operation that runs in a closure body or a handler clause above the handler (a frame between the handler and the operation) if that closure or clause captures the variable by value: its moved captures, and the captures of an inner clause. The simplest sound rule is to give no spared_at for an operation whose node is inside a closure or clause frame above the handler frames. Add the three functions to tests/programs/124_local_suspends.wf as bad cases.

issues.finding: FD1 missed shapes: an on abort function can fail at run time through join, fs.read, fork or a scope end. Its row has no Fail, so W0118 is silent
issues.description: check_on_abort_rows (crates/weft-sema/src/program.rs) looks only at the named effects of the inferred row. Several operations can raise a failure at run time without Fail in the row: Task.join (`/ async`), FsCap.read (`/ fs`), fork and the end of a scope with a failed child. The IP1 text lists the same points. Inside an on abort function, such a failure does not reach the Fail handler around the computation. The run ends with 'failed: ...'. This is the FD1_onabort_fail shape that the decision ('no fail') was meant to close.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2c/repro/V2a_onabort_fs_read_fails.wf: 0 errors. `weft run` prints 'undo', then 'error: failed: cannot read /nonexistent/missing.txt' at 7:11. The Fail handler around the computation never prints 'caught'. SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2c/repro/V2b_onabort_join_fails.wf: 0 errors. On seeds 1, 2 and 3 it prints 'caught child failed', then 'undo', then 'error: failed: child failed' at 9:11 (the join in undo_join).
issues.suggested_fix: Treat each node that sema marks abortive through a runtime failure (join, scope end, fork, FsCap.read; also with_timeout, which is already in the row) as failing for the on abort check. For example, record a 'can raise a runtime failure' flag in the inferred EffectSig and give W0118 for it, as for Fail. Add bad cases to tests/programs/120_on_abort_effects.wf and update ADR 0007.

issues.finding: OR6 shape left open: a place as the tail of a block whose value is discarded (block statement, for/while body) moves and drops at run time, but sema sees no move
issues.description: The fix covers only a bare place in statement position. When the place is the tail of a block whose value is discarded, the interpreter still moves the value into the block value and drops it. Examples: `{ t }` as a statement, `for i in 0..2 { t }`, `while c { ...; t }`. Sema reports neither a move nor a drop. The OR6 decision says that a block tail moves, so sema must see the move and the drop (W0601/W0302), or the interpreter must not move. The gap was already there at base. It has the same root cause as OR6, and 'every shape' was required.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2c/repro/V3_tail_place_statement.wf: 0 errors at HEAD and at base. Stock interpreter: block_tail, for_tail, while_tail and immovable_block_tail fault with 'a value is used after it was moved', and vec_block_tail faults with 'a place does not exist'. Oracle: linear leak for the first three, and 'ORACLE: access to a freed cell (a dangling reference)' for vec_block_tail.
issues.suggested_fix: Pick one meaning for a discarded block tail and use it in both tools. Either sema lowers the tail as a move into the block value and drops that value (W0601 for a linear value, W0302 for a later use), or compile.rs compiles a local-place tail of a discarded block as a place, as it does for a statement. Record the choice in ADR 0003. Add the cases to tests/programs/127_place_statements.wf and crates/weft-interp/tests/programs/place_statements.wf.

issues.finding: FD4: a resource temporary given to a generic callee that holds it across a multi operation is not checked
issues.description: callee_holds (crates/weft-sema/src/body/call.rs, the `holds` loop) gets `once` from val_not_many. For a temporary, `v.var` is None, so a value of a Prop::Resource type (a nonportable extern type) is not once. W0503 fires when the same value is in a named local, or in a Vec in a named local, but not when it is a temporary argument.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2c/repro/V4_resource_temp_generic_holder.wf: `generic_resource(open())` at line 14 gets no W0503. `named` (line 11) and `in_vec` (line 19) get it.
issues.suggested_fix: In the holds loop, also treat the argument as once if its type has Prop::Resource or is !Move (ty_has_strict(&av.val.ty, Prop::Resource)), not only if its variable is once.

issues.finding: RR9 message change also hits closures, and callee_drops tests for a 'temporary' sentinel string
issues.description: Corpus 71 line 163 used to read 'a closure moves a linear value, but it can go out of scope without a call'. It now reads '`gen_drop` drops a value of the linear type `fn() -> ()`'. A closure type is not a linear type, so the new text is less clear. callee_drops picks the new text with `if name == "temporary"`, the string that generic_arg returns when it cannot name the argument. A user local named `temporary` therefore also gets the callee text.
issues.repro: `target/release/weft check tests/programs/71_closure_modes.wf` gives 'error[W0601]: `gen_drop` drops a value of the linear type `fn() -> ()`' at 163:14. The sentinel is at crates/weft-sema/src/body/call.rs:1034, and generic_arg returns it at lines 1055 and 1056.
issues.suggested_fix: Keep the closure text when the dropped type is a closure type. Make generic_arg return Option<String> (None when it cannot name the argument) instead of a sentinel string.

R2c: effects, continuations, on abort an.summary:
All gates pass at 3af6118 in /home/user/wt-core. fmt --check, clippy -D warnings (the workspace enables pedantic and nursery) and cargo test --workspace (41 binaries) pass, and so does cargo doc -D warnings. proofs/verify-all.sh passes: borrowing 169, effects 122, link 233 and weft-verified 66, all with 0 errors. Every named repro for the 14 items behaves as claimed, and the R2 repro and triage marker sets show no regression against base f211d13. I built base and the HEAD oracle in scratch and have since deleted both.

Adversarial probing found one blocker regression. The OR4 spared_at fix spares an outer linear value at a local operation in two cases: when the operation runs inside a closure that took the value by value, and when it runs inside an inner handler clause that captured the value. In both cases the value lives in the handled body, and the abort unwinds it. Base gave W0602; HEAD gives 0 errors, and the oracle reports a linear leak (V1).

Two major missed shapes remain:
- FD1: an on abort function can still fail through join or fs.read (and, by the same mechanism, fork or a scope end), because these failures are not in its row. The failure escapes the Fail handler (V2a/V2b).
- OR6: a place as the tail of a block whose value is discarded still moves and drops in the interpreter, but sema sees nothing. This was already so at base (V3).

There are also two minors: a resource temporary through a generic holder (V4), and a less clear W0601 text for closures together with a 'temporary' sentinel string.

Repros are in SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2c/repro/, and probes in the p/ directory next to it.

issues.finding: FD1 missed shape: an on abort function that calls a closure held in its value
issues.description: check_on_abort_rows reads only the inferred row of the on abort function. A call of a function value from the linear value (a field of type `fn()`, or an element of a `Vec<fn()>`) adds no effects and no mutations to that row. So the closure can perform a user effect through a handler inside the aborted body, fail, or change an rc group or an outer local, and W0118 is silent. These are the same faults FD1 was meant to close: no handler, a failure that escapes to main, and dangling references.
issues.repro:
Probes are in SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2c: effects, continuations, on abort and drops/p/. Each has 0 errors at HEAD. Run with `weft run --unchecked`, seeds 1 and 2, with the stock and the oracle interpreters:
- fd1_v14_fnfield_user_inner.wf (`linear struct T { f: fn() }`, `undo` calls `f`, closure `|| print(ask())` made inside an inner `handle Ask`): 'no handler for `Ask.ask` on this task'.
- fd1_v9_vecfn_inner.wf: same shape with a `Vec<fn()>` field, same fault.
- fd1_v13_fnfield_fail_inner.wf: the closure fails. The run ends 'failed: boom' and main has no `fail`.
- fd1_v15_closure_field_mut.wf: the closure pushes to an rc group. Oracle: 'access to a freed cell'.
- fd1_v16_closure_field_local.wf: the closure clears an outer local by reference. Oracle: 'access to a freed cell'.
issues.suggested_fix: Treat a call of a function value that the on abort function reaches through its parameter as an unknown call: W0118 unless the value's closures are known to be clean. A simpler option is to reject an on abort function that calls a function value from its parameter, or a linear type with on abort that holds a function value.

issues.finding: RR3/OR9 missed shape: a multi clause gives a resuming closure to the handled body through the resume value, and the body lets it escape
issues.description: The kcap check covers the clause value, the clause's stores and calls, and an outer local that the body assigns. It does not cover a body that returns the closure in the value of the handle, gives it to a callee that stores it, or runs it in a task. The op result carries no kcap, so these paths are not seen. There is a second, interpreter problem: a resume of a multi continuation whose clause has ended does not fault. copy_frames copies an empty frame list and deliver gives the resume argument back as the body's value. That is a type confusion.
issues.repro:
Probes are in SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2c: effects, continuations, on abort and drops/p/. Each has 0 errors at HEAD:
- rr3_v12_multi_value_fault.wf (`multi fn ask() -> fn() -> u64`, clause `let k = || { let (h, s) = resume(|| 7); h() + 1 }; resume(k)`, body `(ask(), "x")` returned from `make`, called in main): 'this value is not a tuple of that size' on every seed, in both interpreters.
- rr3_v13_multi_body_storing_callee.wf: the body calls `keep(h2.clone(), f)`, which stores into an Rc. Same fault.
- or9_v2_multi_body_task.wf: the body runs `f()` in `s.spawn`, and the rest of the body runs on that task. 'no handler for `Note.note` on this task' on every seed.
- rr3_v11_dbg.wf shows a silent no-op resume after the handle ends.
issues.suggested_fix: Give the op result the kcap of each clause that resumes with a value holding kcap. A simpler sound option is to forbid a resume argument that holds kcap. Then the existing W0313/W0314 checks apply to the handle value, stored values and tasks. In the interpreter, mark a multi record Dropped when its clause frame pops, so a later resume faults.

issues.finding: RR5 missed shapes: frees and changes in a callee of the handled body, and a resume through a closure or a callee
issues.description: inner_frees only sees moved_at and scope_end of nodes lowered in the handled body. (a) When the body calls a function that performs the operation with a reference to its own local, the clause parameter dangles after resume. (b) When the clause resumes through a closure (`let k = || resume(()); k()`) or through a callee (`call_it(|| resume(()))`), the frees and the mutations of the body do not reach the call node. Even the old RR5 mutation control (`clear` in the body) goes through without W0301 in that form.
issues.repro:
Probes are in SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2c: effects, continuations, on abort and drops/p/. Each has 0 errors at HEAD:
- rr5_v1_callee_local.wf (`fn helper() / Peek { let local = Entity{hp:1}; peek(&local) }`, clause `resume(()); print(e.hp)`): oracle reports 'a reference into a local whose scope ended is used (dangling)' on every seed.
- rr5_v7_callee_moves.wf: the callee clears and moves its Vec. Stock: 'a place does not exist'. Oracle: 'access to a freed cell'.
- rr5_v8_resume_in_closure.wf (via_closure, via_callee): the local of the body ends. Oracle: dangling.
- rr5_v9_closure_resume_frees.wf (moved_via_closure, cleared_via_closure_t, moved_via_callee): both interpreters fault, 'place does not exist' / 'access to a freed cell'.
issues.suggested_fix: (a) For an operation of a caller handler, or one performed in a callee of the body, treat a reference clause parameter as freed by every resume. (b) Carry the releases and mutations of a resume node into the summary of a closure that resumes, so that the call node of that closure invalidates them, as the direct resume node does.

issues.finding: OR6 missed shape: a place as the tail of a block whose value is discarded
issues.description: The fix covers only `StmtKind::Expr(e)` where e itself is a place. In `{ v }` as a statement, in a loop body `for i in 0..2 { v }`, and in `while c { i += 1; v }`, the interpreter compiles the block tail as a value: it moves the value and drops it. Sema sees no move. The decision says the tail of a block does move, but sema does not record that move here, so the checker and the interpreter still disagree.
issues.repro:
Probe: SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2c: effects, continuations, on abort and drops/p/or6_v2_block_tails.wf. It has 0 errors at HEAD and at base. Results on every seed:
- loop_tail, while_tail, block_stmt: 'a value is used after it was moved'.
- block_linear (`{ t }` then `commit(t)`): oracle reports a linear leak.
- block_dangling: stock 'a place does not exist', oracle 'access to a freed cell'.
issues.suggested_fix: Choose one meaning for a discarded block whose tail is a place, and use it on both sides. Either sema records the move and the drop (W0302/W0601), or the interpreter compiles a discarded block tail that is a local place as a place, as in the statement case.

issues.finding: IP4 missed shape: a closure in an rc object captures a local of the multi continuation
issues.description: copy_frames maps the clause cells of Frame::Handle, and closures in frame slots. A closure that sits inside an Rc object is shared by the copies, and it still points at the template's cell. So the first copy changes the template state, and the next resume starts from that changed state. The Phase 1 meaning in the ADR is that owned cells are copied and each resume starts from the captured state. This breaks it.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2c: effects, continuations, on abort and drops/p/ip4_v1_rc_closure.wf (`let count = 0; let h = Rc.new(H { f: || count += 1 }); let b = choose(); let g = h.f; g(); all.push(count)` under a handler that does `resume(true); resume(false)`). It prints [0, 1]. The Vec form (ip4_v2_vec_closure.wf) prints [1, 1].
issues.suggested_fix: Reject an rc object that holds a closure capturing a local of the handled body by reference when the closure is live across a multi operation (W0503). Or document this as a known difference and add an interpreter test.

issues.finding: FD4 missed shape: a !Move local that is live across a multi operation only through a reference
issues.description: once_var(V) :- immovable(V) works on uses of V. A !Move local `f` that is used after the operation only through `r = &f` or `&f.buf[1]` is not live_out, so W0503 is silent. The resume still copies f to a new address. In the copy, r points to that new address and the self-reference `cur` is remapped. That breaks the 'keeps its address' rule that FD4 cites. A !Move value inside a Box is copied in the same way. The interpreter does not fault here, because it remaps references.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2c: effects, continuations, on abort and drops/p/fd4_v6.wf (ref_immovable, ref_part): 0 errors at HEAD. Compare FD4_multi_immovable.wf, which gets W0503. boxed_immovable in fd4_v5.wf (Box<Frame> across choose) is also accepted.
issues.suggested_fix: Count a reference that points into an immovable variable as a use of that variable for live_across_multi, for example through points_into. Or record the Box case as a known gap in ADR 0007.

issues.finding: W0601 text for a closure that a generic function drops now says the closure type is linear
issues.description: The callee_drops change names the callee when the argument is a temporary. For a closure argument the message is now '`gen_drop` drops a value of the linear type `fn() -> ()`'. `fn() -> ()` is not a linear type. The closure is linear because it moves a linear value. The old text, 'a closure moves a linear value, but it can go out of scope without a call', explained the cause.
issues.repro: weft check tests/programs/71_closure_modes.wf, line 163: `gen_drop(|| rollback(tx))`. Base prints the closure message; HEAD prints the 'linear type `fn() -> ()`' message.
issues.suggested_fix: When the type of the dropped value is a function type, keep the closure wording, or say that the closure moves a linear value.

R2c: effects, continuations, on abort an.summary:
Gates pass at 3af6118: fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --workspace, cargo doc -D warnings, and verify-all (borrowing 169, effects 122, link 233, weft-verified 66, 0 errors). Every named repro of the 14 items behaves as the report says. No new false positives appear on the corpus, the examples, the interpreter programs or about 1,660 R2 probe files. On the 26,400 generated programs, only 3 new rejections appear; each is a deliberate scope-binder W0503. The 36 newly accepted programs run with the oracle with no memory fault.

The adversarial probes still found accepted programs that fault, in 4 items:
- FD1: an on abort function that calls a closure held in its value escapes W0118. Results: no handler, a failure that escapes main, dangling references.
- RR3/OR9: a multi clause gives a resuming closure to the body through the resume value. The body returns it in the handle value, stores it through a callee, or runs it in a task. Results: 'not a tuple of that size', 'no handler for Note.note'. The interpreter also lets a finished multi continuation be resumed: it gives back the resume argument.
- RR5: frees and changes are missed when the operation runs in a callee of the body, and when the clause resumes through a closure or a callee. Results: oracle freed-cell and dangling faults.
- OR6: a place as the tail of a discarded block (`{ v }`, loop and while bodies) still moves and drops in the interpreter but not in sema. Results: use after move, dangling, linear leak.

Majors:
- IP4: a closure in an Rc that captures a continuation local still points at the template cells (prints [0, 1]).
- FD4: a !Move local that is live across a multi operation only through a reference gets no W0503.

Minors: a W0601 message now calls `fn() -> ()` a linear type (71_closure_modes.wf:163), and design.md:212 does not mention spared_at.

The probes are in SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2c: effects, continuations, on abort and drops/p/. The scratch build dirs are deleted. The worktree is clean and unchanged.
