R2c: effects, continuations, on abort an.summary:
All 14 verifier findings on R2c are fixed in one commit, acd05a8, on review/s5 in /home/user/wt-core. I reproduced each one first: every verifier probe had 0 errors at HEAD except the parts that HEAD already caught. Each fix has bad and clean cases in tests/programs 120 and 122 to 125 and 127, and some also have sema, diagnostics or interpreter guard tests. All gates passed. cargo fmt --check and clippy -D warnings are clean. cargo test --workspace passes (41 binaries, 0 failed). cargo doc -D warnings is clean. Random agreement passed with PROPTEST_CASES=4000. proofs/verify-all.sh passes: borrowing 169, effects 122, link 235 and weft-verified 67 verified, 0 errors. I re-ran it because weft-verified and proofs/link changed.

Main changes: the spared_at regression is closed for closures and clauses. On abort functions now get W0118 for runtime failures (a new inferred EffectSig::raises part) and for unknown function values. A resume cannot give the handled body a resuming closure (W0313), and the interpreter ends a continuation when its clause ends, through the new verified Continuation::end and its link theorem end_linked. Resume frees reach clause parameters when the operation runs in a callee and when a closure or a callee runs the resume. A discarded block tail moves in sema, as the interpreter does. A !Move value in a Box, a reference or a reference argument into a !Move value, and an Rc to closures or references are not many. There are two new spec rules for live_across_multi, mirrored in rules.rs; there is no new input relation. The decisions are recorded in ADR 0003, 0005 and 0007, design.md, proofs/effects/README.md, proofs/link/README.md and the codes.rs texts.

A diagnostics scan over 27,559 R2 programs found no newly accepted and no newly rejected programs. The oracle build and the binary copy are deleted. The probes and scan scripts stay in SCRATCH/s5/.

R2d: tasks, scopes, fork and the schedul.summary:
I finished stage R2d in /home/user/wt-core (branch review/s5) as one commit, d593692, on top of acd05a8. I reproduced all 14 items before I changed them, and all 14 are fixed or documented as the task asked. The gates pass: fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --workspace (41 suites), and rustdoc -D warnings. I did not run verify-all.sh, because nothing in weft-verified or proofs changed.

The checker side has three new spec input relations, each in all the places of the 8-step checklist (except the sink field, because none is a new sink):
- kept(T, Rt): a task keeps the cell of a copy variable that it captures.
- opaque(T): a task runs code that the function cannot check.
- spawns_in(T, U): task U starts inside the code of task T.
New spec rules: the free rule of task_conflict excludes kept roots; pinned(T) :- opaque(T); pinned(T) :- spawns_in(T, U), pinned(U).
EffectSig has two new parts: task_runs (thread / twice / with) and pins. The new sema module is crates/weft-sema/src/body/tasks.rs. New corpus files are tests/programs/130 to 136. There are new interpreter programs, and new unit tests in sema and in the checker.

Side effects of the changes, in the corpus and in the oracle's generated programs:
- Corpus: 111 and 117 now mark an extra W0405 that is a real race (a new value of r while a task reads r). 38_callbacks via_foreign gets W0405, because foreign code can run the closure on two threads at one time. 40_library_values uses the new 3-parameter sim.run.
- Scan of the 8459 programs that the oracle accepted: 35 now get W0405. 28 of them race in the HEAD oracle. The other 7 are uncalled functions with the same race shape, so all 35 are true positives.
- The same scan: 14 programs now get W0102. In each one an if branch or a unit closure ends with a fork that gives a tuple, which follows the IP6 decision.
- All 62 programs that the oracle found unsound before are now rejected or run cleanly. The one exception is p972, which is an endless recursion.

Imprecisions in the worst-case handling of closures, unknown values and foreign code, and in held fields, are recorded in ADR 0006. The scratch builds (inst, harness, tmp) are deleted.

findings.evidence: R2/oracle/repro/OR8_task_whole_local.wf now gives W0405 at lines 16 (print(count)), 24 (count += 5), 32 (print(v)) and 41 (r = &v[1]). tests/programs/130_task_locals.wf has 9 bad cases (also a fork, a whole struct, a ref rebind in a task, and a call of f while a task sets it) and 5 clean cases (both read, two fields, two fields through a ref, after a join, loop and let variables). The HEAD oracle reports a race on each bad case and none on the clean cases.
findings.notes: name() reads the variable place (Lower::var_place). A reference local gets a cell root with no owner (Local::cell). Assignment writes the place, and a place through a ref local reads the cell. A new input relation kept(T, Rt) keeps the end of a captured copy variable from being a free for the task. Without it, loop and let captures and 67_task_starts would get false positives. Moved (by-value) captures are left out of the task footprint. ADR 0003 and ADR 0006 record this.

findings.evidence: R2/oracle/repro/OR5_borrow_during_task.wf: W0405 at 15:9 and 26:9 (the &v[i] borrow), W0301 at 17:15 and 28:11 (print(r + 1)). tests/programs/131_task_ends.wf covers a join, a scope end, a fork and an abort path, plus two clean cases.
findings.notes: A TASK_END node follows each join, fork join, scope end and abort node. It gets lends_mut of the task's writes at the end of lowering (finish_task_ends). An index reads its base place. The W0301 and W0405 texts for task-end nodes are adjusted. ADR 0006 has the new wording in place of 'A spawn is a mutation at the spawn node'.

findings.evidence: R2/oracle/repro/OR7_tasks_of_fn_params.wf: W0403x2 and W0405x2 at par(...) on line 31, W0405 at bg(...) on 37 and at bg_and_call(...) on 43. In stealable_rc the runtime spawn in bg_one is pinned (harness trace). tests/programs/133_task_params.wf has 15 bad shapes: fork, spawn twice, spawn+call, loop, task+call, pass-on, Rc in a fork, a closure callee, an unknown value, an item value, a returned closure, a field, a field passed on, and foreign field. It also has 3 clean shapes; the clean case joined_first proves that with() is precise across a join. The oracle shows a race on every bad function. tests/programs/134_steal_pins.wf marks bg_one's s.spawn(f) as pinned. There is a sema unit test for task_runs.
findings.notes: EffectSig.task_runs: BTreeMap<param, TaskRun{thread, twice, with}>. It is computed from the CFG active sets of the tasks and from the nodes where params run. At each call, arg_tasks makes stand-in tasks after the call node: a fork kind when thread, a second start when twice, and reads of the footprint of each concurrent argument. Closures whose task runs their parameter, unknown values and foreign code use the worst case. A closure parameter with an unknown type is treated as a possible function parameter. ADR 0006 records the decision.

findings.evidence: R2/redteam/repro/RR4_scope_escape.wf: W0301 at 22 (escape), 25 (as_value, at the let that takes the scope value), and 33+34 (as_field). tests/programs/132_scope_escape.wf has 3 bad cases and 2 clean cases; its main runs.
findings.notes: A closure that captures a Scope-typed local points into the root of that local. Recorded in ADR 0003.

findings.evidence: The harness at HEAD on ip_steal_shares_rc.wf with --workers 4, seeds 1 to 8: 'spawn t1 from t0 on w0 (pinned)', 'spawn t2 ... (pinned)', 0 steals. Before the fix, seeds 2 and 3 showed 'steal t1 w2 -> w0'. tests/programs/134_steal_pins.wf has //~ pinned on the outer spawn, on a task that calls a pinning helper, and on a task that gives a callee a closure with an Rc. Plain cases stay //~ stealable.
findings.notes: pinned(T) :- spawns_in(T, U), pinned(U) and pinned(T) :- opaque(T). The EffectSig pins part covers pinned tasks inside callees. A task that only runs a function param does not set pins, because the caller checks that value.

findings.evidence: Harness with --http 2 on ip_http_pinned.wf: 'spawn t1 from t0 on w0 (pinned)' and 'spawn t2 ... (pinned)', no steal. A handler with no Rc is stealable and is stolen. New test request_task_of_a_nonportable_handler_is_pinned in crates/weft-interp/tests/http.rs.
findings.notes: Op::MakeClosure and ClosureVal carry the span of the closure expression. http_poll lets a request task move only if the checker marks the handler closure (its stand-in task at the serve call) stealable. Otherwise the task stays on the server's worker. ADR 0010 records this.

findings.evidence: ip_fork_generic_unit.wf: 0 errors, prints 3|x|y|units. ip_fork_unit.wf: 0 errors, prints left|right|joined. New interpreter program fork_unit.wf with .out.
findings.notes: Sema types fork as Ty::Tuple(rets), and fork_step always delivers a tuple. A unit function can still end with fork. ADR 0010 notes that an if branch or a unit closure must use let _ = fork(...). 14 oracle-generated programs now get W0102 for that reason.

findings.evidence: Repros with the resume removed, seeds 0 to 5 and workers 1, 2, 4: 'main handler: child failed' (twice) and 'outer handler: child failed', never 'scope returned normally'. Interpreter program child_fail_lexical.wf also covers the case where the scope frame is in the continuation of a clause outside the scope: 'clause done', then 'scope handler: child failed'. semantics.rs child_failure_goes_to_the_handlers_of_the_scope sweeps the seeds.
findings.notes: ScopeRec.henv holds the handlers at the scope or fork. Interrupt::Fail{msg, scope} leads to scope_fail_unwind, which unwinds the frames from the Scope/Fork frame and then performs fail with the scope's handlers. If the frame is away, the owner is not woken; the failure is raised when the frame is back or at the scope end. check_interrupt, sleep_for, yield_now and blocking_call are now infallible.

findings.evidence: ip_timeout_lost.wf prints 'caught: timeout|end|'. ip_multi_timeout.wf prints 'fast|caught timeout|end|' on seeds 0 to 2. The control ip_timeout_ctl.wf is unchanged. New interpreter program timeout_continuation.wf with .out.
findings.notes: Machine.expired keeps the timeouts whose deadline passed while their frame was away. check_interrupt fires them when the frame is back on the stack. copy_list gives each multi copy of a Timeout frame a new id and timer with the same deadline (copy_timeout).

findings.evidence: ip_sim_determinism.wf with seed 1 and workers 1, 2, 8 (and seeds 2, 3) gives one order: 'task 3 step 0 task 1 step 0 task 2 step 0 ...'. The new determinism test simulation_order_does_not_depend_on_the_run sweeps seeds and workers over sim_workers.wf. tests/programs/135_sim_args.wf checks the sim.run arguments (W0103).
findings.notes: Each simulation has its own SimState with its own scheduler RNG and simulated worker queues (workers argument, default SIM_WORKERS = 4). A ready simulation is one choice of the machine scheduler, and the simulation's own RNG then picks the task. The prelude is now sim.run(seed, workers, body); the compiler fills in the default for workers. ADR 0010 records this.

findings.evidence: ip_clock_outside_sim.wf: the outside task reads 12ms and then 20ms (before: 7ms). ip_clause_outside_sim.wf: the clause reads 15ms (before: 5ms). New interpreter program sim_lexical.wf with .out.
findings.notes: sim_of(task) is the nearest Sim frame on the task stack (also inside an unwinding), else the simulation of the task's spawn site (Task.sim). The clock, randomness, run queue and partition all use it. ADR 0010 records this.

findings.evidence: ADR 0010 now says that Phase 1 does not simulate the network: sim.net.partition and sim.net.heal only record the partition in the trace, and http.serve binds a real socket. The comment in crates/weft-interp/tests/programs/sim.wf says the same.
findings.notes: No behavior change, as the task asked.

findings.evidence: tests/programs/136_call_reads.wf keeps the OR10 shape (helper_part, W0405 marked as the documented imprecision). The HEAD oracle runs it cleanly. field_part is a clean control.
findings.notes: ADR 0006 'What stays imprecise' records that a call reads all of its reference arguments, and that a read part in signatures would fix it. No code change.

findings.evidence: FD11_shared_not_required.wf stays accepted (0 errors). tests/programs/136_call_reads.wf fn both pins the case: two fork branches read through an aliased reference that is not @ shared.
findings.notes: ADR 0006 now says that reads from several threads need no @ shared, because W0403 and W0405 cover writes. ADR 0003 now says that Phase 1 has no globals as place roots.

design_decisions: New spec input relations kept(T, Rt), opaque(T) and spawns_in(T, U), mirrored in rules.rs, bridge.rs, weft-facts (mark, rewind, normalize) and agreement_random. The free rule of task_conflict excludes kept roots. pinned(T) :- opaque(T) and pinned(T) :- spawns_in(T, U), pinned(U).

A reference local has a cell root with no owner (Local::cell). A use of a local as a value, or a call of a closure local, reads its variable place. x = v and x += v write it. A let or loop variable is a new variable and writes nothing.

Task ends: a TASK_END node follows each join, fork join, scope end and aborted scope. It gets lends_mut of the task's writes, not mutates_at, so W0702 and W0402 errors are not repeated. Diagnostics give it its own text.

Signature parts: task_runs (TaskRun{thread, twice, with}) and pins. Stand-in tasks at a call have the span of the argument. They feed W0401, W0403, W0405 and IP3 pinning, and the interpreter uses them only for http.serve handler closures.

Worst case (thread, twice, with all) for a closure whose task runs its parameter, a function value the body does not know, and foreign code. http.serve: spawn, twice. A held field value can be any value that the body stores (held_run).
A fork always gives a tuple. if branches and unit closures follow the general rule for values (let _ = fork(...)).
sim.run(seed, workers = 4): each simulation has its own scheduler and queues; the simulation is the nearest Sim frame of the task or that of its spawn site. The network is not simulated in Phase 1.
A child failure goes to ScopeRec.henv through an unwind to the scope frame. If the frame is in a continuation, the failure waits until the frame is back or until the scope end.

issues.finding: kept(T, Rt) regression: the checker accepts a task that borrows a captured copy variable and uses the reference after the variable ends
issues.description: The new free rule `!kept(T, M)` drops the W0405 free conflict whenever task T captures a copy variable. kept_roots (crates/weft-sema/src/body/tasks.rs) leaves a variable out of kept only if a captured variable or part holder already holds a reference into it when the task is made. It does not see a reference that the task makes itself (`let r = &n`, `&c.k`, or `&n` passed to a callee that keeps it across a suspension). ADR 0006 says 'A reference into the variable that the task holds is still invalid after it'. The checker no longer enforces this. Base acd05a8 rejected all four shapes with W0405 ('frees `n` while a task reads `n`'). HEAD accepts them. The oracle reports 'a reference into a local whose scope ended is used (dangling)' on every seed. The copy-value control (task_value) is still accepted, and the oracle runs it cleanly.
issues.repro: P='SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2d: tasks, scopes, fork and the scheduler/p'; weft check "$P/kept4.wf": HEAD reports only via_closure (base: 5 errors). Shapes: task_ref `{ let n = 5; s.spawn(|| { let r = &n; sleep(1.ms); print(r) }) }`, via_callee `s.spawn(|| show_later(&n))`, struct_field `&c.k`, and loop_ref (a per-iteration `let k`). Each one run alone with the oracle (run --unchecked, seeds 1-3, workers 2) gives ORACLE dangling. Also kept3.wf task_makes_ref_then_body_ends.
issues.suggested_fix: Emit kept(T, Rt) only when the task code makes no reference into Rt: no borrow of the variable or of a part of it, and no lend of it to a callee or to a function value. Or keep the free conflict for the places that the task borrows. Add these shapes as bad cases to tests/programs/130 or 34 (the corpus has no bad case at the kept boundary where the task makes the reference itself).

issues.finding: OR7 missed shape: a callee that keeps a function parameter in a local container or tuple runs it as a task with no W0405 or W0401 at the caller, and the task is stealable
issues.description: opaque and task_runs come from sum.params, passthrough and held. A function value read back from a local Vec, tuple or Vec of structs (`fs.push(f); let g = fs[0]; g()`, `let t = (f, 1); t.0`, `js.push(Job { f: f })`) loses its parameter identity, and it is not marked unknown either. So (a) the task that runs it is marked stealable, (b) the callee gets no task_runs entry, so the caller checks nothing. Direct forms (`s.spawn(f)`, a field of a local struct, a Vec<fn()> parameter) are handled. This is unsound for the race and for the mode rule. The harness shows the Rc-holding task stolen to another worker while main holds the Rc.
issues.repro: P=.../verify/s5/R2d: tasks, scopes, fork and the scheduler/p. or7_race_vec.wf: weft check gives 0 errors. Oracle on seeds 1-3, workers 4: race_vec and race_tuple give 'ORACLE data race: task 1 writes cell 0 ... task 2 wrote'. rc_fork (fork branch runs an Rc closure from fs[0]) gives 'a stealable task reaches a nonportable value (Rc)'. or7_steal.wf: the marks put line 7 at 'Spawn stealable'. The harness trace with --workers 4 shows 'steal t1 w0 -> w3' on seeds 1-6. or7_pin2.wf: via_tuple and via_vec_jobs are stealable, and the oracle flags the Rc.
issues.suggested_fix: Let an element or field read from a local that holds a function parameter carry the parameter (like held / part_holders for fields), or treat a function value from a container as one that the body does not know: the worst-case TaskRun, and opaque for the task. Add these shapes to tests/programs/133 and 134.

issues.finding: OR7 missed shape: an operation's function argument that a handler clause runs as a task or fork branch gets no W0405 or W0403 at the perform
issues.description: The clause parameter of an operation is a function value that the clause can spawn or fork. This is the same root cause as OR7, but the task_runs part exists only for function signatures. The perform site and the local handler do not check the argument as a task. These programs are accepted at base and at HEAD, and they race in the oracle. W0314's text already says 'A clause can run a function argument of its operation as a task'. Pinning is handled (clause_spawn_rc is pinned).
issues.repro: P=.../verify/s5/R2d: tasks, scopes, fork and the scheduler/p. or7_v3.wf: clause_twice (`handle Run { fn run(f) { scope { s => s.spawn(f); s.spawn(f); () }; resume(()) } } in { run(|| n += 1) }`), clause_fork (`fork(f, g)` in a clause over `run2(|| n += 1, || n += 2)`), and clause_spawn_resume (the clause spawns f into an outer scope and resumes, then the body prints n). or7_clause.wf caller_handles: the handler is in the caller and the perform is in the callee uses_run. weft check gives 0 errors for each. The oracle (seeds 1-3) gives 'ORACLE data race' on every seed.
issues.suggested_fix: Give operations (or local clauses) a task_runs view of their function parameters, computed from the clause bodies. At a perform whose handler is known, or with the worst case for an unknown handler, call arg_tasks for the function arguments. Add bad and clean cases to the corpus.

issues.finding: Interpreter crash: a stale Interrupt::Fail of a scope dropped with its continuation leads to 'internal: the operand stack is empty'
issues.description: A child fails while the frame of its scope is in a continuation. scope_fail_unwind (effects.rs) re-arms Interrupt::Fail{scope} at each suspension point until the frame is back. If the clause drops the continuation, the frame never comes back. The interrupt stays for good, and the failure is lost (base printed 'h1: first'). Later a child of another scope fails. fail-child propagation sees interrupt.is_some(), so it does not record the new failure, but it still wakes the blocked owner with no value. check_interrupt takes the stale interrupt, re-arms it and returns None. The sleep then resumes with no value, and the machine faults. The checker accepts the program.
issues.repro: weft run '.../verify/s5/R2d: tasks, scopes, fork and the scheduler/p/ip2_stale.wf' (seeds 0-2, workers 1 and 4) gives 'first gave 0' and then 'error: runtime error: internal: the operand stack is empty' at the sleep(50.ms) of second(), line 23. Base gives 'h1: first|h2: second|end'. second() alone runs correctly.
issues.suggested_fix: When the frames of a scope or fork are unwound or dropped (for example with an aborted continuation), clear the pending Interrupt::Fail for that scope, or decide and document what happens to the failure. Keep several pending failures (do not drop a new one because an old one is set). Never wake the owner unless the interrupt it will find is its own. Add an interpreter program for this shape.

issues.finding: IP9 incomplete: the order inside sim.run still depends on --seed and --workers when the task that enters the simulation is not on machine worker 0
issues.description: spawn_task gives a child the machine worker index of its parent (self.task().worker), and enqueue maps it to simulated worker w % n. A task that enters sim.run on machine worker 1 (for example a spawned or stolen task) puts the children of the simulation on another simulated queue than a run with --workers 1 does. So the order inside sim.run(seed: 3) changes with the outer seed and worker count, and a failing seed does not replay. The ADR 0010 claim ('the order inside it depends only on its seed and its workers') does not hold. The single-sim repro and the new tests pass only because the test task starts on worker 0. Two simulations at one time show the same defect.
issues.repro: P=.../verify/s5/R2d: tasks, scopes, fork and the scheduler/p. ip9_d.wf (sim.run inside o.spawn): `weft test --seed 3 --workers 1` gives 'sim 3 step 0|sim 2 step 0|sim 1 step 0|...', and `--seed 3 --workers 2` (also 4 and 8) gives 'sim 1 step 0|sim 2 step 0|sim 3 step 0|...'. The harness trace shows 'steal t1 w0 -> w1', then 'spawn t3 from t1 on w1'. ip9_c.wf: two simulations with seed 3 each give 2 orders over seeds 1/2/5 and workers 1/2/3/8.
issues.suggested_fix: On entry to sim.run, put the entering task on simulated worker 0 (store a simulated worker per task while it is in the simulation, separate from the machine worker). Give children of simulation tasks a simulated worker that the simulation chooses. Add a determinism test with sim.run inside a spawned task, and one with two simulations at one time.

issues.finding: New W0405 false positive at the task-end node of a task that starts another task in the same scope
issues.description: finish_task_ends gives the TASK_END node lends_mut of all task_writes of the task. The writes of a task include the writes of a task that it starts into the outer scope. That task can outlive the join. At the join of a, task b is still active and touches the same place, so task_conflict fires. The program has no race and no other conflict. Base accepted it, and the oracle runs it cleanly. This contradicts the ADR 0006 imprecision note, 'The first conflict of the two tasks is already an error'.
issues.repro: P=.../verify/s5/R2d: tasks, scopes, fork and the scheduler/p/or5_fp2.wf nested_join: `let v = mk_v(); scope { s => let a = s.spawn(|| { s.spawn(|| v.push(2)); () }); a.join(); print(1) }; print(v.len())` gives 'error[W0405]: this code waits for a task that can change `v` while a task reads `v`' at 13:9 (a.join()). Base: 0 errors. Oracle: clean on seeds 1-3. The other three clean shapes in the file stay clean.
issues.suggested_fix: At the end of task a, lend only the writes that a makes itself. Leave out the writes of the tasks in spawns_in(a, u) that have their own active range in the parent's facts, or skip the conflict with a task u where spawns_in(a, u). Add this clean case to tests/programs/131 and correct the ADR 0006 imprecision sentence.

issues.finding: IP5: a with_timeout block whose deadline passed in a continuation still finishes normally if it does not suspend after the resume
issues.description: The expired deadline is checked only at the next suspension point (check_interrupt). A block that returns right after the resume gives its value after its deadline. On the normal path, a wake after the deadline times out at once. ADR 0010 states 'at its next suspension point', so this is documented, but it differs from the wake semantics. Nested, never-resumed and in-time variants behave correctly.
issues.repro: '.../verify/s5/R2d: tasks, scopes, fork and the scheduler/p/ip5_a.wf' no_suspend_after (the clause sleeps 50 ms, deadline 10 ms, the block prints and returns x after the resume) prints 'block finished after its deadline|v = 1' on every seed.
issues.suggested_fix: Check `expired` when a resume puts a Timeout frame back on the stack (time out at the resume), or state in ADR 0010 that a block with no later suspension point keeps its value.

issues.finding: Foreign callbacks that write through their reference parameters are now always W0405, and closures that write captured locals are W0403
issues.description: callee_task_runs treats every extern fn as running each function argument on another thread, twice at one time, and with every other argument. So `foreign_apply(|x| x.entities.push(..), world)` in tests/programs/38_callbacks.wf changed from accepted to W0405. Each foreign API with a mutating callback is now rejected, and the program cannot declare that a callback runs one at a time. This is sound and documented in ADR 0006, but it changes an existing corpus expectation.
issues.repro: weft check tests/programs/38_callbacks.wf: the new W0405 is at 43:5 (base: no error on that line).
issues.suggested_fix: Accept this as the decision, or let an extern signature state its task_runs (for example sequential callbacks).

issues.finding: docs/design.md still says sim replaces the network
issues.description: IP11 updated ADR 0010 and the sim.wf comment. docs/design.md line 319 still says 'The test harness can replace every root handler at once: clock, network, randomness and the scheduler.' The task asked only for ADR 0010 and sim.wf, so this is an inconsistency, not a missed step.

issues.finding: http handler stealability is keyed only by the (lo, hi) span, with no unit
issues.description: http_poll calls rt.is_stealable(c.span) for the closure expression. stealable_spans keeps (lo, hi) of root-unit tasks only, and Span has no file id. A handler closure from another unit (module file) whose byte offsets equal those of a stealable root-unit task would count as stealable. This already applied to spawn sites. issues.repro: Reasoning only: crates/weft-interp/src/lib.rs stealable_spans and machine/http.rs line ~224.

issues.finding: kept(T, Rt) regression: a reference that the task itself makes into a kept copy variable is accepted after the variable ends
issues.description: kept_roots (crates/weft-sema/src/body/tasks.rs) drops a captured copy variable from the free rule of task_conflict whenever no captured local holds a reference into it. It does not look at references that the task body makes into the variable (`&x`, `&p.a`, `show(&x)`), before or after the end. ADR 0003 says that a reference into a plain-data local is still invalid after its scope. The base commit acd05a8 rejected all four shapes below with W0405 ('this code frees `x` while a task reads `x`'). HEAD accepts them, and the oracle reports 'a reference into a local whose scope ended is used (dangling)' on every seed. The 27k-program diff missed this because no generated program has the shape. No corpus file has a bad case for kept: 130 has only clean loop and let cases.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2d/p/d4_kept_ref_in_task.wf (ref_after_end, ref_to_callee, ref_across_end, ref_in_loop). HEAD: 0 errors. acd05a8: 4x W0405. R2/triage/verify.sh with the HEAD oracle: 'dangling' for each function.
issues.suggested_fix: A task keeps the variable only if its body makes no reference into it: also exclude roots that the closure summary borrows (or places that it reads through a reference that it makes). Or keep the free rule and make the end of the variable invalidate references into it for the task. Add a bad case to tests/programs/130.

issues.finding: OR7 missed shape: a callee writes or reads a non-function argument while it runs a function parameter as a task
issues.description: task_runs records only thread, twice and `with` (other function parameters). If a callee spawns `f` and, while that task runs, writes (or reads) through a reference or Rc argument that the closure argument also uses, the caller does not check it. The stand-in task starts after the call node, so the callee's own mutations at the call node never overlap it. W0312 does not fire for copy captures, because a closure does not point into a copy capture. The oracle reports a race on every seed.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2d/p/a1_callee_writes_ref.wf (writer_param: `bg_write(|| print(n), &n)`, where bg_write spawns f and then does `x += 1`) and p/a2_variants.wf (two_tasks: a second task of the callee writes x; struct_write: the callee writes p.a while f reads p.a). HEAD: no error for these functions. Oracle: 'task 1 reads cell 0 ..., task 0 wrote ... with no join between'.
issues.suggested_fix: Let the task_runs part also record which reference and rc parameters the body (or another task) reads or writes while the task runs (the places, in callee roots). At the call, make the stand-in task's active nodes access the substituted argument places, as is done for `with`.

issues.finding: OR7 missed shape: a held function value in a struct that a callee returns is not in held_run
issues.description: held_run builds the stand-in for an argument that holds function values from `self.escaped`, the function values that this body stores. A struct that holds a closure and comes from a callee's return value (`let j = make_job(&n); bg_job(j)` or `bg_job(make_job(&n))`) is not covered. The callee bg_job spawns j.f twice, and the race is not reported. The closure-only form via_made_fn is caught.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2d/p/h3_held_returned.wf (via_made_job) and p/h4_held_variants.wf (job_local, job_direct). HEAD: 0 errors for these functions. Oracle: a race on every seed.
issues.suggested_fix: For a held argument, also take the function values that the argument's places can hold from callee returns (the ret part and its fn_stores), or use the worst case (an unknown footprint over every place that the argument reaches) when the holder came from a call.

issues.finding: RR4 missed shapes: the scope capability in a tuple or an Option
issues.description: The fix in expr.rs makes a closure point into a capture's root only when the capture's type is exactly Ty::Scope. A closure that captures `t = (s, 1)` or `o = Some(s)`, takes s out, and spawns can leave the scope with no error. Its call after the scope starts a task that no scope joins. The stock interpreter prints 'task runs 1' after the caller's local ended, and the oracle reports a dangling reference. A Vec of such closures and a struct field are caught.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2d/p/e3_rr4_tuple_option.wf: `weft check` gives 0 errors. `run --unchecked` prints 'task runs 1' twice. The oracle reports 'a reference into a local whose scope ended is used (dangling)' at 11:28 (in_tuple) and 21:67 (in_option).
issues.suggested_fix: Use a 'type holds a Scope' test (tuple, enum payload, struct field, recursively) instead of `matches!(ty, Ty::Scope)`. Add tuple and Option cases to tests/programs/132.

issues.finding: IP2 regression: the interpreter fails with 'internal: the operand stack is empty' when a pending child failure is stale
issues.description: scope_fail_unwind puts Interrupt::Fail back on the task while the Scope frame is away (in a continuation). The interrupt is never cleared if the frame does not come back (the clause does not resume), and it still blocks a new failure while the frame is away and the owner waits in another scope. A child of a second scope then fails. The child-failure path does not set the interrupt (interrupt.is_some()), but it still wakes the blocked owner (`on_stack && Blocked`). check_interrupt takes the stale Fail, finds no frame and gives None, so the owner resumes with no value and no flow. Base acd05a8 runs both programs (with the old wrong-handler behaviour). HEAD crashes on every seed and worker count. ADR 0010 does not say what happens to a pending failure when the frame of the scope goes away with a continuation.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2d/p/j4.wf (the clause does not resume, then a second scope's child fails while the owner sleeps) and p/j5_pending_fail_clause_scope.wf (the clause resumes and has its own scope B whose child fails). `weft run FILE --seed S --workers W` for S in 0..3 and W in 1,2,4 gives 'error: runtime error: internal: the operand stack is empty' at 13:13 and 12:21.
issues.suggested_fix: Clear a pending Interrupt::Fail{scope} when that Scope or Fork frame is unwound or dropped (also in a dropped continuation). Keep pending failures per scope, not in the one interrupt slot. Wake the owner only when its interrupt was set for this scope. Add both programs to crates/weft-interp/tests/programs and record the dropped-continuation case in ADR 0010.

issues.finding: OR5-adjacent: a borrow through an unstable deref (Box) while a task writes the Box is not an access
issues.description: Since OR5, an index borrow `&v[i]` reads the indexed place. A borrow `&b.items` through `Box` (deref: unstable) does not read b, but the oracle reports a race on the read of the pointer. A later use of the reference is still caught: W0405 while the task runs, W0301 after the join (c1_or5_shapes.wf). So the gap only covers the borrow itself.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2d/p/c2_box_borrow_nouse.wf: 0 errors. Oracle: 'task 1 writes cell 4 ... path [], task 0 read path [] with no join between'.
issues.suggested_fix: Make a borrow through an unstable deref step read the place of the pointer, as for an index, or record in ADR 0006 that only an index borrow is a read.

issues.finding: IP9 incomplete: the order inside sim.run depends on --seed and --workers when sim.run runs in a spawned task
issues.description: enqueue puts a child of the simulation in sim queue `w % n`, where w is the machine worker of the task that spawns it. When sim.run is called from a spawned task, that worker index comes from the outer schedule. So the order inside the simulation changes with --seed and --workers, and a failing seed does not replay. ADR 0010 says that the order depends only on the seed and workers of sim.run. At the root (k3_sim_root_sibling.wf) the order is fixed.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2d/p/k2_sim_in_task.wf: `weft test FILE --seed S --workers W` for S in 1,2,3,9,11,42 and W in 1,3,8 gives 3 different orders.
issues.suggested_fix: When a task enters sim.run, give it simulated worker 0 (or a worker that the sim RNG picks), and place the children of a simulation by simulation state only.

issues.finding: IP7 over-pins: a function-item handler of http.serve is always pinned
issues.description: http_poll makes a request task stealable only for a Value::Closure whose span the checker marked stealable. A function-item handler, as in docs/design.md and tests/programs/06_http.wf (`http.serve(l, handle)`), captures nothing and is portable. Its request tasks are now always pinned (at base they were stealable). This changes only performance, not soundness.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2d/p/g3_http_item.wf with the trace harness, --http 127.0.0.1:18439 3: 'spawn t1 from t0 on w0 (pinned)' for each request.

R2d: tasks, scopes, fork and the schedul.summary:
R2d (d593692 on top of acd05a8) passes every gate: cargo fmt --check, clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings (the workspace lints include pedantic and nursery), cargo test --workspace, and rustdoc -D warnings. The diff does not touch weft-verified or proofs, so verify-all.sh does not apply. I found no unwrap or expect in the production code that the diff adds.

All 14 listed repros behave as claimed. A base-vs-HEAD checker diff over 27,366 R2 programs found no new false positives, with each new W0405 checked against the oracle.

I found 5 blockers:
1. The new kept relation brings back unsoundness. A reference that the task makes into a kept copy variable after (or across) its end is now accepted: base rejected it with W0405, and the oracle reports a dangling reference. Corpus 130 has no bad case for kept.
2. OR7 misses the callee's own reads and writes of non-function reference or Rc arguments while it runs a function parameter as a task.
3. OR7 misses held function values in a struct that a callee returns.
4. RR4 misses a scope capability inside a tuple or an Option.
5. The IP2 change brings in an interpreter crash: 'internal: the operand stack is empty'. A stale Interrupt::Fail stays on the task, and a later child failure wakes the owner with no interrupt. The crash happens on every seed. Base runs these programs.

Minor issues: a Box-deref borrow is not a read, sim.run in a spawned task is not deterministic, fn-item http handlers are always pinned, and docs/design.md contradicts the FD11 note.

The repros are in SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2d/p/ and the diff results are in .../R2d/diff/. I deleted the scratch builds (inst, base, harness). I did not edit the worktree.

resolved: kept(T,Rt) regression (both reports): kept_roots now leaves out a copy variable that the task code borrows. The checks are a variable that gets a value in the task's node range and points into the variable, a call_arg there, and the closure's ret_refs. kept4 and d4 (task_ref, via_callee, struct_field, loop_ref, ref_across_end, ref_in_loop) give W0405 again, and task_value stays clean. Corpus 130 has 4 bad cases and 1 clean case. ADR 0006 is updated.

OR7 containers: task code that calls a value the body does not know (from a local Vec, tuple or Vec of structs) counts the param_nodes in its node range as parameters it runs, and caller_runs there make it opaque. race_vec and race_tuple give W0405, rc_fork gives W0401, and via_vec, via_tuple, via_vec_spawn and via_vec_jobs are now opaque and pinned. Corpus 137 has these cases, corpus 134 marks bg_vec and bg_tuple //~ pinned, and there is a sema unit test.

OR7 clauses: a clause function parameter is now the join of the op_fn_args that the operations give (Lower::clause_fns, used in value_summary, add_fn and apply_value). Clause tasks and fork branches therefore have real footprints and captures: clause_twice W0405, clause_fork W0403 and W0405, clause_spawn_resume W0405, clause_fork_rc W0401. A perform to a handler of a caller runs its function arguments in the worst way (worst_runs plus arg_tasks), so caller_handles gives W0405 at the perform in uses_run.

OR7 callee accesses: TaskRun gains writes and reads (SigPlaces of the parameters). They hold what the body and its overlapping tasks access at the nodes where the task is active. At the call, run_access substitutes the argument places, and an ARG_TASK node lends and reads them while the stand-in runs. Unknown and foreign callees and caller clauses lend all reference arguments. writer_param, two_tasks and struct_write give W0405, and bg_other (another field) and bg_first (write before the spawn) stay clean. W0405 has its own text for these nodes. There is a sema unit test.

OR7 held value returned by a callee: a call result that holds function values from a callee with a body gets a new caps::MADE mark. held_run then lends and reads the argument's refs. via_made_job, job_local and job_direct give W0405, and read_job (a literal closure that only reads) stays clean.

RR4 tuple/Option: the capture rule uses ty_has(Prop::Resource) instead of matches!(Ty::Scope). in_tuple and in_option give W0301. Corpus 132 has 2 bad cases and 1 clean case (tuple_inside), and ADR 0003 is updated.

IP2 stale Interrupt::Fail crash: Interrupt::Fail is removed. A failure stays in ScopeRec, and check_interrupt raises the outermost scope on the stack whose failure has not been raised. The owner is woken only if it is blocked, not aborting, and the scope frame is on its stack with a failure that has not been raised. ip2_stale, j4 and j5 run with no fault on seeds 0-3 and workers 1/2/4 ('dropped gave 0', 'h2: second', and so on). The new interpreter program is child_fail_dropped.wf. ADR 0010 records that a failure goes away when an abort unwinds its scope.

IP9 sim order: each Task has a sim_worker, apart from its machine worker. sim.run puts the entering task on simulated worker 0 and gives back the outer one at the end (Frame::Sim.outer). A child starts on the sim_worker of its parent. k2, ip9_d and the per-sim order of ip9_c no longer depend on --seed or --workers. sim_workers.wf has two new tests (a sim in a spawned task, two sims at one time), and determinism.rs sweeps them. ADR 0010 is updated.

W0405 false positive at a nested join: finish_task_ends leaves out the writes of a task that the ended task starts, if that task is still active at the end node. or5_fp2 nested_join is clean. Corpus 131 has the clean nested_join and the bad nested_join_writes and nested_joined. The ADR 0006 imprecision sentence is corrected.

IP5 no_suspend_after (minor): a resume that puts back a Timeout frame whose deadline passed times out at once (late_timeout). ip5_a prints 'caught: timeout' for no_suspend_after and nested. timeout_continuation.wf has the new case and a clean in_time case, and ADR 0010 is updated.
IP7 function item handler (minor): a FnItem handler of http.serve is stealable when sigs[f].effects.pins is false. There is a new http test with a clean item and a pinning item.

Span key without unit (minor): the stealable set is keyed by (unit, lo, hi). Code carries its unit, and spawn uses the unit of the spawning code frame. Tasks of every unit are now included. A new units.rs test runs a package whose root and dependency closures have equal byte offsets: the root task is stealable and the dependency task is pinned.
docs/design.md (both minors): the sentence about data seen by several threads now says writes need shared and reads do not, and the network sentence says Phase 1 does not simulate the network.
Foreign callbacks W0405 in 38_callbacks (minor): kept as a decision and recorded in the ADR 0006 imprecisions (an extern signature cannot state that it runs callbacks one at a time).
Box borrow (minor): recorded in ADR 0006 that only an index borrow reads the place it goes through (see not_resolved for why there is no code change).

not_resolved.issue: Box borrow with no use (c2_box_borrow_nouse.wf): a borrow &b.items through an unstable Box deref does not read b
not_resolved.reason: If the borrow read the Box place b, it would overlap every place inside the box. Then a task that writes b.items while the parent reads b.other would get a new false W0405. A later use of the reference is still caught (W0405 while the task runs, W0301 after the join). This is recorded as an imprecision in ADR 0006, as the verifier's alternative suggested.

not_resolved.issue: Clause that spawns its function parameter into an outer scope and then resumes, with no later access in the body
not_resolved.reason: This is a new imprecision, not a missed race. resume mutates the changes of the handled body (ContInfo.muts), and these include what the op closure changes at the perform node. So the task that the clause starts before resume conflicts with the resume (W0405). Keeping the op-argument effects apart from the body's own changes needs a separate record of each change in the body summary. It is recorded in the ADR 0006 imprecisions, and the corpus 137 case clause_after_resume (a real race) marks it.

not_resolved.issue: Function values in a struct that a callee returns, called later by an unknown value outside a task (for example `let g = j.f; g()` after the struct's referent changes)
not_resolved.reason: This gap existed before R2d and is not in the findings. The fix covers the reported task shape through the caps::MADE mark. An attempt to put such values into Lower::escaped gave false W0301 errors in corpus 113_returned_closures, so it was reverted.

R2d: tasks, scopes, fork and the schedul.summary:
Commit ee68916 on review/s5 (on top of d593692) fixes every blocker and major from the verifiers and most of the minors. I reproduced each finding before I changed it, using the stock binary and an oracle built at HEAD (the patch hunk that did not apply was applied by hand).

All gates pass: cargo fmt, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings, cargo test --workspace (41 suites, all pass), and rustdoc -D warnings. verify-all.sh is not needed: nothing in weft-verified or proofs changed. No spec relation changed: the new facts work is in sema, plus the facts constant ARG_TASK and new diagnostic text.

I scanned 27,862 programs (oracle runs, seeds, probes, redteam, fidelity, interp) and compared the HEAD checker with the new one. Only one generated program changed: f7_spawn_param_parent gets a new W0405, which is a true positive (it already had W0312). In the corpus the changes are the new and extended files 130, 131, 132, 134 and 137, plus one new W0405 in 48_lend_alias give_closure. That W0405 follows the documented worst case for unknown function values, and the line already had W0312 and W0301.

The bad cases of 137 race in the oracle, and its clean cases run cleanly. I ran the accepted programs with the interpreter: the 18 runtime errors found are the same as at the base, so there is no interpreter regression.

Decisions recorded in ADR 0003, 0006 and 0010:
- kept excludes variables that the task code borrows.
- A captured value that holds a scope points into its root.
- Task code that calls an unknown value runs the function parameters in scope.
- Clause parameters are the join of the operation values.
- A clause of a caller's handler runs function arguments in the worst way.
- TaskRun has writes and reads.
- caps::MADE marks callee-made function values.
- A task end leaves out what a nested task still writes.
- Child failures stay in scope records, and an abort drops them.
- Each task has a simulated worker.
- A block times out at the resume.
- An HTTP function item handler is stealable unless its function can start a pinned task.
- Stealable marks are keyed by unit.

The scratch builds under scratchpad/s5 (inst, the binary copies, tmp, t, rp) are deleted.

findings.evidence: Before the fix, the repro printed results with arguments bound by position, not by name. Now `weft run RR10_named_args.wf` prints -7, -7, -7 and 'e.hp = 2, n = 5'. Sema binds arguments in crates/weft-sema/src/body/args.rs (order_args) and exports FnFacts::arg_order. The interpreter's ordered_args in crates/weft-interp/src/compile.rs uses the same order. Regression tests: tests/programs/140_named_args.wf (bad and clean cases) and crates/weft-interp/tests/programs/named_args.wf/.out. Commit bb077de.
findings.notes: This covers functions, methods, operations, function items held in locals, struct constructors and trailing blocks.

A nameless callee now gives W0104 '`f` has no parameter names: give the argument `b` by position'. A valid named constructor field binds by name (line 13 prints 8). Changed markers are in 65_call_forms.wf, 77_body_checks.wf and 135_sim_args.wf. New test: 140_named_args.wf. Commit bb077de.

The parser uses EffectPath, and sema uses effects::resolve/resolve_path with pub rules. The repro and a multi-unit package now check with 0 errors and run (each prints 1). tests/programs/141_effect_paths.wf has 5 W0101 cases, 2 W0702 cases and clean cases. Interp test: effect_paths.wf/.out. CLI units tests cover private effects and the written names in the W0702/W0805 hints. Commit bb077de.

`weft check RR15_op_shadowed.wf` now reports W0107: operation `sleep` of `Nap` has the name of the prelude function `sleep`, so a call `sleep(...)` does not reach it. Program::find_op searches modules from the inside out. In tests/programs/142_op_names.wf, 7 W0107 cases cover a prelude function, print, fork, an item, a variant, a second op with the same name and a parent-module item. The clean cases include `Nap.sleep(...)` called by its path. Commit bb077de.

findings.evidence: `weft run RR14_int_width.wf` now faults with 'integer underflow: -8 does not fit in `u64`' at 11:11. With line 11 removed, it faults at 7:33 (underflow). With lines 11-12 removed, it faults with 'integer overflow: 260 does not fit in `u8`'. Sema exports int_ops, and the interpreter emits Op::CheckInt(IntTy) and CompoundStore(BinOp, Option<IntTy>). Test: crates/weft-interp/tests/programs/int_width.wf/.out. Commit 78ae4e0.

RunOptions::oracle and `weft run --oracle` turn them on. For each check, a repro function runs clean on the stock machine and faults under the oracle (tests in guards.rs and semantics.rs). R2e: names, interpreter fidelity, proof.summary: All 13 R2e items are done in 4 commits on review/s5 in /home/user/wt-core (bb077de, 78ae4e0, e4c4b3e, 2920483), on top of base ee68916. Each item was reproduced first and has a regression test with a bad case and a clean case. Before each commit, fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --workspace and cargo doc -D warnings passed. verify-all passed with 169, 122, 235 and 67 verified. IP8 is partial: the hypotheses are tested, not proved, and ret_ok for the `in` form is only documented. The FD7 counts at HEAD (67 and 235) differ from the task's 66 and 233 because of the earlier R2c changes; the docs follow Verus. The scratch dirs of this stage under scratchpad/s5 are deleted, and the working tree is clean.
design_decisions: A named argument that is unknown, or given to a callee with no parameter names, is W0104. A name given twice, or a wrong number of arguments, is W0103 (ADR 0009).
The binding of arguments is computed once in sema and exported as FnFacts::arg_order, so the interpreter binds arguments the same way the checker does.

An effect path resolves the same way a type path does: the first name from the module outward, then the next names inside that module, with pub rules across modules and units (ADR 0005). Hints show the name as the user wrote it.
Program::find_op searches modules from the inside out. An operation that a bare call cannot reach is W0107.
A dependency with the name `main` is W0107, because the effects of the root have `main` in their identity.
Sema exports int_ops, and the interpreter checks integer ranges after each arithmetic and compound store.
The oracle checks are off by default. RunOptions::oracle and `weft run --oracle` turn them on. Tests and corpus runs turn them on (ADR 0010).
caps::Held is a typed enum that keeps the order of the old bit encoding, so the output did not change.

issues.finding: RR13 (missed shape, unsound): sema ignores the arguments of `t.join(...)` and `t.detach(...)`, but the interpreter runs them
issues.description: In crates/weft-sema/src/body/call.rs, method_call has an early branch `(Ty::Adt(a,_), "join" | "detach") => return self.join(&rv, ...)` that never lowers, counts or name-checks `args`. The interpreter compiles the call as an ordinary CallMethod and evaluates every argument. So a named argument to a callee that has no parameters is accepted silently, which breaks the RR13 rule that it is W0104. Extra positional arguments get no W0103. The argument's moves and effects are also invisible to the checker, so accepted programs fault at run time. The gap was already present at ee68916, but the new ADR 0009 list of nameless callees (`resume`, `print`, `fork`, `s.spawn`) leaves out join and detach.
issues.repro: Probe dir: SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2e: names, interpreter fidelity, proof claims and refactor/adv/p/. g1_join_args.wf: `let r = t.join(x: take(v))`, then `print(v.xs.len())`. `weft check` reports 0 errors; `weft run` (seeds 0 and 1) prints 5, then `runtime error: a value is used after it was moved` at 10:11. g2_join_pos.wf (positional `t.join(take(v))`) and g3_detach.wf (`t.detach(take(v))`) behave the same way. g4_join_effect.wf: `t.join(ask())` with no handler for Ask gets 0 errors (no W0805) and faults with `no handler for Ask.ask`.
issues.suggested_fix: In the join/detach branch, call no_names("`join`"/"`detach`", args). Report W0103 for any argument or trailing block. Lower the arguments (or refuse to lower the call) so their moves and effects are seen. Add a bad case to 140_named_args.wf and list join/detach in ADR 0009.

issues.finding: OR11: the oracle's stealable-portability check gives false alarms on accepted programs
issues.description: Machine::oracle_portable (crates/weft-interp/src/machine/exec.rs) maps a `Value::Ref(p)` or `Value::Loc(p, _)` to `Some(p.cell)` and walks the whole cell value, not the value at `p.path`. A stealable task that holds `&w.score` (a `&u64`, which is portable, so the checker marks the task stealable) therefore 'reaches' an `Rc` in a sibling field of `w`. The run then fails with `oracle: a stealable task reaches a nonportable value (Rc)`. This breaks the stated requirement that accepted programs give no false alarm. The corpus, examples, design snippets and about 570 accepted generated programs gave no false alarm, so the gap is in the shape, not the corpus.
issues.repro: Same probe dir. o3d_param.wf: `struct W { score: u64, rc: Rc<u64> }`, `fn show(r: &u64) / par, async { scope { s => s.spawn(|| print(r)) } }`, main calls `show(&w.score)`. `weft check` reports 0 errors; `weft run` prints 7; `weft run --oracle` fails at 4:9 (every seed, workers 1 and 4). o3_field_rc.wf (local `let r = &w.score`) and o3c_tuple.wf (`let r = &t.0` with `t = (5, Rc.new(1))`) fail the same way.
issues.suggested_fix: For Ref/Loc, push only the value at the referenced place: resolve the cell value along p.path. Do the same for Boxed/Vec only when they are inside the reached value. Add an accepted-program case with `&w.score` next to an Rc field to the oracle tests.

issues.finding: Performance regression: FnFacts::effect_names costs O(effects^2) for every body
issues.description: Lower::name_effects (crates/weft-sema/src/body/stmt.rs, called from finish for every body) loops over every user effect of the program. For each one it calls effects::identity and effects::written; written calls by_identity, which is an O(E) scan, plus path resolution. Every body therefore pays about E^2, even a body that uses no effects. This came in with bb077de.
issues.repro: Same probe dir. scale_effects5.wf (1200 modules, each with a pub effect, and 1200 trivial functions `fn gN(x: u64) -> u64 { x + 1 }`): `weft check` takes 0.14 s at ee68916 and 8.06 s at HEAD. scale_effects2.wf (1200 effects, 2401 functions): 0.22 s vs 20 s. scale_effects3.wf (200 effects, 5201 functions): 0.25 s vs 3.3 s. scale_effects4.wf (1200 effects, only main): 0.09 s vs 0.06 s, which confirms the cost is per body.
issues.suggested_fix: Compute the written names once per module, not once per body, or compute them lazily for the effect identities that a body's diagnostics name. Make by_identity a map lookup.

issues.finding: RR11 residual: an effect whose path a nearer module name shadows cannot be named, and the hint and note are wrong
issues.description: Code in module `x` that has a child module `a` cannot name the root's `a.Note`: `a` resolves to `x.a`, and there is no path anchored at the root. effects::written returns None, so W0701 and W0702 print the identity `main.a.Note`, which does not parse as a writable path (writing it gives W0101 unknown effect). diagnose::private_note then adds `main.a.Note is private in its package ... must make it pub`, which is false: the effect is pub and in the same package.
issues.repro: Same probe dir. d9_hint_inner.wf: `mod a { pub effect Note {...} pub fn f() / Note }`, `mod x { pub mod a { pub fn z() {} } pub fn kk() { b.call() } pub fn kd() / Clock { b.call() } }`, `mod b { pub fn call() / a.Note { a.f() } }`. Output: `W0701 ... must state its effects: / main.a.Note` and `W0702 ... performs main.a.Note` with the false 'private in its package' note. d9b.wf writes `/ main.a.Note` and gets W0101.
issues.suggested_fix: Choose the private note only when the effect is not visible, not whenever written() returns None. Give a hint for the shadowed case, or add a root-anchored path form (record the choice in ADR 0005).

issues.finding: RR15 residual shapes: some hidden operations still get no diagnostic
issues.description: check_op_names only looks at what a bare call in the operation's own module finds. Two shapes slip past it. (1) An operation named `assert`: the statement `assert(false)` is parsed as an assert statement, so the operation never runs. (2) An operation that an item of a child module hides for bare calls in that child: a function there that states `/ Nap` and calls `nap()` runs the child's function, and the clause never runs. Both give 0 diagnostics.
issues.repro: Same probe dir. e1_assert_op.wf: `effect Chk { fn assert(b: bool) }`, `fn checker() / Chk { assert(false) }` gets 0 errors; the run fails with 'assertion failed' and the clause never runs. e2_child_hides.wf: `effect Nap { fn nap() }`, `mod m { pub fn nap() {} pub fn user() / Nap { nap() } }` gets 0 errors and the clause never runs.
issues.suggested_fix: Treat contextual statement keywords (assert) as hiders in check_op_names. For calls in a child module, warn at the bare call when the operation it names is hidden by a nearer item.

issues.finding: FD15: the mutation scripts count any verify.sh failure as 'caught', and one documented result is incomplete
issues.description: proofs/borrowing/mutations/run.sh and proofs/effects/mutations/run.sh report 'caught' and exit 0 whenever verify.sh fails, even when Verus did not run or the patch broke compilation. They also never compare the result with the README table. The README row `base` says 'lemma_ptr_not_below fails; the base and B2 examples fail', but a real run also fails the B1 example lemma_kill_ring (cfg_examples.rs). All 9 borrowing rows and all 8 effects rows otherwise match the real Verus runs (counts and failing lemmas).
issues.repro: PATH=/usr/bin:/bin proofs/borrowing/mutations/run.sh b1 prints `b1: caught (...): no result. Fails in: no location` and `mutations: 1 caught`, with exit 0. proofs/effects/mutations/run.sh call does the same. With Verus on PATH, base gives: 165 verified, 4 errors; fails in lemma_kill_ring (cfg_examples.rs), lemma_groups (closures.rs), lemma_damage_states (examples.rs), lemma_ptr_not_below (soundness.rs).
issues.suggested_fix: Require a 'N verified, M errors' line with M > 0 before counting a mutation as caught, and treat anything else as not caught. Optionally check the expected failing functions. Add B1 to the README row for `base`.

issues.finding: RR10/RR13 imprecision: an item local that is reassigned to another item loses its parameter names
issues.description: After `let g = diff` and then `g = rdiff`, g definitely holds rdiff. Sema treats it as a value with no names and reports W0104 for `g(b: 10, a: 3)`. Under ADR 0009 ('a function item in a local' takes names), this valid program is rejected. The behaviour is sound (conservative), and it does not affect the corpus or the design examples.
issues.repro: Same probe dir. a1_reassign.wf: `let g = diff`, then `g = rdiff`, then `print(g(b: 10, a: 3))` gives W0104 twice. Shadowing (a11_shadow.wf) and tuple or match bindings are tracked correctly and run by name.
issues.suggested_fix: Optional: keep the item in local_fn_info across a plain assignment of an item, or document in ADR 0009 that names need a local bound once.

confirmed_fixed: RR10: RR10_named_args.wf prints -7, -7, -7 and 'e.hp = 2, n = 5'. Arguments run in parameter order in both sema and the interpreter for item calls, value methods, item locals, static methods, operations and constructors (b1-b8 give W0302 where expected). Reassignment, loops, closures, field and if/match joins are rejected or bound by name the same way at run time (a1-a13, f2-f4).
RR13: a named constructor field binds by name. Unknown names give W0104. Closures, parameters, joins, variants, print, fork, resume and spawn give W0104. Gap: join/detach (see issues).

RR11: RR11_module_effect.wf and RR11_pkg rewritten with paths check with 0 errors and run (print 1). The hints print `a.Note` and `util.Note`. Private dependency effects give W0101 plus a clear note. Nested paths, function-type rows, path performs (`a.Note.note`) and handlers in a sibling module all work. Residual: shadowed paths (minor).
QA5: a dependency named `main` gets W0107. The control still gives W0701 with `/ dep.Note`. Only direct dependencies are loaded, so there is no transitive escape.
RR15: RR15_op_shadowed.wf gets W0107 at 7:17. The 142 corpus cases work, a variant-named operation gets W0107, and Nap.sleep(...) by path works. Residual: assert and child-module shapes (minor).

RR14: the repro faults at 11:11 (u64 underflow). Faults also come for sub(2,10), u8 260, compound stores on locals and fields, unary minus, i8 -(-128), i8 / -1, i32 multiplication, usize len-1, closures, tuple and Vec elements, returns and interpolation. No regression in about 590 accepted programs compared with base.

OR11: each OR11 function is clean on the stock interpreter and faults under --oracle (seeds 0-3). There were 0 stock/oracle differences on the corpus, interpreter programs, examples, design snippets and about 570 accepted generated programs (seeds 0-3 for the file sweep and 0-1 for the generated sweep, workers 1 and 4). Exception: the Rc false alarm (see issues).

FD5/IP8: the three sentences are corrected. hypotheses.rs runs both lints on more than 500 corpus bodies and passes. `weft lint` with the two rule files fires only in stored_in_loop (37_fn_values.wf, which has an expected error). ret_ok.wf is still accepted, as documented (IP8 partial by decision).

FD7: Verus at HEAD gives weft-verified 67 (places 27, dataflow 16, modes 9, lifecycle 15) and link 235 (27/16/15, 2/24/7, 5/34/25, 0, 29, 20, 8, 23), which match the READMEs.
FD15: the effects mutations catch 8/8 and the borrowing mutations 9/9. Counts and failing lemmas match the READMEs, except the incomplete base row (minor).
FD12: docs/traceability.md exists and matches the changes.

QA9: outputs of weft check, check --json, check --explain, facts and agree are byte-identical between e4c4b3e and 2920483 on 3350 files (corpus, interpreter programs, examples, design snippets, packages, about 3000 probe and generated programs). call_fn_as is 35 lines. diagnose_marked is split into per-rule functions. Held keeps the order of the old encoding.
R2e: names, interpreter fidelity, proof.summary:
Adversarial verification of R2e on review/s5 (2920483, base ee68916). The worktree is unchanged; probes and sweep outputs are in SCRATCH/verify/s5/R2e: names, interpreter fidelity, proof claims and refactor/adv/ (also in SCRATCH/verify/s5/adv_r2e/).

Gates: another verifier ran fmt, clippy, test and doc at HEAD (SCRATCH/verify/s5/*.log, exit 0 for all). Its verify-all log shows 169/122/235/67 with rc=0. I re-ran weft-check hypotheses/programs and weft-interp programs/guards (all pass). I confirmed every per-module Verus count myself and re-ran both mutation suites.

All 13 items are substantively done. QA9 is byte-identical on 3350 files.

Findings:
1. Blocker: sema ignores the arguments of `t.join(...)` and `t.detach(...)`; the interpreter evaluates them. A named argument there is silently accepted (a missed RR13 shape), and accepted programs fault at run time (use after move, no handler). This was already present at base.
2. Major: the oracle's portability walk follows a reference to its whole cell, so accepted programs that hand a stealable task `&w.score` next to an Rc field fail under --oracle.
3. Minor: performance. FnFacts::effect_names costs O(E^2) for every body: 1200 effects plus 1200 trivial functions go from 0.14 s to 8.1 s.
4. Minor: an effect whose path a nearer module shadows cannot be named, and its hint and 'private' note are wrong.
5. Minor: an operation named `assert`, and operations hidden in child modules, still get no diagnostic.
6. Minor: the mutation scripts count any verify.sh failure as caught (even with Verus missing), and the README row `base` leaves out the B1 example that also fails.
7. Minor: an item local that is reassigned loses its parameter names (conservative W0104).

The implementer's FD6 evidence text (about a 'named arguments' sentence) does not describe the change, but the change itself is correct. I deleted my large scratch copies.

issues.finding: RR15 fix: W0107 for operation names rejects valid programs that perform by effect path, and its hint gives a remedy that does not clear the error
issues.description: check_op_names (crates/weft-sema/src/program.rs) reports W0107 at the declaration of any operation that a bare call in its module cannot reach. This goes further than the decision, which covered an operation hidden by a prelude function. It also covers a second effect in the same module with the same operation name, and an operation named like a same-module function, variant or type. The error is at the declaration, so the program cannot run even when every perform uses the path. The note says 'rename the operation, or perform it with the effect name: `State.get(...)`', but writing the path does not remove the error. This is also true for the prelude case (corpus 142 has the W0107 marker on `Nap` while its main already performs `Nap.sleep(1.ms)`). Programs that base ee68916 accepted and ran correctly are now rejected. Examples: two effects that both have `get` (Reader/State), and the R2 quality generators r2/quality/gen/ring_N.wf and g_handlers_nested_N.wf, which perform `E1.op(1)` by path (ring_400 now gets 399 W0107). ADR 0005 records the extension, but it is not a soundness rule and it adds false positives. It also contradicts the ADR text 'The effect path still reaches it'.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/p/op2.wf: `effect Reader { fn get() -> u64 }` `effect State { fn get() -> u64 }` `fn both() -> u64 / Reader, State { Reader.get() + State.get() }` plus a main that handles both. At base: 0 errors, prints 11. At HEAD: error[W0107] operation `get` of `State` ... note 'perform it with the effect name: `State.get(...)`', although the code already does that. The same holds for p/op3.wf (`effect Nap { fn sleep(d: Duration) }` performed only as `Nap.sleep(1.ms)`): base runs and prints 'user nap', HEAD gives W0107.
issues.suggested_fix: Do not reject the declaration when the operation is still reachable by path. Report the problem at a bare call site that resolves to a function, a variant or the first operation while another visible operation has the same name (ambiguity: write the path). Or keep the declaration W0107 only for the prelude and builtin case that the decision named, and drop the second-operation, item and variant extension. In either case, make the note match what clears the error. Add a clean case to 142 in which an operation is performed only by its path.

issues.finding: Performance regression: effect_names is computed per body in O(effects^2), so check time grows as bodies x effects^2
issues.description: Lower::name_effects (crates/weft-sema/src/body/stmt.rs) loops over every user effect in every body. For each effect it calls effects::identity and effects::written, and written calls by_identity, which is a linear scan over all effects. The cost is O(B*E^2). FnFacts::effect_name is also a linear search. Base did not have this cost.
issues.repro: SCRATCH/verify/s5/p/many_eff800.wf: 800 effects with distinct operation names and 800 functions `fn fI() / EI { opI(1) }`. `weft check` (debug build) takes 0.32 s at base ee68916, 22.1 s at e4c4b3e and 25.5 s at HEAD. With 400 effects it is 0.14 s at base and 3.35 s at R2e. r2/quality/gen/ring_400.wf goes from 12.0 s to 16.7 s.
issues.suggested_fix: Compute the written names once for each module, not for each body. Or compute them lazily in diagnose, only for the identities that appear in a violation. Use an identity-to-EffectId map in place of by_identity's linear scan.

issues.finding: OR11: the stealable-portability oracle check and the end-of-run linear-leak check have no test
issues.description: The report says that for each oracle check 'a repro function runs clean on the stock machine and faults under the oracle (tests in guards.rs and semantics.rs)'. guards.rs has 5 cases: a freed cell, a dead local, a push moving the buffer, a dropped linear value and a race. No test reaches Machine::oracle_portable ('a stealable task reaches a nonportable value') or the 'still live at the end of the run' branch of oracle_end. guards.rs runs through run_analysis_main, which passes an empty stealable set, so oracle_portable cannot fire there. The semantics.rs diff only changes the underflow message. I could not trigger oracle_portable from the CLI either: the checker pins each task that reaches an Rc.
issues.repro: grep -rn 'nonportable value\|still live at the end' crates/weft-interp/tests crates/weft-cli/tests returns no test. The probes p/st1.wf and p/st2.wf (Vec<Rc> captured by a spawned task) run clean under --oracle --workers 4.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a guards test that builds Runtime::new with the spawn span in the stealable set, for a task that captures an Rc, and expects the oracle fault. Add a test for a linear value that is still live at the end of the run, for example one in a detached task or an Rc cycle.

R2e: names, interpreter fidelity, proof.summary: I ran every gate at HEAD 2920483 in /home/user/wt-core, and all pass: fmt --check, clippy -D warnings (workspace pedantic and nursery), cargo test --workspace, cargo doc -D warnings, and verify-all (169, 122, 235 and 67 verified). The production diff adds no unwrap, expect, unsafe or lint allow, and the worktree is unchanged. Most items hold up under adversarial probes: the named-argument binding (sema exports arg_order, the interpreter follows it), the effect paths with pub rules and hints the user can write, the dependency named main, integer width checks, the oracle (no false alarm in a sweep of the corpus and interpreter programs over several seeds and worker counts, or in 330 single-function wrappers), the proof doc corrections with Verus per-module counts, the mutation scripts (9/9 and 8/8, matching their tables), the traceability matrix and the QA9 refactor (outputs the same on 7130 files). One major issue: the RR15 fix goes past the decision. A second operation with the same name in a module, or an operation named like a same-module item, now gets a W0107 error at its declaration. Correct programs that perform by path are rejected (Reader.get and State.get; the generated ring_N and g_handlers_nested_N probes). Base accepted and ran these. The hint 'perform it with the effect name' never clears the error. Minor issues: an O(bodies x effects^2) slowdown from per-body effect_names (800 effects: 0.3 s at base, 22-25 s at R2e); no test for the stealable-portability oracle check or the end-of-run leak branch; no vacuity guard in hypotheses.rs; the W0101 explain text does not mention private effects; small inconsistencies in the proof docs. not_resolved.issue: RR15 residual e2: an item of a child module hides an operation of an outer module for a bare call (m.nap hides Nap.nap)
not_resolved.reason: Rejected by design. This is the normal scope rule: the program wrote both names, and the effect path reaches the operation. A diagnostic here, at the declaration or at the call, rejects valid programs. That is the class of false positive behind the major W0107 finding. ADR 0005 now states the rule.

not_resolved.issue: RR11 residual: no path form that starts at the root, to name an effect whose first path name a nearer module hides
not_resolved.reason: That is a language change and out of scope for a review fix. The misleading private note is fixed. The new note says that a nearer item hides the path and tells the user what to do. ADR 0005 records the choice.

not_resolved.issue: RR10/RR13 imprecision a1_reassign: `let g = diff` then `g = rdiff` loses the parameter names (W0104)
not_resolved.reason: Not changed in code. A local has one type, which is flow-insensitive, so the type of g is a join of two items. Rejecting the call is the sound choice. ADR 0009 now documents it and gives the workaround (write the arguments by position, or bind a new local).
